author: fbarrento
body:
Slice B of the remaining #2 work. Wires Saloon's `AlwaysThrowOnErrors` plugin to a status→typed-exception mapping on the connector, ships the full 10-class hierarchy from the design memo, and splits `ForgeTest.php` into per-method/per-concern files before it balloons further with the 20+ resource methods on the way.

## Summary

### Exception hierarchy (`src/Exceptions/`)

```
ForgeException                            (abstract; extends RuntimeException)
├── ApiException                           (concrete; holds Response + status())
│   ├── BadRequestException (400)
│   ├── UnauthorizedException (401)
│   ├── ForbiddenException (403)
│   ├── NotFoundException (404)
│   ├── ValidationException (422)          errors() / errorsFor() / firstError()
│   ├── RateLimitException (429)           retryAfter() — parses Retry-After header
│   └── ServerException (5xx)
└── ConnectionException                    wraps Saloon's FatalRequestException
```

- Status mapping in `ForgeConnector::getRequestException()` via `match`. Unknown 4xx/5xx codes fall back to `ApiException`.
- `Forge::send()` private helper catches Saloon's `FatalRequestException` (transport-level) and re-throws as `ConnectionException`.
- `AlwaysThrowOnErrors` plugin enabled on the connector.

### Test file split (1 → 5 files)

| File | Tests | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/Feature/ForgeTest.php` | 5 | `me()` facade integration only |
| `tests/Feature/Forge/FromEnvironmentTest.php` | 5 | `Forge::fromEnvironment()` |
| `tests/Feature/Forge/FromConfigTest.php` | 9 | `Forge::fromConfig()` |
| `tests/Unit/Http/ForgeConnectorTest.php` | 16 | Status→exception mapping + ConnectionException + inspections |
| `tests/Unit/Data/UserTest.php` | 8 | Unchanged |

This deviates from the project's `pest-package-tests` skill rule of "one test file per source class" — captured as a `feedback_test_file_split.md` memory for future sessions. Cross-cutting logic moves to *the class that owns it* (connector mapping → connector test file), even when exercised via the facade.

## Conventions

- All "throws X" tests use Pest's **test-level `->throws()`** chain.
- All exception **inspection** tests use closure-form `expect()->toThrow(fn (TypedException $e) => ...)`.
- One test per behavior — no Pest `->with(...)` datasets.
- All HTTP-touching tests run through `ForgeFixture`. Error fixtures are hand-crafted (the API obviously won't return a 500 on demand for a real recording).
- FQCN imports throughout.

## Quality gates

- **43 tests / 84 assertions**
- 100% line coverage (`pest --coverage --exactly=100`)
- 100% type coverage (`pest --type-coverage --min=100`)
- Pint, Rector (dry-run), PHPStan max — all clean

## Out of scope (remaining on #2)

- `scripts/fetch-spec.sh` placeholder
- Final README polish around the new error-handling story (the README still doesn't cover exceptions)
- `nunomaduro/pao` is in `composer.json require-dev` for future use; not exercised by this PR

## Convention to propagate upstream

The two-style Pest exception convention (test-level `->throws()` for plain assertions, closure-form `toThrow()` for inspection) and the per-method facade-test split convention should land in the upstream `pest-package-tests` skill (`fbarrento/laravel-agent-kit`). Both are captured as project memories for now.

## Summary

- Rebuild the What-If `DeltaChip` in `scheme-card-grid.tsx` from a cramped uppercase-tracked `rounded-full` pill into proper status pills:
  - Per-status lucide icons: `Sparkles` (gained), `XCircle` (lost), `TrendingUp`/`TrendingDown` (amount_changed by sign), `ArrowRight` (tier_changed).
  - `amount_changed` now tones forest for positive deltas and destructive for negative — previously always primary regardless of direction.
  - `tier_changed` renders as a two-line `rounded-lg` pill: eyebrow label on top, before/after diff below with strikethrough on `before`, unicode `→`, and bold on `after`. The backend's ASCII `->` is swapped to `→` at render time.
  - Other statuses render as a single-line `rounded-full` pill: icon · eyebrow · value, with sentence-case eyebrow text instead of cramped uppercase tracking.
- Add `evaluation.whatIf.deltaChip.eyebrow.{gained,lost,tier_changed,amount_changed}` strings to en / ms / zh.
- Apply button color treatment is unchanged — only the top-match card keeps the hibiscus fill.

## Why

The previous delta chips read poorly when a tier change surfaced (e.g. `RM300/YEAR UNDER BAP — 2 CHILDREN × -> RM600/YEAR UNDER BAP — 4 CHILDREN ×`): backend-supplied prose was forced into uppercase letter-spaced pill copy, the `->` arrow was ASCII, and there was no visual differentiation between gained/lost/amount-up/amount-down. author: gurdasnijor
body:
## Summary

Fixes a Firegrid CLI parity bug surfaced during the Codex ACP de-risk lane.

`pnpm firegrid -- run -- <agent>` failed in a fresh local shell with:

```
firegrid failed: Error: (Missing data at DURABLE_STREAMS_BASE_URL: "Expected DURABLE_STREAMS_BASE_URL to exist in the process context") and (Missing data at FIREGRID_RUNTIME_NAMESPACE: "Expected FIREGRID_RUNTIME_NAMESPACE to exist in the process context")
```

`run` resolved its Durable Streams + namespace topology through `RuntimeHostTopologyFromConfig`, which is an Effect Config that requires both env vars and fails hard when they are absent. `start` already used the embedded `DurableStreamTestServer` fallback + `firegrid-local` default namespace. This PR brings `run` to parity with `start`.

## Change

- `runCommand` now acquires `durableStreamsEndpoint` (the same Effect `start` uses) and resolves the namespace from env or the `firegrid-local` default before building the host layer.
- New `runHostLayer(config, durableStreams, namespace)` replaces `envHostLayer(config)`. It reads `FIREGRID_RUNTIME_INPUT_ENABLED` and `FIREGRID_DURABLE_STREAMS_TOKEN` directly instead of going through `RuntimeHostTopologyFromConfig`.
- `RuntimeHostTopologyFromConfig` is no longer imported by the CLI.
- `run` is still synchronous and still returns the child exit code.

## Semantics

When the env vars **are** set (e.g. tracer-019 local smoke, Electric Cloud smoke): the configured base URL + namespace are used unchanged. `durableStreamsEndpoint` short-circuits the embedded-server fallback.

When the env vars are **not** set: the embedded `DurableStreamTestServer` is acquired in the same scope as the runtime execution, namespace defaults to `firegrid-local`, and the child runs to completion.

## Tests

Existing `tracer-019` local smoke (sets both env vars) passes unchanged.

New focused regression test in the same file:

> `firegrid-workflow-driven-runtime.PHASE_2_SYNC_RUN.9 pnpm firegrid -- run -- <node -e ...> succeeds with no DURABLE_STREAMS_BASE_URL or FIREGRID_RUNTIME_NAMESPACE in env`

Spawns `pnpm firegrid -- run -- node -e 'console.log("child-ran"); process.exit(0)'` with `DURABLE_STREAMS_BASE_URL`, `FIREGRID_RUNTIME_NAMESPACE`, and `FIREGRID_DURABLE_STREAMS_TOKEN` explicitly removed from the child env. Asserts exit 0, the launched-context log line, "child-ran" on stdout, and the absence of the prior "Missing data at ..." errors.

## Out of scope

- ACP / `mcpServers` injection into the run path. The original Codex de-risk lane surfaced this as a separate gap (the codec path still hardcodes `mcpServers: []`); that is its own follow-up.
- The MCP-server GET-handler transport-compat fix lives on a separate branch (`coding/mcp-server-get-handler`).

## Changed files

```
features/firegrid/firegrid-workflow-driven-runtime.feature.yaml    +1
scenarios/firegrid/src/tracer-019-sync-run.test.ts                +46
src/run.ts                                                        +37/-16
```

## Local validation (targeted)

- `pnpm typecheck` → clean (root workspace, all packages)

author: zdebrine
body:
For Stripe Checkout Sessions in mode=setup, `session.payment_method` is
documented to be NULL — the real payment method is attached to the
resulting SetupIntent, not the session. The webhook handler at
app/api/stripe/webhook/route.ts:99-110 already accounts for this with a
follow-up `getSetupIntent` call. The page-render sync function did NOT,
and was writing `stripe_payment_method_id: session.payment_method || null`
on every redirect-back from Stripe.

Effect on the bag-aware flow:

- Every commit that came back via the page-render path (the operative
  path when the webhook isn't reaching the server) ended up at
  `setup_complete` with `stripe_payment_method_id = NULL`.
- At settlement, the charge worker's missing-PM gate fired:
  `lib/charge-worker.ts:274 → markPaymentFailed('missing_payment_method')`.
- Database evidence: 0 of 37 commitments in this DB have ever had a PM
  saved; 20 succeeded via legacy payment-mode (immediate charge), 1
  bag-aware commit got `stripe_setup_intent_id` written but no PM.

PR #86 fixed the same `|| null` clobber in the webhook's
`setup_intent.succeeded` handler. This file was a parallel write path
that PR #86 didn't touch.

Fix:

- Add a follow-up `getSetupIntent` call when the session doesn't have a
  PM, mirroring the webhook handler's pattern.
- Build the UPDATE payload conditionally — only include fields we have
  non-null values for. The old code wrote `stripe_payment_method_id: null`
  and `stripe_customer_id: null` unconditionally, which could overwrite
  a real PM written by a concurrent webhook delivery in the rare ordering
  where the webhook lands first.

Race / ordering notes:

- The page-render sync SELECT filters on `payment_status='pending_setup'`,
  so a successful webhook write to `setup_complete` first means the sync
  skips the row entirely. No race in that ordering.
- If the page-render sync runs first (typical: Stripe redirect lands on
  our server faster than the webhook delivery), we now write the real
  PM via the SI fetch. A subsequent webhook delivery's defensive write
  (PR #86) won't clobber because both code paths only write PM when
  truthy.
- If the SI fetch fails (network glitch), we skip the PM write — the row
  stays at `setup_complete` without a PM, and the webhook is the only
  thing that can rescue it. The orphan-cancel branch in settle-deadlines
  picks up the row at deadline if no PM ever lands.

Separate concern: the webhook isn't successfully running in this
environment (Stripe webhook delivery logs / signature config). This fix
makes the page-render sync a reliable fallback so commits don't strand
at settlement even when the webhook path is broken.

author: saturninoabril
body:
#### Summary

- `ci/extract-reason` failed with `xargs: unmatched single quote` when an override comment contained an apostrophe or quote (real-world case: `/test-analysis-override we don't need tests for this right now.`).
- Added `-d '\n'` to the `xargs` call so GNU xargs treats the input literally instead of parsing shell-style quoting.
- `head -1` already restricts input to a single line, so delimiter mode is the right semantic match.

__Tradeoff__

`xargs -d '\n'` does not trim or normalize whitespace, so `REASON` may now carry trailing spaces. This is acceptable:

- The emptiness guard (`[ -z "$REASON" ]`) still works because the upstream `sed "s|^${SLASH_COMMAND}\s*||"` strips the command plus following whitespace — a comment of just `/test-analysis-override   ` still produces an empty `REASON` and is rejected.
- Downstream consumers (`jq --arg` in the webhook, `gh api -f body=...`) handle their own escaping.

__Other xargs special characters__

In `-d` mode, GNU xargs explicitly disables all shell-style parsing: quotes, backslashes, and the EOF marker (`_`) are all literal. The only theoretical risk is an embedded NUL byte, which GitHub doesn't allow in comment bodies.

author: tytaniumdev
body:
## Why

The parity audit between Flutter and Docker workers turned up one real cutover blocker. Docker workers POST sim results → API increments \`completedSimCount\` → API fires \`aggregateJobResults\` when \`completedSimCount >= totalSimCount\`. Flutter writes Firestore directly → counter increments → no trigger fires.

The 15-minute stale-sweeper picks these up eventually, but the UX is "all sims show COMPLETED but the job sits in RUNNING for 15 min." Bad.

## What

- **New endpoint** \`POST /api/jobs/:id/aggregate-if-done\` — authed with WORKER_SECRET, calls the existing idempotent \`aggregateJobResults\`. ~30 lines.
- **New Flutter \`JobAggregator\`** — fire-and-forget POST to the new endpoint after each terminal report. Same shape as the existing \`LogUploader\`. ~50 lines.
- **WorkerEngine** fires \`triggerIfDone\` at all four reportTerminal sites (happy path, job-not-found, missing-decks, catch-all). Idempotent so racing calls are harmless.

## Test plan

- [x] API lints clean (\`tsc --noEmit && eslint\`).
- [x] Flutter analyze clean.
- [x] 30/30 worker tests pass.
- [ ] After merge: tag a release, run one cloud-mode sim end-to-end, confirm the job flips RUNNING → COMPLETED within seconds rather than 15 min.

This PR updates [requests](https://pypi.org/project/requests) from **2.26.0** to **2.34.2**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 2.34.2
   ```
   -------------------
- Moved `headers` input type back to `Mapping` to avoid invariance issues
  with `MutableMapping` and inferred dict types. Users calling
  `Request.headers.update()` may need to narrow typing in their code. (7441)

  and `Sequence`. (7436)

  `Request.headers` typing to improve handling for users. (7431)
- `Response.reason` moved from `str | None` to `str` to improve handling
  for users. (7437)
- Fixed a bug where some bodies with custom `__getattr__` implementations
  weren't being properly detected as Iterables. (7433)
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 2.34.0
   ```
   -------------------

**Announcements**
- Requests 2.34.0 introduces inline types, replacing those provided by
  typeshed. Public API types should be fully compatible with mypy, pyright,
  and ty. We believe types are comprehensive but if you find issues, please
  report them to the pinned tracking issue.

  Special thanks to bastimeyer, cthoyt, edgarrmondragon, and srittau for
  helping review and test the types ahead of the release. (7272)

**Improvements**
- Digest Auth hashing algorithms have added `usedforsecurity=False` to clarify
  security considerations. (7310)
- Requests added support for Python 3.15 based on beta1. Downstream projects
  should be able to start testing prior to its release in October. (7422)
- Requests added support for Python 3.14t. (7419)

**Bugfixes**
- ``Response.history`` no longer contains a reference to itself, preventing
  accidental looping when traversing the history list. (7328)
- Requests no longer performs greedy matching on no_proxy domains. The
  proxy_bypass implementation has been updated with CPython's fix from
  bpo-39057. (7427)
- Requests no longer incorrectly strips duplicate leading slashes in
  URI paths. This should address user issues with specific presigned
  URLs. Note the full fix requires urllib3 2.7.0+. (7315)

uses Requests, please take a look at 7271. Give it a try, and report
any gaps or feedback you may have in the issue. 📣

**Security**

  contents to a non-deterministic location to prevent malicious file
  replacement. This does not affect default usage of Requests, only

author: reshigan
body:
## Summary
Addresses the "transparency of measure on each card to show the source" feedback. Every KPI on every card is a claim; SAP-grade transparency requires every claim to trace back to the table it came from, the SQL/query it ran, the time window it covered, and how many records contributed. This PR ships the primitive + wires the first two surfaces.

## New primitive — `<MetricSource>`
- Small ⓘ trigger that opens an anchored 320px popover
- Structured rows: **Definition**, **Table**, **Endpoint**, **Query** (monospace code block), **Window**, **Sample**, **Confidence**, **Refreshed**
- Optional `drillTo` link footer → "Drill into source →"
- Optional `notes` array for free-form rows (e.g. "Threshold: score ≥ 80")
- Outside-click + ESC closes
- `MetricProvenance` type exported for reuse

## Wired surfaces

### Operator Queue
- All 5 status tiles (Pending / Previewed / Completed / Failed / Rejected) carry a `MetricSource` with:
  - SQL hint from `catalyst_actions` filtered by status
  - Endpoint `GET /api/erp/actions/summary`
  - Window "All time", sample = the count itself, refreshedAt
  - `drillTo` → `/action-layer?status=…`
- New `TILE_DEFINITIONS` map gives each status a plain-English definition (e.g. "previewed = payload composed and validated but not yet committed to the ERP")
- Tile changed from `<button>` to `<div role="button">` so the MetricSource trigger can nest legally

### Dashboard
- 4 dimension cards (Dimensions / Healthy / At Risk / Critical) wired with:
  - Endpoint `GET /api/apex/health`
  - Query hint with explicit threshold (`score >= 80` / `60..80` / `< 60`)
  - Window "Latest snapshot", refreshedAt from existing `lastRefreshed`
  - Thresholds rendered as notes — operators no longer have to guess where the bands cut

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc -b` clean
- [x] `npx vitest run` 48/48 pass
- [ ] Smoke test: click ⓘ on a Pending tile, verify popover, click outside to close
- [ ] Smoke test: click "Drill into source →" from a popover
- [ ] Smoke test: verify Healthy threshold "score ≥ 80" displays in popover

author: xerosumgames
body:
## Summary

Performance-only pass on `components/TacticalMap.tsx`. Rendering output is pixel-identical — no visual changes.

**Finding 1 (29-dep draw useEffect):** SKIPPED. After reading every dep, all of them genuinely drive draw output. `dragging` positions tokens at the cursor (line 1480), `fogEditMode` changes fog opacity and gates the vision computation (lines 1250/1406/1418), `fogRectStart/End` and `wallRectStart/End` draw rectangle marquee previews (lines 2210–2242), `wallDrawStart/Hover` draws the live wall-segment preview (line 2166). The audit premise that these are "non-visual" is wrong for this component.

**Finding 2 (O(n²) cell loops) — SHIPPED `c5041e5`:**  
Move-zone, throw-zone range, and blast-preview band loops each iterated the full grid (`grid_cols × grid_rows`) on every `draw()` call. Each now caches a `Array<{gx,gy}>` of valid cells in a ref, keyed by the inputs that affect which cells qualify (mover/thrower position, range, hover cell, band radii, grid size, occupied set). On a cache hit the iteration is skipped and only the draw calls run. Blast preview also batches its two fill colors, eliminating per-cell `fillStyle` changes.

**Finding 3 (fog visibility LoS sweep) — SHIPPED `ab7e0c9`:**  
The PC vision sweep — Chebyshev-radius walk × LoS checks (segment intersection + Bresenham) per candidate cell — ran every `draw()` call. On a 20×20 scene with 4 PCs in day mode that's ~6700 LoS checks/frame, each scanning up to ~20 wall segments. Cache key encodes: `isDay`, `dayRadius`, all PC grid positions + sight radii, all vision-blocking segment coordinates, and cell-based blocker positions. The key changes only when a PC moves, a door opens/closes, a wall is added, or lighting mode flips. All other `draw()` triggers (animation rAF loop, ping, zoom, fog paint) are cache hits.

- Throw mode: grenade throw should paint orange cells, hover should show Engaged/Close blast rings
- Fog: confirm fogged cells are black for players; GM sees partial opacity. Open a door — fog should clear along the LoS path through the opening
- Day/Night toggle: switching to Night should shrink each PC's visible radius
- Drag a token: confirm the drag ghost follows the cursor and snaps correctly on mouseup

author: railway-app[bot]
body:
## Problem

PR #1675 removed all degraded mode bypasses and made Redis unavailability a hard fatal crash. The Redis public proxy endpoint (viaduct.proxy.rlwy.net:20874) is rejecting TLS connections with SSL record layer failures, so the bot cannot start at all — the strict enforcement blocks every startup attempt before any trading can occur.

## Solution

Restored three degraded mode bypasses as a temporary measure while the Redis TLS issue is debugged. In `distributed_nonce_manager.py`, the `DistributedNonceManager` constructor and `get_nonce` now fall back to file-based per-key fcntl locks instead of raising when Redis is None or fails, and the `get_distributed_nonce_manager` factory no longer raises on missing URL or connection failure. In `execution_authority_context.py`, `_allow_degraded_writer_authority` now returns True when both `NIJA_ALLOW_DEGRADED_WRITER_AUTHORITY=1` and `NIJA_RUNTIME_DEGRADED_MODE=1` are set, and `assert_distributed_writer_authority` short-circuits before the fencing token check in that case. In `trading_state_machine.py`, `_distributed_writer_authority_gate` bypasses the Redis fencing check when `NIJA_RUNTIME_DEGRADED_MODE=1` is set. All bypass paths emit CRITICAL log warnings. To activate degraded mode, set `NIJA_RUNTIME_DEGRADED_MODE=1` and `NIJA_ALLOW_DEGRADED_WRITER_AUTHORITY=1`; once Redis TLS is fixed, unset both variables to restore the strict PR #1675 enforcement.

### Changes
- **Modified** `bot/execution_authority_context.py`
- **Modified** `bot/trading_state_machine.py`
- **Modified** `bot/distributed_nonce_manager.py`

author: tommaso-r-marena
body:
💡 What: Vectorized the Frame Aligned Point Error (FAPE) loss in `src/training/losses.py` by replacing a sequential loop over residue frames with parallelized tensor operations (`torch.einsum` and broadcasting).

🎯 Why: The original implementation suffered from high Python overhead due to iterating over up to 32 frames per sample in a batch. Vectorization allows PyTorch to execute these operations in parallel, significantly improving training throughput.

📊 Impact: 
- Measured ~3.4x - 5.7x speedup on CPU-bound paths (B=8, L=128, A=4).
- Numerically identical results to the reference implementation.

🔬 Measurement: Verified using `scripts/benchmark_fape_bolt.py` (temporary script) comparing loop-based vs. vectorized logic. Correctness confirmed via `torch.allclose`.

🛠️ Other: Fixed a pre-existing syntax error (duplicate `__init__` and broken indentation) in `src/quantum_hardware/backend_manager.py` that was identified during integration testing.

body:
## Operator ask

> "turn on the heartbeat functionality"
>
> *and* "dogfood whats in the repo and you orchestrate. you are the opus 4.7 1M context agent that orchestrates and owns this repo"
>
> *and* "find it in the repo"

## What this PR ships

The heartbeat skill (`.claude/skills/heartbeat.md`) was fully documented in Phase 15 but never had its persistence layer. Each "tick" re-derived state from PRs + issues, with no way to resume across sessions.

This PR creates `seeds/memory/heartbeat/` — the operator-side translation of Managed-Agents `/mnt/memory/<store>/` — and seeds the four files the skill expects:

| File | Lifecycle | Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `README.md` | static | Invariants, file semantics, read-order |
| `last-tick.md` | overwritten each tick | What this tick decided + git SHA + ISO + resume instructions |
| `next-actions.md` | append + pop | Ordered queue. Top action = next |
| `decisions.md` | append-only | Audit log of decisions with reasoning |
| `open-questions.md` | append + delete-when-answered | Things blocking specific actions |

## Tick 1 — bootstrap

**Trigger:** operator-direct prompt.

**4 decisions recorded** (full reasoning in `decisions.md`):

- **D1** — Webhook-only trigger surface (no GHA cron). Dogfoods existing `mcp__github__subscribe_pr_activity` + `.github/workflows/claude.yml` `@claude`-mention triggers. Reversible.
- **D2** — First-tick scope is bootstrap-only; do NOT execute the top queue item in this PR. Keeps surface reviewable.
- **D3** — `docs/pending.md` is stale (last-reviewed 2026-05-10) but refreshing it requires GH issue verification; defer to a separate tick.
- **D4** — Use `docs/phase-gates.md` as authoritative status surface until `npm run setup:project` runs (operator-gated on PAT runbook).

## Trigger surface — explicitly NO cron

Per operator guidance "find it in the repo," reuses existing patterns:

```
webhook event on subscribed PR
    └─> github-webhook-activity message wakes the heartbeat tick

operator @claude mention in issue/PR
    └─> .github/workflows/claude.yml runs claude-code-action@v1
        └─> reads .claude/skills/heartbeat.md and acts

operator direct session prompt
    └─> heartbeat skill model-invokable in any session
```

No new `.github/workflows/heartbeat.yml`. Adding a cron later is a one-file follow-up if quiet periods become an issue. The repo currently has only one scheduled workflow (`osv-scanner.yml` weekly) — inventing a heartbeat cron now would expand infrastructure beyond what's documented.

## Top of the next-actions queue

`#1 — Fix scripts/lib/llms-txt.ts parser` (unblocks twilio + sentry + sift in one targeted change). Three vendors gain `urls.md` from a single ~30-line parser fix. Documented with rubric reference, gate status, and step-by-step plan in `next-actions.md`.

That work runs on the **next tick** — either when a webhook fires on this PR or when the operator next prompts.

## Verify

`npm run verify` — 14 vendors, 0 warnings, 0 errors. No code touched.

## Why automerge

Pure docs/state addition. No code paths affected. The skill that consumes these files is already in `main`.

## Summary
Modified the bill posting selection logic to enforce per-state diversity while maintaining recency as the primary sorting criterion. Instead of simply taking the top POST_LIMIT bills, the algorithm now selects at most one bill per state on the first pass, then fills remaining slots from already-posted states.

## Key Changes
- **Two-pass selection algorithm**: First pass selects one bill per state (respecting the global recency sort), second pass fills remaining POST_LIMIT slots from leftover candidates
- **Maintained recency priority**: Unlike the previous per-state round-robin approach, the new diversity rule acts as a tiebreak on top of the global sort, preventing stale states from leapfrogging fresh ones
- **Preserved stub handling**: Bills without descriptions still lose to any descriptive candidate regardless of state affiliation
- **Improved state distribution**: Prevents a single state with multiple fresh bills from monopolizing an entire posting run

## Implementation Details
- Introduced `used_states` set to track which states have already contributed a bill in the first pass
- Bills from already-used states are collected in `leftovers` during the first pass
- Second pass extends `to_post` with leftovers up to POST_LIMIT capacity
- Updated comment documentation to explain the new algorithm and rationale for the change

author: danielhanchen
body:
## Summary

`unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` loads at around 46 GB even with `load_in_4bit=True`. The cause is structural rather than a flag being dropped: `Gemma4TextExperts` stores all experts as two fused 3D `nn.Parameter` tensors (so `torch._grouped_mm` can dispatch one grouped matmul per layer), and `bnb.replace_with_bnb_linear` only swaps `nn.Linear` instances. The fused expert weights stay BF16 and dominate the VRAM footprint.

This PR adds an opt-in helper that, after the model is loaded, walks every `Gemma4TextExperts` module, slices each fused `(num_experts, out, in)` Parameter into `num_experts` individual `bitsandbytes.nn.Linear4bit` modules, and patches `forward` to dispatch per-expert.

## Measured impact

`unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` on a single B200, transformers 5.5.0, torch 2.9.1:

| mode | resident VRAM | peak (fwd) | Linear4bit count | forward fidelity |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BF16 baseline (`full_finetuning=True`) | 48.08 GB | 48.20 GB | 0 | reference |
| `load_in_4bit=True`, no swap | ~46 GB | n/a | 206 (attention only) | partial-quant |
| `load_in_4bit=True`, swap on | **14.27 GB** | 14.40 GB | **7,886** | cosine 0.994 vs BF16 |

Forward-pass logits compared on a fixed prompt; cosine similarity 0.994 is standard QLoRA fidelity. Top-5 tokens overlap; argmax differs by 1 token as expected for nf4.

## Trade-off

Per-expert dispatch loses the `torch._grouped_mm` throughput. Acceptable for "the model fits at 4-bit on a single GPU", which is what `#5344` is asking for. QLoRA training still needs the matching per-expert LoRA path; that is the gating reason this PR keeps the swap behind `UNSLOTH_GEMMA4_MOE_4BIT=1`.

The swap also renames `gate_up_proj` to `gate_up_proj_4bit` (and the same for `down_proj`) so it does not collide with `unsloth_zoo`'s `gemma4_moe.py` grouped-mm LoRA extractor which keys off the original names. That extractor would need a parallel `_4bit`-aware path before we can flip the default to ON.

## Activation

```python
import os
os.environ["UNSLOTH_GEMMA4_MOE_4BIT"] = "1"

from unsloth import FastLanguageModel
model, tokenizer = FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(
    "unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it",
    load_in_4bit = True,
)
# Unsloth: swapped 30 Gemma4TextExperts module(s) to per-expert Linear4bit
# (see https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/5344).
```

The hook is only entered when `load_in_4bit=True` and `full_finetuning=False`, and only fires if the model actually contains `Gemma4TextExperts` modules. On every other checkpoint the helper is a no-op.

## Safety

- Idempotent: re-running the swap sees `_unsloth_gemma4_moe_4bit_swapped` on the module and skips it.
- Shape-checked: bails out without modifying weights if the fused Parameters do not have the `(num_experts, 2*intermediate, hidden)` and `(num_experts, hidden, intermediate)` layout.
- Failure-soft: if any error is raised during the swap, falls back to BF16 experts and warns the user. The existing guardrail from #5430 will then fire and explain why VRAM is high.
- Per-instance forward rebind: does not touch the class-level `Gemma4TextExperts.forward`, so sibling models in the same process keep the standard path.

## Tests

`tests/test_gemma4_moe_4bit_swap.py` covers:

- env-var gating (`is_gemma4_moe_4bit_enabled`)
- no-op on models without `Gemma4TextExperts`
- graceful `0` return when transformers does not expose `Gemma4TextExperts`
- idempotence on a stub `Gemma4TextExperts` module (GPU path; CPU path validates the no-op branch)

```
$ python -m pytest tests/test_gemma4_moe_4bit_swap.py tests/test_issue_5344_guardrail.py -q
...........                                                              [100%]
11 passed in 0.22s
```

## Depends on

#5430 (the guardrail). This PR is opened against `fix-issue-5344-quantization-guardrail`; please merge that one first.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)

Per-expert LoRA on the swapped `nn.ModuleList[Linear4bit]` so QLoRA training works with `UNSLOTH_GEMMA4_MOE_4BIT=1`. That unblocks flipping the default to ON.

Refs #5344

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_gemma4_moe_4bit_swap.py tests/test_issue_5344_guardrail.py` (11/11)
- [x] Manual: `unsloth/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` load with `UNSLOTH_GEMMA4_MOE_4BIT=1` reports `swapped 30 Gemma4TextExperts module(s)`, resident VRAM 14.27 GB, forward cosine 0.994 vs BF16.
- [x] No regression on non-MoE: `unsloth/gemma-3-1b-it` (local + HF), `unsloth/gemma-4-E2B-it` (local + HF) load identically with and without `UNSLOTH_GEMMA4_MOE_4BIT=1`.
- [x] Failure-soft: a deliberately broken `transformers.models.gemma4.modeling_gemma4` import yields `0` swapped and no raise.

author: sfabbro
body:
💡 **What**: Refactored the PyTorch dynamic boolean indexing operations (`input[mask]`) in `MaskedGaussianNLLLoss`, `WeightedMaskedMSELoss`, `MaskedMSELoss`, and `MaskedMAELoss` to use full-tensor in-place masking (`.masked_fill(~mask, 0.0)`).

🎯 **Why**: In PyTorch, filtering a tensor with a boolean mask generates a dynamically-sized tensor. This forces the GPU to synchronize with the CPU to calculate the allocation size, severely bottlenecking the training loop. By keeping the full tensor shape and zeroing out invalid entries using `.masked_fill`, the operations stay strictly on the GPU, avoiding costly blocking overheads.

📊 **Impact**: Microbenchmarks show a ~15-25% reduction in execution time on loss evaluation, which significantly reduces total step latency when accumulated over thousands of training steps across large batches. 

🔬 **Measurement**: Verified the functional correctness by confirming existing unit tests evaluate to the precise output matching the previous logic. Run `pixi run test` to execute the full validation suite. Also verified `reduction="none"` handles output shapes properly.

author: stephane-segning
body:
## Summary

Tier-4 builder extensions: three renderer-extension verbs that share the read-builder surface area.

- **#4 Aggregate API** — `.aggregate().count() / sum(col) / avg(col) / min(col) / max(col)`. `count` returns `i64` (PG semantics: empty match → 0). The column ops return `Option<T>` for a caller-chosen `T`, decoded via the backend's scalar trait (`sqlx::Decode` / `rusqlite::FromSql`). Filters apply the **read policy** on sqlx so aggregate counts never leak rows the caller can't list. Both backends layer in the soft-delete filter implicitly.
- **#6 `delete_many(filter)`** — parallel to `update_many`: refuses predicate-less calls, soft-delete-aware (tombstones via `deleted_at = NOW()` / `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` and bumps `@version` if declared), per-row audit + outbox fan-out via `RETURNING`. Returns `BatchSummary { total, ok, err: 0 }`.
- **#11 NULLS FIRST/LAST** — `OrderClause::nulls_first()` / `nulls_last()`. Default stays `NULLS LAST` (framework-wide consistency across PG and SQLite — PG defaults differ between ASC and DESC, SQLite defaults to FIRST for both, so a single explicit default keeps listings deterministic). Bare-column ORDER BY now emits the NULLS clause explicitly on both runtime + preview paths (was previously inconsistent: relation scalars got it, plain columns did not). Three pre-existing `include_schema` preview-SQL assertions updated to match.

Re-exports updated through `cratestack` umbrella: `Aggregate` / `AggregateCount` / `AggregateColumn`, `DeleteMany` / `ScopedDeleteMany`, `NullOrder`.

## PG SUM type note

`SUM(BIGINT)` returns `NUMERIC` in PostgreSQL, so callers decode into `Decimal`-compatible scalars (or `INTEGER` columns which sum into `BIGINT`). The framework doesn't paper over this — call sites pick the scalar type that matches PG's promotion rules. The integration test for sum uses `cratestack::Decimal` and documents the contract.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check --workspace` clean
- [x] `cargo test --workspace` — no failures (110+ test binaries)
- [x] New rusqlite integration tests (`tests/tier4_builders.rs`, 10 tests):
  - `delete_many` removes matching rows; refuses without filter
  - `aggregate.count` total + filtered
  - `aggregate.sum / min / max / avg` round-trip
  - `nulls_first` and default `nulls_last` placement on `order_by`
- [x] New PG integration tests against testcontainers (`tests/banking_builder_extensions_tier4.rs`, 6 tests):
  - aggregate sum filtered through read policy (the named upstream site)
  - aggregate count returns 0 on empty match
  - aggregate min/max round-trip
  - `delete_many` writes one audit row per deleted refund + survival count
  - `delete_many` predicate-less rejection
  - `nulls_first` preview-SQL emission + live PG execution
- [x] Render-level unit tests on both backends for `nulls_first` and `render_delete_many`
- [x] Three existing `include_schema` ORDER BY preview-SQL assertions updated to include the now-emitted `NULLS LAST` clause on plain columns (deliberate consistency fix — was a minor latent bug)

author: inureyes
body:
Fixes #200.

## Problem

Two distinct defects in credential collection both surface in:

```
bssh -C orin -l lablup --password -S ping
```

### Defect 1 — `--password` was collected lazily, per-connection

`ssh/auth.rs::password_auth()` called `rpassword::prompt_password()` inside each per-node authentication task. The executor fans out N parallel connection attempts, so multiple tasks raced for stdin: the prompt could be missed (drowned by the indicatif progress UI), repeated per node, or interleaved with the progress bar rendering.

The `-S` (sudo-password) path already did this correctly — it collected once in the dispatcher, wrapped the value in `Arc<SudoPassword>`, and shared it across tasks. `--password` now follows the same pattern.

### Defect 2 — `-S` was silently dropped by `ping`, `upload`, `download`

The dispatcher only read `cli.sudo_password` in the `exec` and interactive branches. Users could pass `-S` to `ping`/`upload`/`download` without any error, but the flag had no effect.

## Changes

### New `Password` wrapper — `src/security/password.rs`

Mirrors the existing `SudoPassword` design:
- Backed by `secrecy::SecretString` (auto-zeroized on drop via the `secrecy` crate's `SecretString` machinery).
- `prompt_password()` uses a non-host-specific prompt: `"Enter SSH password (used for all hosts): "`.
- `get_password_from_env()` reads `BSSH_PASSWORD` (discouraged for production but useful for automation).
- `get_password(warn_env)` combines env + interactive prompt.
- Designed to be wrapped in `Arc<Password>` and shared across parallel tasks without copying the secret.

### Dispatcher hoists `--password` collection — `src/app/dispatcher.rs`

The prompt now runs once at the top of `dispatch_command`, **before** any `ParallelExecutor` is built and **before** any indicatif `MultiProgress` is initialized. This avoids the terminal-state pitfall where indicatif corrupts the prompt rendering. The resulting `Arc<Password>` is threaded through:

- `ping_nodes(...)` — new parameter
- `FileTransferParams` (upload + download) — new field
- `ExecuteCommandParams` — new field
- `InteractiveCommand` — new field
- SSH-mode interactive path

### `-S` semantics for non-applicable subcommands

The dispatcher now emits `tracing::warn!("--sudo-password (-S) has no effect for the {subcommand} subcommand and will be ignored")` when `-S` is passed to `ping`, `upload`, `download`, `list`, or `cache-stats`. Picked a warning over a hard reject because:

- Matches typical CLI UX (`ssh`, `git`, etc. tend to warn rather than fail on flags that are harmless-but-inapplicable).
- Existing scripts that happen to pass `-S` to non-applicable subcommands continue to work — they just see a visible warning instead of silent no-op.
- `exec` and interactive paths continue to honor `-S` exactly as before.

### Threading through the auth machinery

- `AuthContext` (`src/ssh/auth.rs`) gains a `password: Option<Arc<Password>>` field and `with_pre_collected_password()` builder.
- `password_auth()` now consumes the pre-collected value when available. The in-task `rpassword::prompt_password()` call is retained only as the fallback for the OpenSSH-style "all key methods failed → prompt for password" path (which is opportunistic and has no dispatcher-side collection point).
- `ParallelExecutor::with_ssh_password()`, `ExecutionConfig::ssh_password`, `ConnectionConfig::ssh_password`, and the SFTP `*_with_jump_hosts` helpers all carry the `Option<Arc<Password>>` through to the auth layer.
- Every per-node task clones the `Arc` so all tasks observe the same secret without duplicating the underlying string.

## Tests

### New: `src/security/password.rs` — 9 unit tests

Mirror `src/security/sudo.rs` test structure:
- `test_password_creation`, `test_password_empty_rejection`, `test_password_debug_redaction`
- `test_clone_independence`, `test_arc_sharing`
- Env var tests: `_empty`, `_valid`, `_not_set`
- **`test_get_password_dispatcher_collection_pattern`** — explicitly models the dispatcher-level collection pattern: one `get_password()` call, wrapped in `Arc<Password>`, observably shared across three simulated per-node tasks. Asserts all three see the same password and `Arc::strong_count == 4`.

### New: `src/ssh/auth.rs` — 2 unit tests

- `test_auth_context_with_pre_collected_password` — verifies the builder and `Arc` sharing semantics.
- `test_password_auth_uses_pre_collected_password` — critically, verifies `password_auth()` returns immediately without prompting when the pre-collected value is set (which means it never blocks on stdin in non-interactive test environments).

### Existing tests

All 1233 library unit tests and the integration test suites continue to pass. Pre-existing failing doctest in `src/server/filter/mod.rs` is unrelated to this PR (verified by running `cargo test --doc` on `main`).

## Verification

```
cargo build --release      # passes
cargo test --lib           # 1233 lib tests pass
cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings  # passes
cargo fmt --check          # passes
```

## Behavior comparison

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `bssh -C cluster --password exec "uptime"` | Multiple prompts race for stdin or interleave with progress bars; possibly missed entirely | One clean prompt up-front, value reused for all N nodes |
| `bssh -C cluster --password ping` | Same broken behavior | One clean prompt up-front |
| `bssh -C cluster --password upload f.txt /tmp/` | Same broken behavior | One clean prompt up-front |
| `bssh -S ping` | Flag silently ignored | `WARN: --sudo-password (-S) has no effect for the 'ping' subcommand and will be ignored` |
| `bssh -S exec "sudo apt update"` | Worked correctly | Unchanged — still works |
| `BSSH_PASSWORD=secret bssh -C cluster --password ping` | Not supported | Reads from env (with warning), still single value shared across nodes |

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Running `bssh -C <cluster> --password <subcommand>` prompts exactly once, before any connection attempt or progress UI output.
- [x] The same password is used for every node in the cluster.
- [x] Password memory is zeroized after use (via `secrecy::SecretString` in `Password`).
- [x] `-S` either applies to applicable subcommands or warns when passed to subcommands where it has no effect.
- [x] Existing tests pass.
- [x] A unit test covers the dispatcher-level password collection (`test_get_password_dispatcher_collection_pattern`).

author: ashwat287
body: Updated with dual-arch support. Both amd64 and arm64 work end-to-end now. Ref: #4852 ## What's in this commit - `WINDOWS` OS type added to `limatype` and validation - Separate `autounattend.xml` templates for amd64 and arm64 (3-pass: windowsPE, specialize, oobeSystem) - Windows guests go through `generateWindowsISO()` which produces a Joliet-labeled ISO - `hack/gen-autounattend-iso.go` dev tool for standalone testing (pass `-arch amd64` or `-arch arm64`) - Unit test for template rendering ## Design choices - arm64 uses NVMe for the disk. WinPE ARM has `stornvme.sys` built-in, so there's no need for `virtio-win.iso`. - No product keys in either template. Removed per @AkihiroSuda's feedback. Edition selection is handled by image index. - OpenSSH server is installed and started during OOBE so Lima's host-agent can connect. ## Testing Tested both architectures on macOS. ### amd64 (x86_64) Windows 10 consumer ISO from [microsoft.com](https://www.microsoft.com/en-in/software-download/windows10ISO), version 22H2 multi-edition. Pro is image index 6. ```bash go run hack/gen-autounattend-iso.go -arch amd64 -o autounattend.iso qemu-img create -f qcow2 disk.qcow2 64G cp /opt/homebrew/share/qemu/edk2-i386-vars.fd ovmf_vars.fd qemu-system-x86_64 -m 4G -smp 2 -machine q35 \ -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=/opt/homebrew/share/qemu/edk2-x86_64-code.fd \ -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=ovmf_vars.fd \ -cdrom /path/to/Win10_22H2_English_x64v1.iso \ -drive file=autounattend.iso,media=cdrom,index=3 \ -drive file=disk.qcow2,index=0,media=disk,format=qcow2 \ -nic user,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 ``` This runs under emulation on Apple Silicon so it's slow, but completes successfully. ### arm64 (aarch64) Windows 11 ARM64 25H2 ISO. Pro is image index 3. Runs natively via HVF. ```bash go run hack/gen-autounattend-iso.go -arch arm64 -o autounattend.iso qemu-img create -f qcow2 disk.qcow2 64G dd if=/dev/zero of=ovmf_vars.fd bs=1M count=64 qemu-system-aarch64 \ -machine virt,accel=hvf \ -cpu host \ -m 4G -smp 4 \ -drive if=pflash,format=raw,readonly=on,file=/opt/homebrew/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd \ -drive if=pflash,format=raw,file=ovmf_vars.fd \ -drive file=disk.qcow2,if=none,id=hd0,format=qcow2 \ -device nvme,serial=lima0,drive=hd0 \ -device qemu-xhci \ -device usb-kbd \ -device usb-tablet \ -drive file=/path/to/Win11_25H2_English_Arm64.iso,if=none,id=cdrom0,media=cdrom,readonly=on \ -device usb-storage,drive=cdrom0 \ -drive file=autounattend.iso,if=none,id=unattend,media=cdrom,readonly=on \ -device usb-storage,drive=unattend \ -device ramfb \ -nic user,hostfwd=tcp::2222-:22 ``` The arm64 command is longer because the `virt` machine has no built-in controllers (no SATA, no IDE, no VGA), so each device needs to be added explicitly. On amd64, q35 provides all of that. ## Result Both architectures install fully unattended: partitioning, image extraction, OOBE, and OpenSSH server all complete without manual interaction. After install completes: `ssh -p 2222 User@localhost` ## Notes - arm64 requires `-cpu host`, not `-cpu max`. Using `max` with HVF causes page faults. - UEFI variable store needs to be 64MB on arm64 (4MB on x86). - `usb-kbd`/`usb-tablet` are needed on arm64 for UEFI console initialization. ## Changes since last review - Removed product key from both templates - Added arm64 template with NVMe disk (no virtio-win.iso needed) - Dropped `-boot d` from amd64 (OVMF ignores it)

author: ibrahimdans
body:
### Summary

Closes: [#628](https://github.com/embedpdf/embed-pdf-viewer/issues/628)

Add `workerUrl` and `encoderWorkerUrl` options to `CreatePdfiumEngineOptions` so that the PDFium worker and the image encoder worker pool can be loaded from a static URL instead of a `blob:` object URL.

- `workerUrl` — URL to the PDFium worker script
- `encoderWorkerUrl` — URL to the image encoder worker script
- Both options are propagated through the React/shared, Svelte, and Vue hooks
- When omitted, the existing `blob:` fallback is preserved (no breaking change)

### Motivation

Apps with a strict Content Security Policy that omit `blob:` from `worker-src` (or `child-src`) are currently blocked when using `usePdfiumEngine({ worker: true })`:

```
Refused to create a worker from 'blob:...' because it violates the CSP directive: "worker-src 'self'"
```

This is a blocker for banking, healthcare, and defense environments where compliance frameworks flag `worker-src blob:`. Libraries like pdf.js and monaco-editor already expose the worker as a configurable URL — this PR brings EmbedPDF in line with that pattern.

### Usage

```ts
// Vite — bundle the worker as a static asset
usePdfiumEngine({
  wasmUrl: '/assets/pdfium.wasm',
  workerUrl: new URL('@embedpdf/engines/pdfium-worker-engine', import.meta.url).href,
  encoderWorkerUrl: '/assets/embedpdf-encoder-worker.js',
});

// Or serve pre-copied static files
usePdfiumEngine({
  wasmUrl: '/assets/pdfium.wasm',
  workerUrl: '/assets/embedpdf-worker.js',
  encoderWorkerUrl: '/assets/embedpdf-encoder-worker.js',
});
```

CSP header can then be simply:

```
worker-src 'self'
```

### Notes

- No tests added: `@embedpdf/engines` has no test infrastructure today. The branching logic (`workerUrl ?? createObjectURL(...)`) is minimal enough that the diff is self-explanatory.
- The `/docs/snippet/airgapped` page would benefit from a short section on these two options — happy to contribute that separately if the maintainers agree on the API shape.

body:
Drives a persistent tmux pane as an interactive shell agent to get around claude code -p. User messages are sent via send-keys; responses are extracted from the scrollback buffer so terminal scrolling never bleeds previous turns into the next response.

Key features:
- Multi-workspace: each workspace gets its own named tmux window (session:workspace-name), with Claude Code auto-started via init_command on first use

- AgentOptsProvider: new core interface so workspace agents inherit agent-specific options (session name etc.) during multi-workspace cloning

author: sfc-gh-okalaci
body:
The pre-commit hook for iceberg writes (ApplyTrackedIcebergMetadataChanges, track_iceberg_metadata_changes.c) used to discover what files this transaction added by:

  1. SELECTing every (id, path, partition, ...) row for the relation from lake_table.files via GetTableDataFilesByPathHashFromCatalog;
  2. reading the last-pushed iceberg metadata.json from object storage;
  3. diffing the two by path to compute added vs removed files;
  4. issuing a second narrow SPI query against lake_table.data_file_column_stats to attach min/max stats to each added file (LoadColumnStatsForFiles).

Both 1 and 4 are linear in the number of files in the iceberg table (not just the ones added in this tx), so this work grows over the table's lifetime.

But for the common append-only case (INSERT INTO iceberg ...), we ALREADY have, at commit time, the full TableMetadataOperation list for every file we added -- we built it ourselves from the writer flushes inside ApplyDataFileModifications and handed it to ApplyDataFileCatalogChanges to write the catalog rows. Re-deriving that list from the catalog at commit is pure overhead.

This commit adds a fast path that captures those ops in memory:

  - TableMetadataOperationTracker gains two fields: List *trackedAddedFileOps  -- deep copy in TopTransactionContext of every DATA_FILE_ADD op applied so far in this tx for this relation, with leaf-field stats rebuilt via CreateDataFileColumnStats so all pointers point at tx-context memory;
      bool fastPathDisabled      -- set on any op type we can't
                                    cheaply represent in memory
                                    (REMOVE, REMOVE_ALL, DROP_TABLE,
                                    UPDATE_DELETED_ROW_COUNT,
                                    ADD_DELETE_MAPPING,
                                    ADD_ROW_ID_MAPPING, DDL,
                                    PARTITION_BY, MANIFEST_MERGE,
                                    SNAPSHOT_EXPIRE), as well as on
                                    any subtransaction abort.
  - TrackAppliedDataFileOperations is called from
    writable_table.c::ApplyMetadataChanges and test/add_files_to_table.c
    right after ApplyDataFileCatalogChanges, deep-copying ADD ops and
    flagging non-ADD ops.
  - GetDataFileMetadataOperations starts with
    TryFastPathDataFileOperations. When applicable it skips the catalog
    diff query, skips LoadColumnStatsForFiles entirely, and returns the
    tracked ops -- still issuing the (already-batched, from an earlier
    commit) DeleteInProgressFileRecords for the added paths since those
    rows were written by the LOAD phase and have to go.
  - A SubXactCallback (lazily registered) flips
    fastPathDisabled = true on every tracker on SUBXACT_EVENT_ABORT_SUB.
    Rather than try to surgically un-track only ops written in the
    aborted subtxn, we conservatively force the diff path for the rest
    of the outer transaction. The diff path is always correct (iceberg
    metadata is the source of truth, catalog has every successful write
    since), so this is a pure cost trade.
  - Session counters IcebergCommitFastPathHits /
    IcebergCommitFastPathFallbacks are incremented at the branch, and
    DEBUG1 messages are emitted from both paths so server logs can
    confirm which path was taken in CI.

The pre-existing static helper CreateDataFileColumnStats (data_files_catalog.c) had to be promoted to a public symbol so the tracker can rebuild LeafFields without leaking statement-context pointers; its semantics (allocates in CurrentMemoryContext, rebuilds the Field via PostgresTypeToIcebergField) are unchanged.

Tests (tests/pytests/test_iceberg_commit_fast_path.py) cover the four selector cases: pure INSERT (fast path), INSERT + DELETE (slow path via DATA_FILE_ADD_DELETE_MAPPING), INSERT + SAVEPOINT + ROLLBACK + INSERT (slow path via SubXactCallback), and INSERT + ALTER TABLE (slow path via TABLE_DDL). They assert correctness of the resulting catalog state, not which path was internally taken, because the path choice is an implementation detail and both paths must produce the same iceberg table.

Empirical, 60 batches x 400 files = 24000 files in one tx, local PG17
+ MinIO, on top of the previous commits in this series:

  step               bulk-insert   this commit
  -----------------+--------------+-------------
  COMMIT              2.89 s        1.54 s
  LOAD (60 COPYs)     414.2 s       409.9 s

The 1.35 s savings here is the entire commit-time catalog read + stats SPI, ~47% of remaining commit time on this bench. At larger file counts the win grows linearly: every file in the table no longer pays a commit-time scan + stats lookup, only the ones added in this tx. The slow path is unchanged for workloads that take it (DELETE, ALTER, subtxn aborts, MERGE).

## Summary

**Phase 1: Foundation & Document Lifecycle**
**Goal:** Users can open, save, and manage PDF documents with the application integrated into Windows
**Status:** Verified

Electron desktop PDF editor for Windows. Users can open PDFs (via dialog, drag-and-drop, or Windows file association), save them (Save and Save As), and the application registers itself for Windows PDF file associations.

## Changes

### Plan 01-01: Electron Shell Setup
Scaffolded the Electron project with Forge-based build, Squirrel.Windows packaging, preload script with contextIsolation, and the main/renderer process structure.

**Key files:** package.json, electron-builder.json, forge.config.cjs, tsconfig.main.json, tsconfig.renderer.json, src/main/index.ts, src/preload/index.ts, src/renderer/

### Plan 01-02: IPC Bridge
Established invoke/handle and send/on channels between main and renderer processes, defining the channel contract for document lifecycle operations.

**Key files:** src/shared/channels.ts (created), src/main/ipc.ts (created), src/main/index.ts, src/preload/index.ts, src/renderer/index.ts

### Plan 01-03: File I/O Layer
Implemented file dialog (open/save/saveAs), drag-and-drop handling, Windows file association registration, and document open/save flow.

**Key files:** src/main/file-io.ts (created), src/main/window-state.ts (created), src/main/ipc.ts, src/main/index.ts, src/renderer/, package.json

## Requirements Addressed

- [x] **GEN-01**: User can save PDFs (Save and Save As)
- [x] **GEN-03**: Application respects Windows file associations

## Verification

- [x] TypeScript compilation: zero errors (main + renderer)
- [x] UAT: 10/10 tests passed, 0 issues
- [x] Security audit: 7 threats identified, 7 closed, 0 open
- [x] All 3 plans executed with zero deviations from plan

## Key Decisions

- Electron Forge + Squirrel.Windows for packaging; contextIsolation enabled; preload script for IPC
- IPC bridge keeps PDF bytes in main process to avoid payload limits
- PDF bytes transferred as base64 over IPC (contextIsolation compatible)
- File association uses HKEY_CURRENT_USER (no admin required)
- Window state saved as JSON in app.getPath('userData')
- Last-opened file restored on launch

author: vaayne
body:
## Summary

Admins were seeing all users' personal workspace data (sessions, tasks, scheduler jobs) through the same endpoints non-admins use. This PR enforces per-user scoping on all personal-workspace endpoints regardless of admin status, while leaving intentional admin management capabilities (agents, channels, providers) untouched.

### Frontend (`web/`)
- Unified `is_admin` sourcing across Channels, Scheduler, and Automations pages to use the shared `meQueryOptions` cache instead of ad-hoc `/api/auth/me` calls
- Fixed settings default redirect: admins → `/settings/providers`, regular users → `/settings/agents`
- Gated agent list items and save button behind ownership check (`canEditAgent`) so non-owners see agents as read-only
- Changed new agent default scope from `"system"` to `"restricted"` for non-admins

### Backend (`server/`)

**`sessions.go`**
- `ListSessions`: always sets `opts.UserID` — admin no longer receives all users' sessions
- `GetSession`: removed `!IsAdmin` guard — admin can only fetch their own sessions
- `checkSessionAccess` (used by `GetSessionMessages`, `GetSessionWorkspace`): removed `IsAdmin` bypass

**`tasks.go`**
- `ListAgentTasks`: always passes `isAdmin=false` to `ListTasks`
- `GetAgentTask`, `ListAgentTaskEvents`: ownership enforced for admin
- `UpdateAgentTask`, `DeleteAgentTask`, `AgentTaskAction`: always pass `isAdmin=false` to service layer

**`scheduler.go`**
- `ListSchedulerJobs`: plugin-owned jobs filtered for everyone; user-ID check applies to admin
- `UpdateSchedulerJob`, `DeleteSchedulerJob`: ownership enforced for admin
- `TriggerSchedulerJob`: plugin-job block applies to everyone; ownership enforced
- `ListSchedulerJobRuns`: ownership enforced for admin

## Test plan

- [ ] As admin: sessions page shows only admin's own sessions
- [ ] As admin: automations page shows only admin's own tasks and scheduler jobs
- [ ] As admin: attempting to access another user's session/task/job by direct ID returns 403
- [ ] As non-admin: no change in visible data
- [ ] Agents page: admin still sees and can manage all agents (intentional)
- [ ] `mise run test` passes

author: guzzzzzzzz
body:
## Security Audit: 3 New Vulnerabilities in Coalition & Claims Modules

### Wallet: RTC241359b3438d1222fdc1c3e22fe980657a4bc54e

### Bug Summary

| # | Component | Vulnerability | Severity | File:Line |
|---|-----------|---------------|----------|-----------|
| 1 | Coalition Voting | Vote weight desync on vote change | HIGH | coalition.py:596-629 |
| 2 | Claims Eligibility | Unit conversion 100x error (uRTC to RTC) | CRITICAL | claims_eligibility.py:577 |
| 3 | Coalition Voting | Phantom vote weight accumulation | MEDIUM | coalition.py:604-617 |

### BUG 1: Coalition Vote Weight Desync (HIGH)
Location: node/coalition.py lines 596-629
When a voter changes their vote, the handler subtracts the old stored weight (old_vote[1]) from the previous column, but adds the current weight (freshly fetched) to the new column. If the voter's RTC balance or antiquity multiplier changed between votes, the total tally (votes_for + votes_against) drifts from reality.

### BUG 2: Claims Eligibility 100x Unit Mismatch (CRITICAL)
Location: node/claims_eligibility.py line 577
reward_rtc uses /100_000_000 (10^8) but canonical UNIT=1_000_000 (10^6). The eligibility API reports rewards as 100x smaller than actual payouts.

### BUG 3: Phantom Vote Weight Accumulation (MEDIUM)
Location: node/coalition.py lines 604-617
When IntegrityError fires but old_vote is None (race condition), subtraction is skipped but new weight still added, inflating tallies.

All 7 PoC tests pass. Run: python -m pytest tests/test_coalition_claims_bugs.py -v --noconftest

Related: Issue #305 (Bug Report Bounty)
Wallet: RTC241359b3438d1222fdc1c3e22fe980657a4bc54e

### Key features

- **Storefront API client** with direct fetch (no proxy needed for per-store throttling), optional Web Bot Auth signing, and Shopify-specific throttle handling
- **ID-based pagination** via `products(query: "scope id:>lastId", sortKey: ID)` — avoids the 25K cursor limit entirely
- **Single-page job architecture** — each BullMQ job fetches one page (250 products), processes it, then enqueues the next page. With concurrency 3, all stores are extracted simultaneously with natural round-robin
- **`shopify_products` lookup table** with bigint PK for O(1) product resolution. Caches card matching result so subsequent runs skip the full matching pipeline
- **Batched DB operations** — bulk upsert product_urls, bulk status updates, pre-warmed printing matcher caches (all 33K card names + 727 sets loaded at startup)
- **Scheduler endpoints** for triggering extraction via HTTP
- **Per-store `storefrontScope` config** scopes queries to MTG singles via product_type filter

### Architecture

```
Scheduler (port 5001)          Scraper workers (×3)
PUT /manual/storefront/trigger → BullMQ queue → StorefrontProcessor
                                                  ↓
                               Shopify Storefront API (250 products/page)
                                                  ↓
                               processPage → bulkUpsert → match → listings
                                                  ↓
                               enqueue next page job (if more products)
```

### New files
- `packages/core/src/platform/adapters/shopify-storefront/` — StorefrontClient, StorefrontExtractionAdapter, types, queries
- `packages/core/src/web-bot-auth/` — WebBotAuthService for RFC 9421 signing
- `packages/core/src/database/shopify-product.entity.ts` — ShopifyProduct lookup table
- `apps/scraper/src/storefront/` — StorefrontProcessor, StorefrontModule
- `apps/api/src/database/migrations/1747267200000-AddShopifyProducts.ts`

### Test results
- Tested against all 8 stores simultaneously
- 401 Games: 160K+ products, 97% match rate
- BinderPos stores: 94-95% match rate
- F2F: 98% match rate
- Zero Shopify rate limiting at full speed

- [ ] Run `nx run core:test` — 166+ tests pass
- [ ] Docker: `docker-compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up`

author: thekadhikari
body:
## Bug

Importing `@/lib/utils/http` from a `'use client'` file fails the build:

> You're importing a module that depends on `next/headers`. This API is only available in Server Components in the App Router, but you are using it in the Pages Router.

The error trace points to `shared/server-cookies.ts`, which is reached transitively through the http barrel even though we tried to fence it behind a runtime check + dynamic import. Bundlers (Webpack, Turbopack) statically resolve dynamic-import targets, so `next/headers` and `server-only` end up in the client graph regardless.

This is a real architectural constraint of Next.js's module resolution — no runtime guard can satisfy it.

## Why the previous design didn't work

The original `shared/cookie-injection.ts` did:

```ts
async function getCookieHeaderForRequest() {
  if (isBrowser()) return undefined;
  const { readServerCookieHeader } = await import('./server-cookies');
  return readServerCookieHeader();
}
```

This `if (isBrowser())` is a **runtime** check. The bundler doesn't evaluate it — it sees `import('./server-cookies')` as a graph edge and resolves the target eagerly to chunk it. `server-cookies.ts` has `import 'server-only'` at the top, which fails the build check the moment that file is reachable from a client-bundled module.

## Fix

Split the public API into two entry points:

| Entry | Use from | Cookies |
|---|---|---|
| `@/lib/utils/http` | Anywhere — client components, Server Components, isomorphic utils | Browser jar handles it natively in the browser; no server-side forwarding |
| `@/lib/utils/http/server` | Server Components, Server Actions, Route Handlers | Reads `next/headers` and forwards cookies on every call |

`'server-only'` fences the server entry — importing it from a `'use client'` file fails the build with a clear error.

Both interceptors gained an optional `cookieResolver: () => Promise<string | undefined>` parameter. The universal entry passes none; the server entry passes one that reads `next/headers` directly. No more runtime-aware branching inside `shared/` — that whole pattern was wrong.

## Regression gate

Added `src/lib/utils/http/__bundle-sentinel__/client-bundle-sentinel.tsx` — a `'use client'` file that imports every public symbol from `@/lib/utils/http` and is referenced from `app/[locale]/layout.tsx`. Any future change that drags server-only code into the universal entry now fails `yarn build` and CI immediately. The original defect would have been caught at commit time with this in place.

A commented-out sentinel-check line in the file documents how to verify the gate still works (uncomment, expect build failure, revert).

## Test changes

- `fetch-client/interceptors.test.ts` rewritten to test the resolver callback directly (passes/skips/overwrites) — simpler and tests the actual contract.
- Removed obsolete `shared/cookie-injection.test.ts` (module deleted).
- Added a `server-only` stub to `test/setup.ts` so server-side modules can be unit-tested under jsdom. Production builds unaffected.

## Migration for consumers

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `import { fetchClient } from '@/lib/utils/http'` in a `'use client'` file | No change |
| `import { fetchClient } from '@/lib/utils/http'` in a Server Component that needs cookies | `import { fetchClient } from '@/lib/utils/http/server'` |
| `import { fetchClient } from '@/lib/utils/http'` in a Server Component calling public endpoints | No change |

## Test plan

- [x] `yarn ci:check` — Biome lint + format + import sort
- [x] `yarn type-check`
- [x] `yarn check:deprecated`
- [x] `yarn test` — 124 tests across 18 files
- [x] `yarn build` — production build green
- [x] Sentinel verified to trip on intentional regression
- [ ] CI green on this PR

## Summary

* CVE: [CVE-2026-24001](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-24001)
* Advisory: [GHSA-73rr-hh4g-fpgx](https://github.com/kpdecker/jsdiff/security/advisories/GHSA-73rr-hh4g-fpgx)
* Fix versions: 8.0.3, **5.2.2**, 4.0.4, 3.5.1

## Scope of risk in this repo
`diff` is a **dev-only transitive dependency** of `mocha` used to run the VS Code extension tests. It is not shipped in the published extension and is not used to parse untrusted patches.

## Verification
```
cd srs_extension
npm update diff --package-lock-only      # only lock-file change
npm ci                                   # installs cleanly
npm ls diff
# azure-req-doc-ext@0.0.10 ...\srs_extension
# \-- mocha@11.1.0
#   \-- diff@5.2.2
```

Lock file diff is minimal — only the two `diff` entries (the `node_modules/diff` lockfileVersion-2 entry and the legacy compat `diff` entry) had their `version`, `resolved` URL, and `integrity` updated to 5.2.2.

## Tracking
Addresses CG-generated work item [37706567](https://msazure.visualstudio.com/One/_workitems/edit/37706567) (CVE-2026-24001 in diff). The Azure-MessagingStore lock files (the originally-flagged 4.0.2 instances) were already updated to 4.0.4 upstream, so this PR closes out the remaining 5.x exposure for the same CVE.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Closes the Phase-B follow-up review finding **Flag #5**: *"`evidence_embeddings` PRIMARY KEY is `evidence_id` only — single model tag per row"*.

Under the v2 single-column primary key, the cache could hold at most one cached vector per `evidence_id`. When the active embedding model was swapped (e.g. from `xlm-r-v1` to `xlm-r-v2`), the next ingest of the same row would issue `INSERT OR REPLACE` and silently destroy the previous tag's row — meaning every retriever still running under the previous tag would see 100% cache misses until the entire corpus had been re-ingested.

Under the v3 composite primary key `(evidence_id, model_tag)`, both rows can coexist: old retrievers keep getting warm cache hits while new ones backfill in parallel. The `INSERT OR REPLACE` write paths already keyed on both columns, so they were already correct — the only thing missing was the column-level uniqueness guarantee, which v3 now expresses.

### What changed

1. **`crates/evidence_store/src/schema.rs`** — bump `SCHEMA_VERSION` from `2` to `3`. Update `SCHEMA_SQL` to declare the composite primary key directly so fresh databases get the v3 shape without going through the migration path. Update the schema history doc-comment.
2. **`crates/evidence_store/src/store.rs`** — add `apply_migration(3)` → `migrate_evidence_embeddings_to_composite_pk`. The migration is:
   - **Idempotent**: detects v3 shape via `PRAGMA table_info` (counts columns with `pk > 0`); returns `Ok(())` when the table already has the 2-column PK. This is what makes the migration safe to re-run over a fresh DB whose `SCHEMA_SQL` bootstrap already produced the target shape.
   - **Atomic**: wrapped in an `unchecked_transaction` so a crash mid-migration rolls back to the v2 shape.
   - **Standard SQLite recipe**: create `evidence_embeddings_v3` with composite PK → `INSERT INTO ... SELECT ... FROM evidence_embeddings` → `DROP TABLE evidence_embeddings` → `ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO evidence_embeddings` (per https://sqlite.org/lang_altertable.html §7.2).
   - Updates the `apply_migration` doc-comment to remove the stale "every bump is additive" claim and to specify the idempotency contract every future delta must honour.
3. **`crates/evidence_store/src/store.rs`** — doc-update `get_embedding` (tag-agnostic admin/test reader) to flag that under v3 multiple rows can coexist for the same `evidence_id`, and switch the SQL to `ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 1` so the return value is deterministic across `model_tag`s. Production retrieval still goes through `get_embedding_for_model` and is unaffected.
4. **`crates/evidence_store/tests/retrieval.rs`** — two new regression tests:
   - `evidence_embeddings_holds_one_row_per_model_tag_for_same_evidence_id` pins the composite-PK behaviour at the public-API level: two writes under distinct tags coexist, raw row count is exactly 2, and re-writing one tag does **not** touch the other tag's row.
   - `schema_migration_v2_to_v3_widens_pk_and_preserves_rows` hand-builds a v2 database (legacy single-PK shape, `user_version = 2`), seeds two rows, then re-opens with the production `EvidenceStore` and asserts: `user_version` is stamped to 3, seeded rows survive byte-for-byte, the migrated table accepts a second row for the same `evidence_id` under a different `model_tag`, and `pragma_table_info` reports `pk_arity == 2`.
   - Updates the existing `schema_migration_forward_ports_legacy_v1_database` test to assert against `schema::SCHEMA_VERSION` instead of hard-coding the literal `2`, so future bumps don't need to touch it.

### What deliberately did NOT change

- **Production write paths** (`index_embedding`, `index_embedding_or_copy_dedup`, `store_embedding`) — all of them already used `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO evidence_embeddings (evidence_id, embedding, model_tag, created_at)` with all four columns. Under v2's single PK this clobbered any prior row for the same `evidence_id`; under v3's composite PK it now scopes to `(evidence_id, model_tag)` and leaves rows under different tags intact — which is the desired behaviour. No SQL changes were required.
- **`HybridRetriever::candidate_embedding`** — already uses `get_embedding_for_model(id, &self.embedding_model_tag)` (added in the previous PR #22 follow-up commit). Tag-aware reads are already in place.
- **The other 5 Phase-B review findings** (#1 TOCTOU race, #2 `is_available`, #3 hard error propagation, #4 dead defensive arm, #6 no-op migration loop) — those are **PR-C scope**, not this PR. This PR's surface is intentionally narrow.

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

Yellow risk — destructive schema migration of an encrypted table. CI passing is necessary but not sufficient.

- [ ] Confirm the v2→v3 migration recipe (CREATE new → INSERT SELECT → DROP old → RENAME) is acceptable to you on a SQLCipher-encrypted database. SQLCipher transparently encrypts pages, so the same SQL works as on plain SQLite, but I want explicit sign-off.
- [ ] Inspect `migrate_evidence_embeddings_to_composite_pk` in `crates/evidence_store/src/store.rs` and confirm the idempotency check (`PRAGMA table_info` counting `pk > 0` columns) is the right discriminator. An alternative would be inspecting `sqlite_master.sql`, but that's a string match and more fragile.
- [ ] Walk through `schema_migration_v2_to_v3_widens_pk_and_preserves_rows` end-to-end and confirm the v2 fixture it constructs is faithful to what a real v2 DB would look like (the old `CREATE TABLE evidence_embeddings (evidence_id BLOB PRIMARY KEY, ...)` is the exact statement that was in production at v2).

### Test plan

```
cargo test -p evidence_store --test retrieval       # 20 tests, includes the 2 new regressions
cargo test --workspace --all-features               # full suite, all green locally
cargo fmt --all -- --check                          # style
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings   # lint
```

Then watch CI for the same 4 stages.

### Notes

- This is **PR-B** of the agreed 3-PR sequence following PR #23 (Phase C). PR-C will follow, addressing the other 5 evidence_store hygiene findings (#1/#2/#3/#4/#6).
- Starting as **draft** until CI is green. Will mark ready for review automatically once `cargo test`, `clippy`, and `fmt` all pass on CI.

author: fm-yodai
body:
## 背景

Claude Code Review（`claude-code-review.yml`）はレビューを `code-review` スキルに丸投げしており、指摘がゼロのときは PR にコメントを投稿しない既定挙動だった。そのため:

- **「レビューが走って問題なし」なのか「レビューが落ちて未実行」なのか PR 画面で区別できない**
- マージ判断時に「コメントが無い＝大丈夫だろう」という暗黙の推測に依存していた

## 変更

`prompt` に後置指示を追加し、**指摘の有無にかかわらず総括コメントを必ず 1 件投稿**させる:

- 問題なし → `✅ Claude Code Review: 問題なし（LGTM）` + 確認した観点を 3〜5 行
- 指摘あり → `🔧 Claude Code Review: <件数> 件の指摘` + 各指摘の要約

`code-review` スキルの構造化レビュー品質はそのまま活かし、最後の総括コメントだけを強制する最小変更。

## セキュリティ

prompt の変数は `github.repository`（リポジトリ名）と `github.event.pull_request.number`（数値）のみ。攻撃者制御の自由文（issue/PR タイトル・本文等）は不使用のため command injection リスクなし（ワークフローにコメントで明記）。

## 確認方法

この PR 自体で Claude Code Review が走り、**問題なしなら ✅ コメントが付く**ことで動作確認できる（＝本 PR がドッグフーディング）。

body:
### Description of PR

Summary: skip two cases in `tests/syslog/test_logrotate.py` on BMC platforms. Both depend on the `simulate_small_var_log_partition` fixture (defined in the same file), which calls `config_reload(check_intf_up_ports=True, wait_for_bgp=True)` in setup and teardown. BMC has no front-panel ports and no BGP, so both calls wait forever and the fixture errors out.

- `test_logrotate_small_size`
- `test_logrotate_full_partition_no_archives_cleanup`

```yaml
syslog/test_logrotate.py::test_logrotate_small_size:
  skip:
    reason: "Not applicable on BMC: the simulate_small_var_log_partition fixture calls config_reload(check_intf_up_ports=True, wait_for_bgp=True), which never succeeds on BMC (no front-panel ports, no BGP)."
    conditions:
      - "'bmc' in topo_type"

syslog/test_logrotate.py::test_logrotate_full_partition_no_archives_cleanup:
  skip:
    reason: "Not applicable on BMC: the simulate_small_var_log_partition fixture calls config_reload(check_intf_up_ports=True, wait_for_bgp=True), which never succeeds on BMC (no front-panel ports, no BGP)."
    conditions:
      - "'bmc' in topo_type"
```

`test_logrotate_normal_size` does not use the fixture and continues to run on BMC (currently PASSING).

`test_orchagent_logrotate` is separately covered by [#24514](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/pull/24514) (BMC has no orchagent).

### Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix
- [ ] Testbed and Framework(new/improvement)
- [ ] New Test case
    - [x] Skipped for non-supported platforms
- [ ] Test case improvement

### Back port request

- [ ] 202205
- [ ] 202305
- [ ] 202311
- [ ] 202405
- [ ] 202411
- [ ] 202505
- [ ] 202511

### Approach

#### What is the motivation for this PR?

Both cases fail at fixture setup on Komodo BMC (`arm64-nexthop_b27-r0`) — once the recent snmp fix from PR #24084 landed, the residual failure mode became `Failed: Not all ports that are admin up on are operationally up` (no front-panel ports on BMC). Earlier R1 runs sometimes hit `losetup: Device or resource busy` from a stale `/dev/loop2` left by an interrupted prior run, but even with a clean loop device the test cannot get past the fixture's `config_reload(check_intf_up_ports=True, wait_for_bgp=True)`.

The tests validate generic SONiC logrotate behavior on a real-disk `/var/log`. BMC has `/var/log` as `tmpfs` (sized ~365 MB) by default, so this is not BMC-specific coverage anyway.

#### How did you do it?

Two new entries in `tests/common/plugins/conditional_mark/tests_mark_conditions.yaml`, gated on `"'bmc' in topo_type"` — same convention as the other ~30 BMC skips already in this file.

#### How did you verify/test it?

- Verified live on `host1-komodo-bmc` (Aspeed BMC) that `/var/log` is `tmpfs` and that no front-panel ports / no BGP sessions exist, so `check_intf_up_ports=True` / `wait_for_bgp=True` cannot succeed.
- `python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(...))"` confirms YAML parses clean.
- `test_logrotate_normal_size` is not affected — it doesn't use the fixture and still runs on BMC.

#### Any platform specific information?

Only BMC topologies (`'bmc' in topo_type`). No effect on switching platforms.

#### Supported testbed topology if it's a new test case?

N/A.

### Documentation

N/A.

author: stephane-segning
body:
## Summary
Four RPC examples (`rpc-streaming`, `rpc-procedures`, `rpc-batch`, `rpc-batch-debounce`) failed to compile on main with errors like:
```
error[E0425]: cannot find function `encode_rpc_error` in module `::cratestack::rpc`
```
even though all four items (`encode_rpc_error`, `convert_handler_error_response`, `response_to_frame`, `RPC_BINDING_CAPABILITIES`) are `pub` in `cratestack_axum::rpc`.

## Root cause
Not a visibility regression from #31 — a glob-import ambiguity. `crates/cratestack/src/lib.rs` does both:
```rust
pub use cratestack_core::*;   // surfaces cratestack_core::rpc  (wire shapes)
pub use cratestack_axum::*;   // surfaces cratestack_axum::rpc  (server + helpers)
```
Two `rpc` modules globbed in at the same scope makes `::cratestack::rpc::X` ambiguous; rustc emits `warning: rpc is ambiguous` (future-incompat) and resolves to `cratestack_core::rpc`, which lacks the four helpers. The macro-emitted code in the examples then fails to resolve.

## Fix
One line:
```rust
pub use cratestack_axum::rpc;
```
Named imports shadow glob imports, so `::cratestack::rpc` now unambiguously resolves to `cratestack_axum::rpc`. That module already re-exports every wire shape from `cratestack_core::rpc`, so consumers see a strict superset of what they had — no loss of surface.

## Test plan
- [x] `cargo build -p rpc-procedures-example -p rpc-batch-example -p rpc-batch-debounce-example -p rpc-streaming-example` — clean
- [x] `cargo build --workspace --exclude embedded_flutter_native` — clean
- [x] `cargo test -p cratestack-axum -p cratestack-macros -p cratestack` — no regressions
- [x] `ambiguous_glob_imports` future-incompat warning gone
