author: liuhao1024
body:
## Summary

Change the default streaming transport from `"auto"` to `"edit"` to avoid visible content flicker/rollback in Telegram DM responses.

## Root Cause

Commit `4ed293b38` introduced native draft streaming via `sendMessageDraft` (Telegram Bot API 9.5+) and set the default transport to `"auto"`.  On DMs with python-telegram-bot ≥ 22.6, `supports_draft_streaming` returns `True`, routing mid-stream frames through `sendMessageDraft` instead of progressive `editMessageText`.

The problem: `sendMessageDraft` frames are "typing preview" animations in the Telegram client — not real messages.  Each time a new draft frame is sent with the same `draft_id` but more accumulated text, the Telegram client **re-renders the preview from scratch**: existing content briefly collapses or disappears before the updated text renders.  This is Telegram client behavior, not a Hermes bug per se, but the UX result is worse than the legacy edit-based path for most users.

## Fix

Change the default transport from `"auto"` to `"edit"` in three locations:
- `gateway/config.py` — `StreamingConfig.transport` default and `from_dict()` fallback
- `gateway/stream_consumer.py` — `StreamConsumerConfig.transport` default and `_resolve_draft_streaming()` fallback
- `gateway/run.py` — both `StreamConsumerConfig` construction sites

Users who want draft streaming can opt in via `streaming.transport: auto` (or `draft`) in config.yaml.

## Code Intelligence

- Analyzed: `_resolve_draft_streaming` (callers: 1, callees: 0, flows: 1)
- Blast radius: LOW — only `GatewayStreamConsumer.run()` calls this method
- Related patterns: PR #25907 adds empty placeholder drafts for topic mode (orthogonal change)

## Regression Coverage

- `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_draft.py` — 11 tests pass (all explicitly set `transport="auto"` for draft tests)
- `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer.py` — 138 tests pass (existing edit-based tests unaffected)
- `tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_fresh_final.py` — 15 tests pass
- `tests/test_gateway_streaming_nested_config.py` — passes
- `tests/gateway/test_config.py` — passes

## Testing

```bash
scripts/run_tests.sh tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_draft.py tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer.py tests/gateway/test_stream_consumer_fresh_final.py tests/test_gateway_streaming_nested_config.py tests/gateway/test_config.py -x -q
# 164 passed
```

body:
## Summary

Closes the runner-side branch of the references-init bottleneck. \`PluginRegistry.expose_all()\` gains a \`requested_plugins\` kwarg; when set, only plugins in that list (plus introspection + permission + enrichment-only plugins) get \`initialize()\`'d. Profiles that omit references now skip its 7.6s SentenceTransformer model load.

## Why

Three runner-side BootstrapTimer measurements (0.6.91, 0.6.93, 0.6.95) showed \`references\` plugin's init at 7.6-7.9s, 79-81% of runner-side bootstrap. Cost paid by EVERY session — even those whose profile didn't list references — because \`expose_all\` initialized every discovered plugin unconditionally.

\`profile.plugins\` was already the authoritative inclusion gate for tool exposure (per \`_get_essential_plugins\` design). This PR aligns init with that gate.

## Pool-reuse forward-compat

User flagged the interaction: when [pool slot reuse](../memory/project_backlog_pool_slot_reuse_for_cascades.md) lands, sessions in the same slot have different plugin sets. \`expose_all\` is naturally incremental via the \`name not in self._exposed\` filter — a warm slot serving a follow-on session only initializes plugins NEW to that session's requested set. Pool reuse composes with C iff it preserves \`registry._exposed\` state across sessions. Filed as [`project_backlog_pool_reuse_plus_gated_init_interaction.md`](../memory/).

## Test plan
- [x] 10 new tests in \`test_plugin_registry_gated_init.py\` — back-compat (None preserves original) + gated behaviour (essentials always init / enrichment always init / requested-only / skipped-but-registered / config flows only to inited / PARALLEL_INIT respects gate)
- [x] 26/26 in combined runner-tests + new-registry-tests sweep
- [ ] Restart daemon with \`JAATO_BOOTSTRAP_TIMING=true\`, run profile-less smoke + cascade smoke; expect references-init line to drop out of the per-plugin breakdown for sessions that don't include references

## Expected cascade savings

kb-enablement-2.0's 6-stage cascade — if 5 stages don't include references, reclaims ~38s of wall-clock (5 × 7.6s) per cascade run.

author: phuongnse
body:
## Summary

- **`ExecutionStep` aggregate** (WorkflowEngine.Domain): full state machine (`Pending → Running → Completed/Failed/Waiting/Skipped`, `Cancel` from any non-terminal state), `StepType` enum (Form/HttpRequest/Condition/Script/Notification), `ExecutionStepCompleted`/`ExecutionStepFailed` domain events, `IsTerminal` property for Wolverine handler idempotency check (US-093/098)
- **`FormSubmission` aggregate** (FormBuilder.Domain): `Pending/Submitted/Expired/Cancelled` state machine, `Guid AccessToken` for unique no-login form URL, four domain events (`FormTaskCreated/Submitted/Expired/Cancelled`) (US-086–089)
- 34 new unit tests; all 354 unit tests pass

## Design decisions

- `ExecutionStep` is a **standalone aggregate root** (not an entity under `WorkflowExecution`) because step handlers run as independent Wolverine message handlers — each step needs its own transaction boundary and concurrency control; loading the parent aggregate on every step state change would cause contention in parallel executions
- `FormSubmission.AccessToken` is a `Guid` (not JWT) — the token is purely a lookup key; all state/expiry logic lives on the record itself, making the token revocable by changing status without a blacklist
- `StepType` is an enum — all step types are known at compile time; custom step types are explicitly out of MVP scope

## Test plan

- [x] `ExecutionStepTests` — Create, Start, Complete, Fail, Wait, Skip, Cancel, IsTerminal, domain event payloads (21 tests)
- [x] `FormSubmissionTests` — Create, Submit, Expire, Cancel, idempotency edge cases, event payloads (20 tests)

author: jjackson
body:
## Summary

New slash command + skill that takes a Connect program page URL (e.g. `https://labs.connect.dimagi.com/programs/chc`) and produces a fully-populated `spec.yaml` for ace-web's videos surface, then POSTs it as a new program. After the command finishes, the program shows up in the workspace's Videos UI and the operator can click **Re-render** to produce the first MP4.

Pairs with ace-web changes that:
- ship binary upload + audio/music asset migration (#382)
- publish output.mp4 / explorer.tar.gz / feedback.md to Drive on render success (#383)

## What changed

- `commands/video-from-program-page.md` — slash command entry point. Accepts `<program-url>` as first positional + `--slug` / `--workspace` / `--template` / `--gdrive` / `--base-url` flags.
- `skills/video-from-program-page/SKILL.md` — the contract the agent executes:
  1. Fetch ace-web's `60s-campaign-overview` template bundle.
  2. WebFetch the program page (or read operator-pasted source).
  3. Optionally enumerate a Drive folder for media (ace-gdrive MCP).
  4. Fill the prompt's JSON contract, marking unknowns as `[TBD] ...` for grep-ability.
  5. Substitute placeholders into the skeleton → complete spec.yaml.
  6. `POST /api/w/<ws>/videos/programs` with `{slug, spec_yaml}`.
  7. Report the program detail URL + the list of `[TBD]` items needing operator review.

Honors the prompt's per-beat narration word budgets and the brand-voice rule that `narration_hook` must paraphrase the Connect tagline (not invent a new one).

Auth via `ACE_WEB_PAT_TOKEN` Bearer — same pattern as `upload-transcript`; mint via `/ace:ace-web-pat-mint`. Slug collisions surface as 409 without auto-suffixing (slugs are human-meaningful identifiers).

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test test/lib/artifact-manifest-lint.test.ts test/fixtures/artifact-manifest.test.ts` — 15/15 pass (manifest gate not broken).
- [x] No artifact-manifest entry — skill writes outside `ACE/<opp>/runs/<run-id>/`, so it correctly stays off the opportunity manifest.

Replaced a redundant manual `await pokeDB.getLocations()` call inside a debounced `useEffect` with a top-level `@tanstack/react-query` `useQuery` cache in `src/components/LocationSuggestions.tsx`.

🎯 Why
On every keystroke in the search bar, the UI waits for the 250ms debounce and then executes a full read of the IndexedDB `locations` store. Since locations are a static data set, fetching it repeatedly blocks the main thread unnecessarily and incurs constant I/O latency. 

📊 Measured Improvement
IndexedDB hits for the `locations` table dropped from O(k) (k = number of debounced search inputs) to O(1) per session. The `locations` array is now reliably cached in-memory and instantly accessible when filtering.

How to Verify
1. Run `pnpm test` and `pnpm lint`.
2. Launch the app and search for locations in the terminal search. Monitor the network/storage tabs to verify IndexedDB is not repeatedly queried for `locations`.

Swagger UI was unreachable because the docs endpoint was hardcoded and could diverge from the configured API prefix, including cases where the prefix is empty or only slashes. This PR aligns the docs route with the runtime prefix so the Swagger UI is consistently reachable.

- **Routing alignment**
  - Build the Swagger docs path from the configured `API_PREFIX` so docs are served under the versioned API route (or `/docs` when no prefix is set).

- **Operational clarity**
  - Log the resolved Swagger URL to match the actual route.

```ts
const normalizedApiPrefix = apiPrefix.replace(/^\/|\/$/g, '');
const swaggerPath = normalizedApiPrefix
  ? `${normalizedApiPrefix}/docs`
  : 'docs';
SwaggerModule.setup(swaggerPath, app, document);
```

body:
## Summary
Implements issue #128 with a standalone `vault create` command and a `witness` command that create and use passphrase-protected age vaults without writing decrypted vault contents to disk.

What changed:
- replaces the SOPS runtime path with native Haskell age scrypt encrypt/decrypt
- adds `vault create` to import one Cardano payment signing-key envelope, derive its key hash, and write a binary age vault
- supports `--signing-key-paste` for human vault creation, using hidden terminal input for pasted signing-key JSON
- supports `--signing-key-stdin` for automation from a secret manager; terminal stdin is rejected so operators use paste instead
- keeps `--signing-key-file` only as a compatibility/test import path
- updates `witness` to unlock the vault through a no-echo `/dev/tty` prompt or `--vault-passphrase-fd`
- keeps `tx-build`/build unsigned-only; witness output remains raw CBOR hex for `attach-witness`
- refreshes Spec Kit docs, user docs, fixtures, unit tests, and smoke coverage

## Review Focus
- operator custody flow: paste the signing-key envelope once or stream it from a secret manager, create `treasury.vault.age`, then sign only with encrypted vault plus passphrase
- secret intake contract: no argv secrets, no terminal `--signing-key-stdin`, no decrypted vault on disk
- passphrase intake contract: `/dev/tty` no-echo prompt, `--vault-passphrase-fd`, and no argv passphrase
- macOS portability proof: new `Darwin vault TTY smoke` job builds `.#checks.aarch64-darwin.vault-tty-smoke` on GitHub `macos-14`
- use of experimental Hackage `age-0.0.1.0`, isolated in `Amaru.Treasury.Vault.Age`
- supported age scrypt work-factor range is 1-18 so created vaults remain decryptable by `witness`

author: gfazioli
body:
## Summary

Pressing `enter` on a PR row drills into the PR detail (as of v0.11.0). This release adds **`f inspect`** at that level: a full-screen files list with cursor navigation, plus a per-file unified diff viewer with chroma syntax highlighting. First feature request to land off the v0.11.0 Product Hunt thread.

A second sweep across the app emphasises **the key over the label** in every hint line — same convention lazygit / k9s / gh-dash use — so the new keybind (and every existing one) reads as actionable rather than dissolving into the muted footer.

## What lands

### `f inspect` — files list + diff viewer
- New `github.FileChange{Path, Status, Additions, Deletions, Patch, Truncated}` plus `Client.FetchPRFiles`. REST against `/repos/{o}/{n}/pulls/{n}/files` because GraphQL doesn't expose the raw `patch` body.
- `FetchPRDetail` now runs the GraphQL drill-in **and** the REST files fetch **in parallel** (goroutines + `sync.WaitGroup`, same idiom as the v0.10.1 dashboard split). Wall-clock latency stays close to the slower of the two; first error from either side aborts so the drill-in never paints a half-populated payload.
- Patches over **500 hunk lines** are dropped and flagged `Truncated`; pagination caps at **300 files per PR**. Hard limits chosen so a worst-case 5000-line patch can't freeze the viewport.
- `Path` and `Patch` both pass through `github.Sanitize` at the boundary — hostile diff content can't inject ANSI escapes (same defence pattern from v0.11.0).
- `PRFilesModel` nested inside `PRDetailModel` renders the files list: cursor `↑↓ j/k`, status glyphs `A/D/M/R/C`, +Additions/-Deletions counts, viewport-style windowing so the cursor never scrolls off-screen.
- `PRDiffModel` deeper still renders the patch through chroma's `diff` lexer + monokai + terminal256 formatter (chroma is already in the binary via glamour — no new dep). `bubbles/viewport` for scrolling, width-keyed body cache mirroring the markdown body cache.
- Dedicated empty states for binary files, removed entries, content-less renames, and patches truncated by the cap — no blank sections.

### UI hint visibility refactor
- New `internal/ui/hints.go` with `keyHint(key, label)` and `keyHints(pairs ...string)`. The key renders in accent (pink) + bold; the label stays muted; entries join with a shared `keyHintsSep`.
- All hint sites in the app migrate to the helper: three drill-in title bars, their retry hints, the new sub-view footers, three list-tab footers, action menu, settings panel, global footer + scroll-hint suffix, boot loading + error screens.
- `f inspect` moves from the Files-changed meta line up into the title-bar hints alongside `esc / o / r` — every drill-in action concentrated in one visual region.

### Polish
- `urlCopiedMsg` learns a `noun` field so the toast reads \"Path copied\" when we copy a file path and \"URL copied\" when we copy an item URL. New `copyPathCmd` wraps the same primitive with `noun=\"Path\"`.
- `PRDiffModel` grows a `c` keybind that copies the current file's path, plus the matching footer hint.

## Architecture notes

- Two new sub-models (`PRFilesModel`, `PRDiffModel`) nest **inside `PRDetailModel`** rather than as peers of the root model's `repoDetail` / `prDetail` / `issueDetail`. They exist only while a PR detail is open, so the root dispatcher stays untouched — no extra mutual-exclusion bookkeeping at the top level.
- `Client.rest *http.Client` shares the oauth2 transport with the GraphQL client (or falls back to `http.DefaultClient` unauthenticated), so REST and GraphQL use the same auth context without duplicate setup.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build` clean (dual-target: `./octoscope` + `/opt/homebrew/bin/octoscope`)
- [x] `go test -race ./...` passes
- [x] Manual smoke (maintainer): PR with mixed files (added / modified / removed / renamed), patches small / large / truncated, binary / content-less renames render dedicated empty states
- [x] Manual smoke: `c` toast reads \"Path copied\" in the sub-views and still \"URL copied\" in the list tabs
- [x] Manual smoke: every key hint line across the app uses the new accent-key + muted-label style

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Side-by-side diff view (only unified for the first cut)
- `?w=1` ignore-whitespace toggle
- Inline diff comments / review actions — octoscope stays read-only

author: antonydespaux-bit
body:
## Le bug fondamental

La saisie `/controle-gestion/ventes/budgets` affiche **"TOTAL"** sur chaque cellule (jour-de-semaine × lieu × service) et y écrit la somme des occurrences du mois. Exemple Joia mai 2026 : dimanche midi saisi à **23 375 €** = total des 5 dimanches × 4 675 €/dim.

Mais `periodBudgetTotal` sur `/analyses` traitait cette valeur comme un **budget journalier** : pour chaque jour calendaire de la plage, il ajoutait le total mensuel. Conséquence :
- pour 1 dimanche dans la plage → budget calculé = 23 375 € (au lieu de 4 675 €)
- pour mois entier → 5 × 23 375 = 116 875 € (au lieu de 23 375 €)

C'est ce qui expliquait :
- ton retour précédent "le budget Marsan paraît 1,5× trop gros" (en réalité ≈ ×N où N = nb d'occurrences moyennes par mois) ;
- et le retour actuel où, après le fix d'isolation mensuelle (#93), le dimanche Joia tombait à 0 € de budget si la row mai était filtrée par mon `mois ≠ monthNum` strict.

## Le fix

`periodBudgetTotal` et `dailyBudgetForCell` divisent maintenant le total mensuel par le nb naturel d'occurrences du jds dans le mois (`countIsoJdsInMonth`) avant d'additionner.

**Propriété fondamentale validée** : pour une plage = mois entier, le total retourné = le total mensuel saisi exactement. C'est ce qui rend la saisie "TOTAL" cohérente avec l'affichage cumulé.

Le ratio override `nb_jours_override` reste appliqué de la même façon (proportionnel sur la plage).

## Tests

- Tous les tests existants reformulés explicitement avec la sémantique "total mois" + propriété fondamentale ajoutée
- Nouveau test "cas Joia" avec valeurs réelles (23 375 € total → 4 675 € pour un dim seul)
- **49/49 passent** sur `caAnalyses.test.ts`, **70/70** au total

## Known issue — pas dans cette PR

Le même bug existe dans :
- `lib/rapportHebdo.js` → `periodBudget`, `couvertsParService` (page rapport hebdo)
- `app/controle-gestion/ventes/page.js` (logique inline)

Ces deux pages affichent encore des budgets gonflés ≈ ×N. À traiter en suivi : il faut aussi mettre à jour les tests `rapportHebdo` qui dépendent de l'ancien comportement.

## Test plan

- [ ] Joia / `/analyses` / mai → le dimanche 03/05 affiche Δ Budget = `caTot - 4 675` (rouge probablement) au lieu de `+caTot` en gris
- [ ] Marsan / `/analyses` / 01/01→14/05 → le total budget redescend depuis 3,1 M€ vers ≈ 600-700k€ (à valider avec tes config)
- [ ] Vérifier qu'aucun chiffre n'a régressé sur `/ventes` ou `/ventes/rapport-hebdo` (ces pages gardent l'ancien comportement bogué pour l'instant — cohérence entre elles préservée)

- Present whenever `digraphsThNodeLevel === 'intro' || 'practicing'`
- Motion: 200ms opacity fade in; static thereafter (no exit animation per spec §4.2)
- `overflow-hidden` on the parent `<m.main>` clips naturally

Both placements: `pointer-events-none`, `aria-hidden`, `th` label text rendered below the image, cue inert to answer outcomes and pose changes. SVG referenced by direct path `/assets/emma-th-mouth.svg` — NOT added to `EmmaPose` or `EmmaCharacter`.

**App.tsx** wiring follows the `crossVowelMixing` precedent (lines 1148-1162): computes `wordSongDigraphsThLevel` + `wordSongDigraphsThFirstEncounter` from `loadProgress()` once at session-start, freezes on the prop, resets in both the imperative teardown ref and the leave-effect's `queueMicrotask`.

## Why

Spec #231 — `design/word-song/digraphs-th-mouth-cue-integration.md`. The `/θ/` digraph requires a visible articulation cue because the `th` sound is not phonetically transparent to Tagalog-primary speakers. The mouth cue provides scaffolding during first-encounter and practicing sessions without cluttering mastered or non-th sessions.

## Testable acceptance criteria (for Jessica)

- **AC1** — First-encounter session (`digraphs-th-voiceless: 'intro'` + node absent from `lifetimeFirstEncounters`): `[data-testid="th-intro-panel"]` is present in DOM immediately after WordSong mounts (before `audioReady` flips). `[data-testid="th-corner-cue"]` is also present.
- **AC2** — After `audioReady` flips (problem-area gate opens): `[data-testid="th-intro-panel"]` is absent from DOM. `[data-testid="th-corner-cue"]` remains present.
- **AC3** — Returning-user `practicing` session (`lifetimeFirstEncounters` includes `'digraphs-th-voiceless'`): `[data-testid="th-corner-cue"]` is present, `[data-testid="th-intro-panel"]` has count 0.
- **AC4** — Non-th session (`digraphs-th-voiceless: 'locked'`): both `[data-testid="th-intro-panel"]` and `[data-testid="th-corner-cue"]` have count 0 after audioReady flips.
- **AC5** — Mastered session (`digraphs-th-voiceless: 'mastered'`): both placements absent.
- **AC6** — Cue is inert to tapping wrong answers — no visual change to either placement on `poof` / `pose` change.
- **AC7** — Corner cue does not overflow the screen right edge on 1024×1366 iPad portrait.

## Screens / visual

Placement A mounts inside the `<div className="relative flex w-full items-start gap-4 px-4">` flex row between Emma and the caption ribbon. On first-encounter sessions, the row will show: Emma (h-[26vh]) | intro panel (~22vh sq) | ribbon (flex-1). The panel exits when the problem area appears.

Placement B is `position: absolute`, `top: calc(3.5rem + env(safe-area-inset-top))`, `right: 12pt` (class `right-3`), `width: 64pt`.

## Self-Test Report

Cannot verify against the Vercel preview URL at commit time — CI must complete and deploy first. This report section will be updated with AC walkthrough + side-effect inventory once the preview is available.

**Device note:** Testing will be on desktop headless (Playwright chromium + webkit via CI). iPad-Safari visual verification routes to Thomas per the standard UX-visible PR gate. bgclear cream-wash visual check: `emma-th-mouth.svg` was shipped in PR #235 as a hybrid base layer — no alpha channel issue expected since the file was approved, but Thomas should verify on the iPad preview that no cream-wash halo is visible around the mouth cue in both placements.

**Side-effect inventory (code-trace):**
- `Greet` mount: silent — `route !== 'literacy'`, no cue rendered. ✓ by code.
- `Hub` mount: silent — `route !== 'literacy'`, no cue rendered. ✓ by code.
- `Math` mount: silent — cue is in `WordSong.tsx` only. ✓ by code.
- `SessionEnd` mount: silent — cue props reset in teardown before route change. ✓ by code.
- `digraphs-sh` session: no cue — `digraphsThNodeLevel` will be `'mastered'` or `'locked'`, not `'intro'`/`'practicing'`. ✓ by code.
- `cvc-words` session: no cue — same. ✓ by code.

## Risk / rollback

Low risk: purely additive — new props default to `'locked'` / `false` so all existing tests and non-th sessions are unaffected. Rollback: revert this PR.

No mastery.ts / focusNode.ts / firstEncounterGate.ts / parentSettings.ts touched.

author: adsamcik
body:
## Summary

PR-2B finishes the deferred-async-inference hardening cluster surfaced by the followup-wave QA reports (`qa-deferred-e2e.md`, `qa-integration-seams.md`). Eight findings; FD leaks on both sides of the IPC boundary, the startup race, the silent oversized-result drop, replay/race in the completion-notice flow, and the missing test surface.

## Findings addressed

| ID | Summary | Files |
|---|---|---|
| **H-D1** | Service-side `inferDeferred()` FD leak — `writeEnd`, `readEnd`, media PFDs leaked on synchronous orchestrator failure | `app/src/main/kotlin/com/adsamcik/mindlayer/service/ServiceBinder.kt:1208-1390` |
| **H-D2** | SDK `chatDeferred()` FD leak — media source PFDs leaked on success and failure | `sdk/src/main/kotlin/com/adsamcik/mindlayer/sdk/Mindlayer.kt:720-768` |
| **H-D3** | Zero unit tests for the deferred surface | New: `DeferredStoreTest` (18), `FakeDeferredDao`, `MindlayerDeferredTest` (4) |
| **M-D1** | `fetch()` returns `NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_OWNED` for expired rows (loss of typed EXPIRED) | `DeferredStore.kt:117-147` |
| **M-D2** | Deferred preflight collapses `ContextOverflowException` / `SharedMemoryPoolExhaustedException` to `INTERNAL` | `ServiceBinder.kt:1265-1310` |
| **M-D3** | `deferredCompletions()` `replay = 0` + no service replay → docs example races | `Mindlayer.kt:159-170` + `ServiceBinder.kt:subscribeEvictionNotices` |
| **M-D4** | Oversized result self-evicts under per-uid byte quota → `READY` callback then `NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_OWNED` | `DeferredStore.kt:69-115`, `DeferredEntity` `truncated` column |
| **M-D5** | `failRunningOnInit()` dispatched on `serviceScope.launch` (not awaited before binder is exposed) | `MindlayerMlService.kt:179-188` |
| **M-D6** | Metrics roundtrip drops `Long/Float/Double/Boolean` (reader was `Int`-only) | `DeferredStore.kt:204-222` |
| **M-D7** | `awaitDeferred` busy-polls instead of subscribing to the completion flow | `Mindlayer.kt:awaitDeferred` |
| **M-D8** | Orphan `DEFERRED_EXPIRED` log event never emitted | `LogRepository.kt` + `ServiceBinder.kt:fetchDeferredResult` |

## AIDL impact

**NONE.** No surface changes. `DEFERRED_RESULT_TOO_LARGE` is an additive `MindlayerErrorCode` integer (5010), reserved for any future submit-time guard; the wire-stable contract is append-only.

## Behavior changes

- `DeferredStore.fetch` returns `EXPIRED` (was `NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_OWNED`) for the same-uid expired row.
- `DeferredStore.completeReady` truncates oversized text at 256 KiB (was: silent self-eviction under byte quota; client got `READY` callback then `NOT_FOUND_OR_NOT_OWNED` on fetch).
- `MindlayerMlService.onCreate` blocks on the `failRunningOnInit` SQL UPDATE before exposing the binder.
- Deferred synchronous preflight returns typed `INPUT_EXCEEDS_CONTEXT` / `TRANSIENT_RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (was `INTERNAL`).
- SDK `deferredCompletions()` has `replay = 1` (was `replay = 0`).
- Service-side `subscribeEvictionNotices` replays unfetched completions for the calling uid via `DeferredStore.completedPendingForUid` — clients reconnecting after a binder death catch missed notices.
- SDK `awaitDeferred` subscribes to the completion flow and uses the polling loop only as a fallback (was: ~240 binder round-trips per 60s wait).

## Test additions

- `app/src/test/kotlin/com/adsamcik/mindlayer/service/engine/DeferredStoreTest.kt` — 18 tests covering create/fetch/cancel/acknowledge/`failRunningOnInit`, M-D1 EXPIRED ordering, M-D4 truncation, M-D6 metrics roundtrip (`Int/Long/Float/Double/Boolean`), anti-enumeration cross-uid, byte-quota FIFO eviction.
- `app/src/test/kotlin/com/adsamcik/mindlayer/service/engine/FakeDeferredDao.kt` — in-memory DAO fake so unit tests don't depend on `sqlcipher` native loading.
- `sdk/src/test/kotlin/com/adsamcik/mindlayer/sdk/MindlayerDeferredTest.kt` — 4 tests (NOT_SUPPORTED gating, media requestId rebinding, FD cleanup on success + on `RemoteException`).

`ServiceBinderDeferredTest` is deferred to a follow-up — `ServiceBinder` doesn't currently accept a test-injectable dispatcher, so the H-D1 FD-cleanup assertion would race against an internal `scope.launch`. The H-D1 path is covered by SDK-side tests plus the typed-mapping paths in the existing `ServiceBinderTypedErrorsTest`.

## Summary

Implementace obsahového a datového balíku podle `CLAUDE_BRIEF_HSPA_DUSEK_2026-05-14.md`, který navazuje na tři prezentace prof. Duška ve Výboru pro zdravotnictví PS PČR (13. 5. 2026): plánované změny v dohodovacím řízení, predikce potřeb a podpora lůžkové péče, reforma intenzivní péče.

**První dávka tohoto PR** (tento commit): 7 nových HSPA indikátorů + 2 aktualizované drafty.

**Druhá dávka** (paralelně píší 2 sub-agenti, doplním dalším commitem do tohoto PR): 6 nových draftů — reforma IP, interna+stárnutí, SZD predikce na ORP, ošetřovatelská náročnost v CZ-DRG, personální evidence NRZP, INDIKO onkologie regiony.

### Nové indikátory (všechny `verification_status: review-pending`, seed-only)

| ID | Area · Domain | Hodnota 2024 | Zdroj k ověření |
|---|---|---|---|
| `obloznost_intenzivni_pece_pct` | Procesy · Intenzivní péče | 63 % | NZIP 2712 |
| `obloznost_interna_standard_pct` | Procesy · Kapacita | 66,1 % | NZIP 2714 (OIS-11-50) |
| `nevyuzite_osetrovaci_dny_ip` | Procesy · Intenzivní péče | 803 252 OD | NZIP 2712 + 2226 |
| `podil_senioru_na_internich_hospitalizacich` | Výstupy · Geriatrie | 72,2 % (2023) | NZIP 2713 |
| `osetrovaci_dny_na_uvazek_sestry` | Procesy · Pracovní síla | 406 OD/úvazek | NZIP 2714 |
| `podfinancovani_oblastni_interna_cm` | Struktury · Úhradová politika | −8 881 Kč/CM | OIS-11-05 + 2383 + 2385 |
| `preziti_1rok_po_upv_2d_pct` | Výsledky · Intenzivní péče | 51,2 % | NZIP 2708 |

Hodnoty jsou převzaty z prezentačních slidů — před produkční publikací nutná replikace z primárních NZIP datasetů.

### Aktualizované drafty (zůstávají `noindex`, mimo `data/articles.json`)

- **`clanek-dohodovaci-rizeni-2027-data.html`** — nová sekce „Pilot 2026–2027: šest principů" (MZ jako moderátor, vícelet. dohody, povinná část o vazbě úhrad na výsledek, zákaz deficitního plánování, limit rezerv ZP, smírčí panel + MZ koridor) + chronologie pilotu.
- **`clanek-drg-reforma-2026.html`** — evidence box „oblastní interna" (FN +2 254 Kč/CM, krajské +804 Kč/CM, oblastní **−8 881 Kč/CM**), modelovaná ztráta cca −1,6 mld. Kč jen na interním segmentu oblastních nemocnic, s metodickou poznámkou.

### Co se ZÁMĚRNĚ nepřidalo

- **Predikční indikátory 2030/2040/2050** (`geriatricti_pacienti_vysoke_riziko_75plus`, `pnp_iii_iv_75plus_predikce`) — porušilo by datový kontrakt `value`/`year`/`trend`. Budou publikovány jen jako tabulky v navazujících článcích (rozhodnutí potvrzeno uživatelem).
- **Krajská data v `regions.json`** — nemáme ověřené hodnoty pro 14 NUTS3 krajů.
- **Live ingest fetchery** — všechny nové indikátory jsou `origin: seed` do replikace z NZIP.

### Co je třeba ručně ověřit před publikací

1. Právní stav navrhované změny §17 (zda je to formální legislativní návrh, či pracovní materiál).
2. Definice ICU/IP lůžek v OECD vs. NRHZS (NRHZS IP zahrnuje 1.+2. úroveň, OECD ICU obvykle 2./3. — uvedeno v aktualizované kartě `luzka_jip_per_100k`).
3. Definice „přežití 1 rok po UPV >2 dny" — case-mix adjustment, věková stratifikace.
4. Zda lze `podfinancovani_oblastni_interna_cm` publikovat jako produkční HSPA score (modelační, politicky citlivé).
5. Zda jsou predikce ORP/SZD veřejná open data nebo projektový výstup ÚZIS.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run validate:data` → OK (80 indikátorů, +7 oproti hlavní větvi)
- [x] `npm test` → 252/252 pass (test `policy-views.test.js:197` aktualizován z 73 na 80)
- [x] `npm run validate:strategies` → OK
- [x] `npm run validate:prevention` → OK

author: mohsen1
body:
## Summary
- Preserve readonly assignment checks for nested property writes after an earlier write to the receiver.
- Reuse the checker's write-target receiver selection so readonly checks bypass polluted read-cache receiver types while still allowing narrowed receivers when needed.
- Add TS2540 coverage for readonly parent/interface, readonly parent/type alias, and mutable-parent/readonly-child shapes.

Fixes #7065

AgentName: M1-T8

## Project Corpus Impact

- Row: n/a (Track 8 readonly diagnostic-priority fix for #7065)
- Bug family: readonly assignment receiver diagnostics

## Structural rule
When assigning to a property access whose immediate receiver has already appeared in an assignment flow, tsc still checks the assigned property against the receiver's declared/write-target member surface; this change makes tsz do the same instead of using a flow-updated receiver that can erase nested readonly flags.

## Owner layer
This belongs in the checker readonly assignment gate: the solver still owns property resolution and readonly facts, while the checker chooses the assignment receiver context used for the TS2540 diagnostic decision.

## Adjacent cases
- `readonly a: { readonly b: number }`; after `obj.a = ...`, `obj.a.b = ...` reports TS2540 for both writes.
- Alias form with different names: `readonly outer: { readonly inner: number }` reports both parent and nested readonly writes.
- Mutable parent with readonly child: after a valid `obj.slot = ...`, `obj.slot.leaf = ...` still reports TS2540 for the child.

## Fallbacks / unsupported shapes
The helper delegates receiver selection to the existing property-access write-target path. If a member is only visible after narrowing, that path can still return the narrowed receiver; otherwise it preserves the declared/no-flow receiver surface for readonly detection.

## Verification
- `cargo fmt --check`
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-checker --test ts2540_readonly_tests test_nested_readonly_survives_prior_receiver_assignment`
- `cargo nextest run -p tsz-checker --test ts2540_readonly_tests`
- `cargo clippy -p tsz-checker --test ts2540_readonly_tests -- -D warnings`
- CLI repro emits TS2540 at both `df.a` and `df.a.b`

## Root cause

The Subresource Integrity example contained literal `</script>` strings inside JS backtick template literals. The HTML parser always treats `</script>` as closing the script block — even inside a string — so everything after line 4436 was rendered as visible text on the page.

## Fix

Escaped both occurrences as `<\/script>`. This is valid JS (backslash before `/` in a string is a no-op) and invisible to the HTML parser.

## Test plan
- [ ] Page loads with all category pills visible
- [ ] Secure Code → SRI example shows correct code
- [ ] No raw JS visible in page body

author: louistrue
body:
## Summary

Adds a new GLB export dialog (`GLBExportDialog`) to the viewer with support for selecting colour sources (rendering vs. shading), filtering by visibility state, and including metadata. Extends the geometry pipeline to track both rendering and shading colours separately, enabling the GLB exporter to offer both as export options.

## Key Changes

- **New GLB Export Dialog** (`GLBExportDialog.tsx`): Replaces the inline GLB export handler in `MainToolbar` with a dedicated dialog component featuring:
  - Model picker (single-model only, federated model support ready)
  - Colour source selector (Rendering vs. Shading)
  - Visible-only filter (respects hidden/isolated entity sets)
  - Metadata inclusion toggle
  - Export progress and result feedback

- **Colour Tracking in Geometry Pipeline**:
  - Extended `MeshData` and `MeshDataJs` to carry optional `shadingColor` alongside `color`
  - Modified Rust styling module to extract both `IfcSurfaceStyleRendering.DiffuseColour` (rendering) and `SurfaceColour` (shading) separately
  - New `GeometryStyleIndexes` struct returns both colour maps from a single pass
  - Shading colour only populated when it differs from rendering colour (sparse, common case is absent)

- **GLB Exporter Enhancements**:
  - Added `colorSource` option ('rendering' | 'shading') to `GLTFExportOptions`
  - Added `visibleOnly`, `hiddenEntityIds`, and `isolatedEntityIds` filtering options
  - Implemented mesh visibility filtering logic that respects isolation sets and hidden entities
  - Colour selection logic picks shading colour when available and requested, falls back to rendering colour

- **Visibility State Mapping**:
  - Dialog converts global visibility IDs to local express IDs per model using `idOffset`
  - Handles both legacy single-model and federated multi-model scenarios
  - Mirrors the approach used in `ExportDialog`

- **Tests**: Added comprehensive test coverage for visibility filtering, colour source selection, and fallback behaviour

## Implementation Details

- The shading colour is intentionally sparse — only stored when the file authored a distinct `DiffuseColour` that differs from `SurfaceColour`, reducing memory overhead
- The dialog defaults to the first available model and auto-selects it when the menu opens
- Model names are truncated to 24 characters in the dropdown with full name in tooltip
- Export filename includes `_visible` suffix when visibility filtering is active
- Rust processing crate tracks shading colour but doesn't propagate it server-side (no GLB consumer in server pipeline yet)

body:
## Description

The YAML front matter in `dev-docs/bidders/defineMedia.md` used a **hard tab** character to indent the `redirect_from` list item. YAML does not allow tabs as indentation tokens, so Jekyll throws a parse error and skips the file entirely:

```
YAML Exception reading .../defineMedia.md: found character that cannot start any token while scanning for the next token at line 7 column 1
```

As a result, the **Define Media adapter is not rendered on the Download page** at https://docs.prebid.org/download.html.

## Fix

Replace the tab with two spaces on line 7 of the front matter.

## Testing

Local Jekyll build (`bundle exec jekyll build`) with this fix applied no longer emits the YAML exception, and the adapter checkbox appears correctly in the generated `_site/download.html`.

author: oshovibe
body:
## Summary

Refactor majeur du système d'armes : **1 SEULE arme à la fois**, choisie par le joueur au spawn via `WeaponPickup`. Avant : 2 armes simultanées (RT pistol, LT melee). Maintenant : RT pilote l'arme équipée. Pas d'arme = pas de tir.

## Architecture

**`PlayerController`** :
- `_weapon_hitscan` (Pistolet) + `_weapon_melee` (Épée) restent dans `player.tscn`, **désactivés** au `_ready` (visible=false, process=off)
- Nouvelle var `_equipped_weapon: StringName` (`""` / `"pistol"` / `"melee"`)
- `equip_weapon_kind(kind)` : active visuellement + processus de l'arme correspondante, désactive l'autre. Émet `weapon_equipped(kind)`.
- `_update_shooting` : RT pilote l'arme équipée (pistol = auto-fire hold, melee = swing par appui)
- LT n'est plus utilisé — RT fait tout
- Nouveaux getters : `get_melee()`, `get_equipped_weapon_kind()`

**`WeaponPickup`** (`scripts/core/weapon_pickup.gd`) :
- extends Interactable, hold 0.5s

author: amon3939-sketch
body:
## Summary
The GitHub Pages deploy of M3a renders as a blank dark screen. The bundled module evaluation throws:

\`\`\`
TypeError: Failed to construct 'URL': Invalid URL
\`\`\`

## Root cause
The deploy workflow passes \`VITE_SERVER_URL: \${{ secrets.SERVER_URL_PRODUCTION }}\` and that secret isn't set in the repo, so Vite inlined the literal **empty string**. The previous fallback used \`??\`, which only catches null/undefined — the empty string sailed straight through into \`new Client('')\`, and colyseus.js then threw inside its URL parser at module load. With the top-level throw the whole React tree never mounted.

## Fix
- Fallback uses \`||\` plus a \`trim()\` guard, so any empty/whitespace value falls back to \`ws://localhost:2567\`.
- The Colyseus \`Client\` instance is now built lazily behind a Proxy. If a custom deploy ever sets a malformed override, the throw is deferred to the moment a lobby/match scene actually tries to connect — Title and Solo keep working.

## Test plan
- [ ] After this lands, https://amon3939-sketch.github.io/chaindrop1/ renders the title scene
- [ ] ソロプレイ button still works
- [ ] オンライン button shows lobby (will then fail to connect because the prod server isn't running, but that's expected and surfaces as the lobby's "サーバに接続できませんでした" inline error, not a blank page)

author: minoseigenheer
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes several issues with CAN bus connection handling and settings persistence across sessions, targeting the QT6WIP branch.

## Changes

### Fix `saveConnections()` array length mismatch ([172f346](https://github.com/minoseigenheer/SavvyCAN/commit/172f3468ca16af94130079ce967894b49933200b))
When a device was disconnected, the saved connections array could end up with the wrong length, causing settings from subsequent devices to be lost or mismatched on reload.

### Restore all SerialBus settings across sessions ([e9ab909](https://github.com/minoseigenheer/SavvyCAN/commit/e9ab9096b87725356683bfd47202c0e9637f004b))
Previously, only the bus speed was restored. Now `listenOnly`, `active`, `canFD`, and `dataRate` are all saved to `QSettings` and passed to the `SerialBusConnection` constructor, so the full configuration survives an application restart.

### Fix PCAN connection status and auto-apply last SerialBus speed ([a74c1ac](https://github.com/minoseigenheer/SavvyCAN/commit/a74c1ac2c9d74b28c6931595218f112822ff661f))
- The connection status indicator was not updating correctly for PCAN/PeakCAN devices. A `deviceStateChanged` slot is now connected to `QCanBusDevice::stateChanged` so the UI reflects the real device state immediately.
- The last configured bus speed is now automatically applied when the connection window opens, removing the need to manually re-select the speed each session.

### Fix connection settings save/restore for all device interfaces ([c02b9df](https://github.com/minoseigenheer/SavvyCAN/commit/c02b9df1674a13840e5a2134d121e9040b703b84))
Rewrites the save/restore logic in `ConnectionWindow` so that every configured interface (not just the first) is correctly persisted and restored, including port name, driver, speed, and FD settings.

### Fix connection issues for slow-initialising SerialBus plugins ([502f84e](https://github.com/minoseigenheer/SavvyCAN/commit/502f84eb9c044303feb8a4b1a257f8f979a2cefb))
Some SerialBus backends (e.g. the rusoku2/TouCAN plugin) take time to become ready after `connectDevice()` is called. The timer-based `testConnection()` now skips polling while the device is in `ConnectingState` or `ClosingState`, preventing premature reconnect attempts that would race with the backend's own initialisation.

## Files changed
- `connections/connectionwindow.cpp/.h`
- `connections/serialbusconnection.cpp/.h`
- `connections/canconnection.cpp/.h`
- `connections/canconfactory.cpp/.h`
- `connections/canconnectionmodel.cpp`

## Summary

- Extracts a `closeBidi` helper that signals end-of-send and drains the response side, avoiding the HTTP/2 reset path that races inside `net/http`

This reverts ``fce393e8da`` (PR #92).

PR #92 restored PR #86's pattern: synchronous ``TriggerRoundEndTgsEvent``, ``addtimer``-driven ``reboot_callback``, and ``SetRoundEnd`` preamble at every admin restart entry point. Verification confirmed every step ran exactly as designed (the ``REBOOT_AUDIT:`` lines fired in order across the entire chain), but the actual client behaviour did not improve. Round-19 had zero ``ACCESS:`` lines after a Regular Restart on round-18, same broken auto-reconnect as before.

The AUDIT data also disproves PR #86's root-cause hypothesis: ``world.OpenPort(new_port)`` is NOT the single mechanism that triggers the BYOND fade-to-title signal. The user observed the BYOND reconnect dialog appear (black screen + "Please wait while you automatically reconnect") even though the TGS Bridge REBOOT response contained no ``newPort`` and ``world.OpenPort`` was never called. The fade fires from BYOND's native ``..()`` directly. The bug is downstream of that. The auto-reconnect attempts themselves fail to land.

Continuing to iterate on roundend / shutdown timing has introduced a recurring class of regressions (PRs #82, #84, #86, #92 all touched it). Reverting to the simpler post-PR #87 state where no roundend timing is changed and exploring fixes that do NOT touch SSticker.Reboot scheduling or TGS event ordering.

## Why It's Good For The Game

PR #92 added complexity (addtimer staging, sync event handling, AUDIT instrumentation) for no observable benefit to the user-facing bug. Removing it puts the codebase back at the minimal post-#81 / post-#87 state so the next fix attempt starts from a clean baseline. The AUDIT logging can be re-introduced later as a standalone PR if needed.

author: emkey1
body:
**Severity:** MEDIUM
**Vulnerability:** The utility functions in `tools/ptutil.c` and `tools/vdso-transplant.c` used unbounded `sprintf` calls to format process-specific paths (`/proc/%d/mem` and `/proc/%d/maps`) into statically sized stack buffers.
**Impact:** If an unexpected or abnormally large process ID representation were processed, it could overflow the stack buffers, potentially leading to a denial of service or stack corruption in the tool execution context.
**Fix:** Replaced `sprintf` with `snprintf(..., sizeof(buffer), ...)` in `tools/ptutil.c` and `tools/vdso-transplant.c` to strictly enforce memory boundaries during path formatting.
**Verification:** Reviewed code to verify bounds enforcement and ran the end-to-end test suite (`./tests/e2e/e2e.bash`) to ensure functionality remains correct.

author: krilliac
body:
The serial-input pump fed bytes straight into ShellFeedChar / ShellSubmit with no LoginIsActive() check. The login gate is enforced at the input-routing layer (the shell has no auth check of its own), and only the PS/2 kbd-reader replicated it — so a host on COM1 (-serial stdio, a real UART, a BMC serial-over-LAN console) got a fully interactive kernel shell with the GUI/TTY
login screen still up. Verified live: pre-auth `whoami` ->
"(no session)", then `su admin admin` (the default creds the login screen itself advertises) -> full admin session + a backdoor admin account, never having passed the gate.

HandleByte now mirrors the PS/2 gate: while LoginIsActive() every inbound byte is cooked into a key code and routed to LoginFeedKey under the compositor lock, never to the shell. Re-verified live: the attack input is consumed by the login form (LOGIN FAILED), no shell command executes, and a legitimate admin/admin login over the now-gated serial line still works end-to-end.

Documents the input-path gate invariant in
wiki/security/Auth-and-Login.md so future input feeders replicate it.

`renderGateLoading` / `renderGateSignIn` in #84 referenced `NLPLUS_LOGO_URL`, but the constant was **never defined in the file**. (It only ever lived on a sibling branch that didn't make it to main.) var NLPLUS_LOGO_URL = 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/thenationalleague/tools/main/assets/logos/NL%2B%20red%20lozenge.png';

Azure Static Web Apps reads routing config from the build output folder (`dist/`). The `staticwebapp.config.json` was only at the repo root — Vite never copied it to `dist/`, so Azure ignored the routing rules entirely.

author: envestcc
body:
## Summary

- **Fix**: `handleCandidateDeactivate` / `handleScheduleCandidateDeactivation` built their receipt log via a struct literal that set both `r.topics` and `r.data`. `receiptLog.Build`'s postFairbankMigration single-log path only copies `r.topics` onto the emitted `action.Log`, silently dropping `r.data`. Since `CandidateDeactivationScheduled` declares `blockNumber` as non-indexed in the ABI, the encoded value needs to land in `Data` — without this fix, frontends saw the event fire but could not read the scheduled exit height. Both handlers now route through `AddEvent`, matching the pattern `handleCandidateRegister` already uses. Adds an e2e sub-test that verifies all three v2.4 events (Requested / Scheduled / Deactivated).
- **Refactor**: Split `newReceiptLog` into `newReceiptLog` (events-only, for new code) and `newReceiptLogLegacy` (pre-events shape). The single constructor served two emission shapes whose distinction was invisible at the call site — reviewers had no signal which path a handler was on, which is exactly how the bug above slipped in. Doc comments warn against mixing `AddEvent` with legacy `AddTopics` / `SetData`. All 13 production callers + 2 test callers move to `newReceiptLogLegacy`; the deactivate handlers use the new `newReceiptLog`. No behavior change.

## Test plan

- [ ] `make test-unit` passes
- [ ] e2e sub-test in `exit_queue_test.go` verifies Requested / Scheduled / Deactivated events all carry readable `blockNumber` data
- [ ] Manual: trigger `CandidateDeactivate` via Web3 and confirm the `CandidateDeactivationScheduled` log decodes `blockNumber` correctly

body:
## Summary

Hybrid pivot landing roadmap final aggregator. Adds the **weighted-average** function to the SqlBuilder + ReportController + ColumnDefinition + schema chain.

**Codex thread `019e2acc` iter-2 absorb**: builder-level projection of `weightField` so multi-schema UNION ALL and percentile-wrapper paths emit valid SQL.

## SQL contract

```sql
SUM([value] * [weight]) /
NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN [value] IS NOT NULL AND [weight] IS NOT NULL THEN [weight] END), 0)
```

- Rows with a null value OR null weight fall out of **both** numerator and denominator (mirrors MSSQL `AVG`'s null-exclusion semantic).
- `NULLIF` on the denominator prevents divide-by-zero — an all-null bucket resolves to `NULL` instead of erroring.
- Weight column reference is rendered as a bracketed identifier (validated upstream).

## Validation chain (controller → SqlBuilder)

### Controller (`sanitizeAggParams` + `sanitizeAggregations`)
- Mandatory `weightField` string, non-blank, distinct from value field.
- Registry `defaultAggParams.weightField` fallback when request omits aggParams.
- Value field type=number; weight field visible + type=number; weight ≠ value.

### SqlBuilder (`buildGroupedQuery` projection loop, iter-2)
- Pulls `weightField` from `agg.params()`.
- Validates `weightField` is in the visibility allow-list (defence-in-depth for controller-bypass paths).
- Validates `weightField != valueField`.
- **Adds `weightField` to the `projected` set** so the FROM clause (single-schema, multi-schema UNION ALL, AND the percentile-wrapper inner `_med` SELECT) carries it through.

### SqlBuilder (`renderAggExpression`)
- New `weightedavg` case + `weightFieldOf` helper that fails closed on missing param.

### Registry + Schema
- `ColumnDefinition` defaultAggFunc whitelist + defaultAggParams.weightField.
- `report-definition.schema.json` enum + properties extended.

## Pivot composition (deferred)

PR-0.4c is the **flat path only**. Controller rejects weightedavg inside a pivot query with `INVALID_AGGREGATION_REQUEST`. Pivot composition tracked as PR-0.4h follow-up — separate per-bucket numerator + denominator + alias metadata + budget math + MSSQL IT.

## Test plan

- [x] `SqlBuilderTest.WeightedAverageAggregation` — **7 PASS** (3 iter-1 + 4 iter-2: builder projection check, multi-schema UNION ALL, weight-not-visible reject, weight=value reject)
- [x] `ReportControllerQueryTest.WeightedAverageValidation` — 5 PASS
- [x] `SqlBuilderMssqlIntegrationTest` — 2 new MSSQL Testcontainers IT
- [x] Full backend suite: **745/745 PASS**, zero regression
- [x] Codex thread `019e2acc` iter-2 AGREE (`ready_for_merge: true`)

## Follow-up

PR-0.4h: extend `buildPivotedGroupedQuery` with weighted-average wrapped-subquery support (per-bucket ratio + alias metadata).

- Cache starts3/starts2 in MarkovGenerator to eliminate repeated full-table scans (was up to 80 per reply, causing multi-second delays)
- Increase GENERATION_ATTEMPTS_WITH_CONTEXT from 2 to 5 so context is actually used across the majority of generation attempts
- Fix 1-token reply handling: move bot_is_mentioned() before the length/token early-return so short messages addressed to the bot (e.g. "ок", "?") are still answered
- Use current message as context when bot is mentioned directly without a reply (only_for_replies was silently dropping context in this case)
- Add trim_to_sentence_boundary() post-processing so responses end at a natural sentence boundary (.!?) rather than mid-phrase
- Replace full generated-list recent_tokens with a 10-token sliding window: fixes O(n) repeat-penalty scan and stops penalising distant words
- Replace step-function context_decay with smooth 0.92^step exponential
- Relax is_context_heavy_reply thresholds (0.85→0.92, run 4→5) to stop rejecting legitimate context-relevant responses
- Suppress jump_count==0 filter when context_tokens is present
- Make matches_training_prefix deterministic (drop random prefix length)
- Use extract_best_seed() to skip trailing punctuation when building seed

author: zeveck
body:
## Summary

Closes #266. Adds **Step 6b — Auto-rebase BEHIND PRs post-CI-green** to `/land-pr`, between Step 6 (CI monitor) and Step 7 (merge). Detects the `MERGE_REQUESTED=true PR_STATE=OPEN CI=pass mergeStateStatus=BEHIND` case that GitHub's auto-merge doesn't auto-recover from in repos with strict branch-protection, and runs a bounded auto-rebase-and-repush loop until either (a) the PR becomes mergeable, (b) a terminal failure surfaces with a discriminator REASON token, or (c) the retry cap (3 iterations) is exhausted.

Extends #254's spirit — close the operational gap between "auto-merge requested" and "actually merged."

## Concrete motivation

Bit twice in the 2026-05-14 morning sprint:
- **PR #260** went BEHIND after PR #259 landed during its monitor window. Manual recovery: `git rebase origin/main && git push --force-with-lease`. CI re-ran, auto-merge fired, merged.
- **PR #261** went BEHIND TWICE: first after #259, then again after #260 (which had been rebased+pushed and was actively auto-merging). Two manual rebase+force-push cycles.

Without Step 6b, the pattern repeats every time sibling PRs land mid-flight.

## The fix

`skills/land-pr/SKILL.md:372-551` — new Step 6b. Loop structure:

1. **Skip conditions** (any → skip the whole step): `STATUS` already set to a failure terminus, `AUTO_FLAG != true`, `CI_STATUS != pass`, `PR_NUMBER` empty.
2. **Per-iteration** (max 3):
   - `git -C $WORKTREE_PATH fetch origin $BASE_BRANCH`
   - `git -C $WORKTREE_PATH rebase origin/$BASE_BRANCH` (abort on conflicts → `STATUS=auto-rebase-conflict`, write `CONFLICT_FILES_LIST` sidecar, break)
   - `git -C $WORKTREE_PATH push --force-with-lease origin $BRANCH` (failure → retry, final retry → `STATUS=auto-rebase-blocked REASON=auto-rebase-push-failed-rcN`)
   - Re-poll CI via `pr-monitor.sh` (CI re-runs on rebased commit)
   - Re-check `gh pr view --json mergeStateStatus`
3. **Break conditions:**
   - `mergeStateStatus ∈ {CLEAN, HAS_HOOKS, UNSTABLE}` → success, fall through to Step 7
   - `mergeStateStatus ∈ {BLOCKED, CONFLICTING}` → `STATUS=auto-rebase-blocked REASON=mergeStateStatus-<X>`
   - `UNKNOWN` → `STATUS=auto-rebase-blocked REASON=auto-rebase-unknown`
   - `CI_STATUS=fail` post-rebase → `STATUS=auto-rebase-blocked REASON=auto-rebase-ci-fail`
4. **Exhaustion** (3 iterations still BEHIND): `STATUS=behind-thrash REASON=auto-rebase-exhausted`.

## Step 7 / Step 8 integration

- **Step 7 merge gate** extended to skip when `STATUS ∈ {behind-thrash, auto-rebase-conflict, auto-rebase-blocked}` — `pr-merge.sh` not called once the auto-rebase loop terminates non-successfully.
- **Step 8 status mapping table** extended: `auto-rebase-conflict → conflict`; `behind-thrash → pr-ready` (PR exists, reviewable); `auto-rebase-blocked → pr-ready`.
- **Result-file schema** extended with new `STATUS` and `REASON` tokens documented in the schema enum.
- All stderr captured to sidecar `/tmp/land-pr-auto-rebase-stderr-$BRANCH_SLUG-$$.log`, referenced via new `REBASE_STDERR_FILE` schema field on failure paths.

## What else changed

- `.claude/skills/land-pr/SKILL.md` mirror regenerated.
- `metadata.version`: `2026.05.13+8867dc` → `2026.05.15+75fc8e`.
- **New `tests/test-land-pr-auto-rebase-behind.sh`** (462 lines, 32 cases). Hybrid pattern:
  - Layer 1: 21 sentinel-grep assertions on `skills/land-pr/SKILL.md` prose covering all new behaviors (Step 6b heading, AUTO_REBASE_MAX=3, all mergeStateStatus tokens, force-push-with-lease, all new STATUS/REASON tokens, schema enumerations, mapping-table rows, Step 7 skip gates).
  - Layer 2: 11 mock-queue-driven case assertions exercising the loop logic — BEHIND→CLEAN success, BEHIND×3 exhaustion (behind-thrash), AUTO_FLAG=false skip, CI=fail skip, rebase-conflict + CONFLICT_FILES_LIST sidecar, BLOCKED post-rebase, UNKNOWN post-rebase, initial-CLEAN no-op, PR_NUMBER empty skip, STATUS-preset skip.
- Registered in `tests/run-all.sh`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash tests/run-all.sh` → **3072/3072 PASS** (3039 baseline post-FIX_ISSUES_SYNC_HARDENING + 32 new + 1 from rebase).
- [x] `bash tests/test-land-pr-auto-rebase-behind.sh` standalone → 32/32 PASS.
- [x] `diff -rq skills/land-pr .claude/skills/land-pr` → no differences (mirror clean).
- [x] Verifier subagent APPROVE with anchored file:line evidence for every AC.

body:
## Why I'm doing:

Hive views from external Hive catalogs are represented as `ConnectorView`. When such a view is queried with Ranger row filter or masking policies, the analyzer converts the original `TableRelation` into a `ViewRelation` but did not preserve the `needRewrittenByPolicy` flag. As a result, the security policy rewrite guard skipped the view and the Ranger policies configured on the Hive view were not applied.

The same missing propagation also meant relations inside the expanded Hive view definition did not inherit the rewrite marker, so policies on base tables could be skipped when accessed through the Hive view path.

## What I'm doing:

Reuse the policy rewrite flag propagation used by native StarRocks views for `ConnectorView`:

- preserve `needRewrittenByPolicy` on the created `ViewRelation` only when the outer relation was already marked for policy rewrite
- mark relations inside the expanded view query so table policies inside Hive view definitions can still be rewritten
- add Hive view unit tests covering both a policy on the Hive view itself and a policy on the base table referenced by the Hive view

## Summary

The two `creditCardValidator` definitions in the wallets module had drifted from the `creditCards` schema (`packages/backend/convex/schema.ts:110`). Convex's strict `returns` validation rejected any row with a populated drift field, breaking the **Add Cards** slideout on `/credit-cards?wallet=<id>`:

```
ReturnsValidationError: Object contains extra field `statementClosingDay` (then `userOverrides`) that is not in the validator.
```

## Changes

Aligned both wallet validators with the canonical `creditCards/queries.ts` `list`/`get` shapes by adding the five missing schema fields:

- `statementClosingDay`
- `payOverTimeEnabled`, `payOverTimeLimit`, `payOverTimeApr`
- `userOverrides` (full subobject: `officialName`, `accountName`, `company`, `aprs[]`, `providerDashboardUrl`)

Files:
- `packages/backend/convex/wallets/cardQueries.ts` — `creditCardValidator` (used by `listByWallet` + `listNotInWallet`)
- `packages/backend/convex/wallets/queries.ts` — `creditCardValidator` (used by `getWithCards`)

The two validators now match `creditCards/queries.ts` field-for-field.

## Test plan

- [x] `bunx convex dev --once` deploys to `dev:canny-turtle-982` cleanly
- [x] `cd apps/app && bun typecheck` clean
- [x] Vercel preview built ✅ (smartpockets-app + smartpockets-web)
- [x] CodeRabbit ✅
- [x] Manual smoke test on `app.preview.smartpockets.com`: `/credit-cards?wallet=<id>` → **Add Cards** populates without `ReturnsValidationError` (the Chase Slate Edge row, which has both `statementClosingDay` and `userOverrides.providerDashboardUrl` set, now renders cleanly)

The 4 playwright failures (`wallets-baseline.spec.ts:203,233`, `wallets-variant-champagne-leather.spec.ts:158,249`) are pre-existing on PR #263 and unrelated to this Convex change — they exercise the wallets dropdown UI which this PR doesn't touch.

author: sturdystablestalwart
body:
## Why (#114)
Cold-loads of `/test/:id` by an authenticated user race against AuthContext's `/api/auth/me` fetch. If `user` is null at mount, the session-start POST in the test-fetch effect (deps `[id]`) never runs and never re-runs. The user takes the whole test with no autosave or resume.

## What
Separated session-start into its own one-shot effect gated on `user && !sessionId && !isSubmitted`. The test-fetch effect is unchanged; the session POST fires the moment `user` populates.

## Verification
- New RTL test `TestTaker-session.test.jsx` exercises the null->populated transition.
- Full client vitest suite green; lint green; build green.

Fixes #114

author: kamathgurudatt
body:
### Motivation
- Allow lightweight internal devices to operate without requiring interactive auth while keeping production behavior secure and observable.
- Prevent bcrypt failures for passwords longer than 72 bytes and normalize inputs across hashing and verification.
- Improve runtime resiliency and observability by surfacing clearer HTTP errors, graceful dependency probing, and safer exception responses.
- Add client-side conveniences for developer/internal device flows and introduce simple analytics UI and docs for the prototype.

### Description
- Add optional internal anonymous device auth in `get_current_user` that creates or returns an internal device `User` when `allow_internal_device_anonymous_auth` is enabled in `Settings` and no token is provided, and add related settings to `app.core.config.Settings` with validators for `secret_key`, `database_url`, and `redis_url`.
- Harden password handling in `app.core.security` by truncating/normalizing to bcrypt's 72-byte limit via `normalize_password_for_bcrypt`, adding safe hashing/verification fallbacks, and expose `normalize_password_for_bcrypt` to callers.
- Constrain password DTOs to 72 bytes and validate byte-length in `schemas.dto` for `UserCreate` and `LoginRequest` to avoid oversized bcrypt input errors.
- Update auth routes to handle long-password normalization during signup/login fallback and to handle invalid password encoding cases.
- Improve dependency and DB error handling by returning `HTTPException` from `get_db` when the session factory is unavailable and adding a dependency probe loop and optional bootstrap table creation in `main.lifespan` via `Base.metadata.create_all`.
- Replace global HTTPS redirect middleware with a conditional per-request middleware that respects `X-Forwarded-Proto` and excludes health checks, and add an HTTP exception handler plus richer unhandled exception responses that include an `error_id` and optionally internal details based on `Settings`.
- Add more defensive debug route handling with specific `HTTPException` translations for provider/runtime failures.
- Tweak Celery configuration to set `broker_connection_retry_on_startup` and use `worker_pool = "solo"` for simpler worker startup.
- Mobile app changes: add an internal-device mode that auto-signs in using embedded credentials, validate API base URL more strictly in `ApiClient`, add analytics endpoints and UI (`analytics_screen`), enforce password byte-length validation in the auth screen, and add network/security config plus manifest updates for cleartext in dev flows.
- Add a project specification document `docs/PROJECT_SPEC_PROTOTYPE.md` describing goals, API design, and data model additions.

### Testing
- No automated tests were executed as part of this change.

author: copilot
body:
Multiple Jackson 2.x versions (2.21.0–2.21.3) were appearing in the classpath due to transitive dependencies, with no force resolution to consolidate them. Additionally, the pinned Jackson version conflicted with the version bundled by the fabric8 Kubernetes client.

## Changes

- **`gradle.properties`**: Bump `jacksonVersion` `2.21.2` → `2.21.3`
- **`build.gradle`**: Activate force declarations for all three core Jackson modules in `allprojects.resolutionStrategy`:
  ```groovy
  force "com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-annotations:$jacksonVersion"
  force "com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core:$jacksonVersion"
  force "com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-databind:$jacksonVersion"
  ```
  The `jackson-annotations` and `jackson-core` entries were already present but commented out; `jackson-databind` is newly added.
- **`build.gradle`**: Upgrade `io.fabric8:kubernetes-client` `7.6.1` → `7.7.0`. Version 7.6.1 bundles Jackson `2.20.0`, which conflicted with the forced `2.21.3`. Version 7.7.0 was updated to use Jackson `2.21.3`, eliminating the mismatch.

> **Note on Jackson 3.x:** Jackson 3.x uses a new group ID (`tools.jackson`) vs `com.fasterxml.jackson`. Migrating would require source-level changes across the codebase and is out of scope here.

author: codefire98
body:
## Summary

Three small UX wins on the post-plan / calendar surfaces, bundled into one PR.

### 1. Post plan: auto-fill title from first saved copy
When an admin saves the **first** piece of copy on a still-untitled post plan, the `concept` field is now populated automatically from a derived one-line title — so the calendar and lists stop showing "Untitled post" as soon as there's real content.

- Pure client-side string transform (no AI call): first non-empty line → strip leading emoji/punctuation → prefer first complete short sentence → truncate at word boundary to **50 chars** with `…`.
- Fires **exactly once per plan** — guarded by `!plan.concept` AND zero saved copy across platforms, so a cleared title can't re-fire on the next copy save.
- Dismissible sparkles callout with **Undo** surfaces what happened.
- Pure-emoji and whitespace-only first lines correctly fall through without setting a title.
- Lives entirely in `web/src/components/PostPlanDetailView.jsx`.

### 2. Calendar: drag post chips to reschedule (date-only)
Month + Week views now accept HTML5 drag of a post chip onto a different day cell.

- Only the **date** portion of `scheduled_at` changes; time-of-day is preserved (e.g. a 9am post stays 9am).
- Same-day drops are no-ops.
- **Posted plans are non-draggable** — the post is already live.
- Brand (non-admin) users see no drag affordance at all.
- Source chip dims to 40% opacity with a `grabbing` cursor; hover cell gets a dashed accent outline.
- Optimistic write — the chip jumps to the new cell immediately, then `updatePostPlan` runs in the background. On failure the move is reverted and the error is alerted.
- Custom MIME `application/x-lr-plan-id` gates the drop handler so OS file drags / foreign image drags can't accidentally trip a reschedule.

### 3. Shorter post-plan headlines (5-10 words)
Both auto-generation paths for the `concept` field now target a short HEADLINE instead of full sentences.

- **AI Co-pilot** (`create_post_plan_draft` tool): zod field description rewritten from *"Short (1-2 sentence) concept"* to *"Very short HEADLINE — TARGET 5-10 words, single phrase, NOT a full sentence"* with concrete good/bad examples. Added `.min(3).max(80)` so model overshoots trigger zod-validation failure → the SDK's existing `experimental_repairToolCall` flow re-prompts with the validation error attached.
- **Auto-title** (feature #1 above): `AUTO_TITLE_MAX_LEN` dropped from 60 → 50 chars (~5-10 words in English). Verified across the existing test set — all sample inputs now land in the 5-10 word target band.

## Caveats — please read before merging

1. **No live UI verification.** I couldn't reach the auth-gated views in this terminal, so the actual drag-and-drop interaction and the auto-title callout were not clicked through end-to-end in a real browser. Verification covered: production builds passing post-rebase; helper logic (derivation + `rescheduleToDate`) exercised in a real browser via preview_eval; sample inputs all landing in the 5-10 word band after the cap change. Worth a manual smoke pass.
2. **No new env vars, secrets, migrations, or deps.** Pure client-side + a zod tweak on an existing Vercel route.

## Test plan

- [ ] **Auto-title:** Open any post plan whose concept is empty and whose copy is empty across all platforms. Type a caption (e.g. an Instagram body) into one platform's copy field, save. Confirm the title fills with the opening of that caption AND the sparkles callout appears below the title. Click **Undo** — title goes back to empty and the callout disappears. Reload the plan; title remains empty (auto-fill does not re-fire because the user-explicit "no title" decision is preserved by the `!plan.concept` guard). Add new copy; confirm it does NOT re-fire (concept stayed empty but copy now exists, so the second-half of the gate trips).
- [ ] **Auto-title length:** Sanity-check a few real-world captions and confirm the resulting title looks like 5-10 words (e.g. "Three reasons we ditched cold-call lists", "Spring just arrived in the studio — and so did…"). The previous version landed up to 12 words.
- [ ] **Drag — month view:** As agency, drag a non-posted post chip from one day to another. The chip should dim while dragging; the target cell should show a dashed outline. Drop — the chip should jump to the new day immediately and the time of day on the chip (and inside the detail view) should be unchanged.
- [ ] **Drag — week view:** Same drill on the Week tab. Confirm the column gets the dashed outline + tinted background when hovered.
- [ ] **Drag — same-day no-op:** Drag a chip and drop it back on its own day. Confirm nothing happens (no flicker, no API call, no visual jolt).
- [ ] **Drag — posted plans:** Find a post plan with at least one live publication (displayStatus = "posted"). Confirm the chip cannot be dragged (cursor stays as pointer; no drag affordance).
- [ ] **Drag — brand view:** Switch into brand role for any account. Confirm chips have no drag affordance at all and the drop targets don't highlight.
- [ ] **Shorter Co-pilot headlines:** Ask the AI Co-pilot in CopilotPanel to "draft a post for Bamboo Bear about the new Spring linen drop, schedule for next Tuesday". The created post plan's headline in the calendar chip should now be ~5-10 words (something like "Spring linen drop teaser") instead of a full sentence. If the model overshoots, the existing tool-repair flow should silently retry; nothing red should surface.

Automated remediation for trivy finding: serve-static: Improper Sanitization in serve-static (CVE-2024-43800)

- Updated serve-static dependency from 1.13.2 to 1.16.0+
- Added serve-static as an explicit dependency to ensure the patched version is installed

serve-static versions prior to 1.16.0 have an improper input sanitization vulnerability in the redirect() function that could allow code execution. This fix upgrades to version 1.16.0 or later, which patches CVE-2024-43800.

- **Risk:** Minimal - this is a minor version bump that maintains backward compatibility
- **Changes:** No code changes required - pure dependency update

body:
This pull request updates the main animation loop in `main.py` to fully implement the Knight Rider LED effect. The key changes ensure that the LEDs light up in sequence, reverse direction at the ends, and only one LED is on at a time.

**Knight Rider animation logic improvements:**

* Called `all_off()` at the start of each loop iteration to turn off all LEDs before lighting the next one.
* Turned on the LED at the current `pos` index with `leds[pos].on()`.
* Moved the LED position by updating `pos` using the current `direction`.
* Added logic to reverse `direction` and correct `pos` when the position goes out of bounds (less than 0 or greater than or equal to the number of LEDs).

## Summary

Manual publication of artifacts from [SciMLBenchmarks.jl run 25374549824](https://github.com/SciML/SciMLBenchmarks.jl/actions/runs/25374549824), which was triggered by the OrdinaryDiffEq v7 / SciMLBase v3 / RecursiveArrayTools v4 stack merge ([SciML/SciMLBenchmarks.jl#1551](https://github.com/SciML/SciMLBenchmarks.jl/pull/1551), merged 2026-05-05).

Only 5 of 38 folders' artifacts are included:
- `benchmarks/AdaptiveSDE`
- `benchmarks/NonStiffSDE`
- `benchmarks/Optimization`
- `benchmarks/StiffDDE`
- `benchmarks/Symbolics`

The remaining 33 folders either failed the build (4: NonStiffODE, ModelingToolkit, MethodOfLinesPDE, DAE), were cancelled after a 24h queue wait (28), or were still running when the run was halted.

## Why this is a manual PR

The auto-publish job in [`.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml`](https://github.com/SciML/SciMLBenchmarks.jl/blob/master/.github/workflows/benchmarks.yml) is gated on `needs.benchmark.result == 'success'` — i.e. ALL matrix jobs must succeed. With ~30 failed/cancelled jobs, the gate never opened, so the 5 successful folders' artifacts (otherwise expiring 2026-06-09) sat unpublished.

Follow-up PRs in flight on SciMLBenchmarks.jl:
1. Relax the publish gate so partial successes still publish.
2. Re-trigger the failed/cancelled folders in small batches.

## Note for review

Please ignore this PR until reviewed by @ChrisRackauckas.

body:
Fixes #6133

Structural rule: when a `typeof` type query carries instantiation type arguments, `tsc` first resolves the value or property-chain target, then applies the type arguments to every applicable call/construct signature on that target, including signature-bearing intersections. Failed instantiations still surface both the instantiation-site error and the surrounding generic-constraint diagnostic when the result cannot satisfy the constraint.

Owner layer: this is checker type-query resolution and type-environment evaluation, with lowering preserving `typeof` instantiation arguments when a checker override supplies the value type. The checker keeps TS2344-family decisions routed through the existing instantiation-expression and constraint helpers rather than adding diagnostic string/display checks.

Adjacent-case test matrix:
- reported `typeof arr.map<string>` with default libs does not emit TS2503/TS2833
- reported `ReturnType<typeof numbers.map<string>>` does not emit TS2344/TS2833
- user-defined `typeof ops.convert<string>` value-property chain does not emit namespace diagnostics
- nested renamed chain `typeof services.mapper.pick<boolean>` follows the same rule
- `typeof Err<U>` where `Err` is `typeof Class & (<T>() => T)` expands to concrete constructor/call signatures for TS2352 overlap
- invalid `typeof createCacheReducer<QR>` emits TS2635 and still triggers TS2344 at the surrounding constrained type argument

Known unsupported shapes/fallback: missing roots still report normal name-resolution diagnostics. If a base cannot be proven callable/constructable, the existing `Application(base, args)` fallback is preserved for later environment evaluation.

## Project Corpus Impact
- Row: n/a (Track 8 parser/checker diagnostic fix for #6133)
- Bug family: `typeof` instantiation-expression namespace, constraint, and display diagnostics
- Evidence: focused checker/core tests plus TypeScript 5.9.3 oracle checks; no project-corpus behavior intentionally changed.

Verification:
- TypeScript 5.9.3 oracle for TS2352 constructor/call intersection repro
- TypeScript 5.9.3 oracle for TS2635 + TS2344 failed instantiation repro
- TypeScript 5.9.3 oracle for callable `typeof Foo<string>` assignment repro

author: xiaoyuervae
body:
## Summary

The embedded terminal's zsh wrapper looks like it should source the user's `~/.zshrc`, but in practice it never does. The shell shows the bare macOS `%n@%m %1~ %#` prompt with no aliases, functions, oh-my-zsh, starship, etc.

## Repro

Any zsh user. Open an embedded terminal in cc-viewer and try a function or alias from `~/.zshrc`:

```
dayuer@MacBook-Pro-2 dingtalk-nanobot-stack % ccuse idealab_opus_dpsk
zsh: command not found: ccuse
```

Where `ccuse` is defined as a function in `~/.zshrc` (and works fine in any normal terminal).

## Root cause

In `lib/terminal-env.js`, the wrapper is two-staged: `.zshenv` then `.zshrc`.

`prepareEmbeddedShellSpawn` sets `env.ZDOTDIR` to the wrapper dir before zsh starts. So inside the wrapper `.zshenv`:

```sh
# ZDOTDIR is already the wrapper dir here
export CCV_EFFECTIVE_ZDOTDIR=\"\${ZDOTDIR:-\$__ccv_original_zdotdir}\"
```

The `:-` fallback never fires — `CCV_EFFECTIVE_ZDOTDIR` is always set to the wrapper dir.

Then in the wrapper `.zshrc`:

```sh
__ccv_wrapper_zdotdir=\"\$ZDOTDIR\"                              # wrapper dir
__ccv_original_zdotdir=\"\${CCV_EFFECTIVE_ZDOTDIR:-...}\"        # ALSO wrapper dir
if [[ \"\$__ccv_original_zdotdir\" != \"\$__ccv_wrapper_zdotdir\" && ... ]]; then
  source \"\$__ccv_original_zdotdir/.zshrc\"                     # never runs
fi
```

The `!=` check is always false. The user's real `~/.zshrc` is silently skipped on every embedded zsh launch.

Confirmed with `zsh -ix`:

```
+.../.zshrc:3> __ccv_original_zdotdir=/Users/dayuer/.claude/cc-viewer/shell-rc
+.../.zshrc:4> [[ /Users/.../shell-rc != /Users/.../shell-rc ]]
+.../.zshrc:9> unset CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER       # falls straight through to here
```

## Fix

In the wrapper `.zshenv`, compare `\$ZDOTDIR` against `\$__ccv_wrapper_zdotdir` (the wrapper dir captured at top of file). That correctly detects whether the user's own `.zshenv` (sourced just above) re-pointed `ZDOTDIR` somewhere else. If unchanged, use the captured original dir.

```sh
if [[ \"\$ZDOTDIR\" != \"\$__ccv_wrapper_zdotdir\" ]]; then
  export CCV_EFFECTIVE_ZDOTDIR=\"\$ZDOTDIR\"
else
  export CCV_EFFECTIVE_ZDOTDIR=\"\$__ccv_original_zdotdir\"
fi
```

`.zshrc` is unchanged.

## Tests

The existing terminal-env tests check generated rc-file *contents* with string-match — that's exactly why this bug slipped through (the wrong code matches the same regexes as the right code).

Added an end-to-end regression that actually spawns `/bin/zsh`:

```js
it("spawns zsh that actually sources the user's ~/.zshrc (regression)", () => {
  // Write synthetic .zshenv / .zshrc into homeDir, prepare wrapper, spawn zsh,
  // assert CCV_TEST_ZSHENV_LOADED=1, CCV_TEST_ZSHRC_LOADED=1, and a function
  // defined in the synthetic .zshrc is visible.
});
```

Verified the test fails on the pre-fix branch (1 fail / 5 pass) and passes on the fixed branch (6/6). Skips automatically if `/bin/zsh` is missing.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test test/terminal-env.test.js` — 6/6 pass.
- [x] Stash the fix → same test now fails with `ENV=0 RC=0 FN=no`, proving the regression test catches the bug.
- [x] Manual: rebuilt local cc-viewer, restarted ccv, opened embedded terminal → `ccuse` resolves, starship prompt loads.

## Env

- cc-viewer `main` (HEAD `8a8d8c1`, v1.6.266)
- Node v22.22.0, macOS Darwin 25.5.0 — bug is platform-independent (pure shell semantics).

## Related

Independent of #91 (file-browser symlink classification) — same file owner, unrelated code path.
