author: onelittlechildawa
body:
### Solved Problem

For EV yaw fusion, `EKF2_EVA_NOISE` is an angular noise value in rad, while the EV yaw aid source stores observation variance in rad^2. 

For magnetic declination fusion, the WMM declination path passed `0.5` directly. I assume that it's a overlook of #23215.

### Solution

Square the EV attitude noise before using it as a yaw observation variance.

Use the existing declination variance for the WMM declination path as well.

### Test coverage

How to trigger:
Enable EV yaw fusion and provide EV yaw variance below the `EKF2_EVA_NOISE` floor.
Use default geo declination handling with WMM declination available and mag declination fusion active.

- [#​13916](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/13916) [`be8a98c`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/be8a98c2be0c83a270415ff4591e1b9971aab747) Thanks [@​emily-shen](https://redirect.github.com/emily-shen)! - Add `--keep-vars` flag to `wrangler versions upload`, matching the existing behavior in `wrangler deploy`. When set, environment variables configured via the dashboard are preserved rather than being deleted before the upload.

##### Patch Changes

- [#​13926](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/13926) [`19ed49a`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/19ed49a008be273df0ce60a817f4f367f4cea8fd) Thanks [@​dependabot](https://redirect.github.com/apps/dependabot)! - Update dependencies of "miniflare", "wrangler"

  The following dependency versions have been updated:

  | Dependency | From         | To           |
  | ---------- | ------------ | ------------ |
  | workerd    | 1.20260511.1 | 1.20260515.1 |

- [#​11471](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/11471) [`3ff0a50`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/3ff0a50349a78c17d64c45c0411771cc2d2dba0a) Thanks [@​HW13](https://redirect.github.com/HW13)! - Improve `wrangler types --env-interface` for multi-worker projects.

  Custom env interfaces generated by `wrangler types` no longer expand from `Cloudflare.Env`, avoiding some unintended type expansion when multiple workers' generated types are used together.

- [#​13910](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/13910) [`bf688f7`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/bf688f7735d602e963a7907a4a703aa7de2038fe) Thanks [@​timoconnellaus](https://redirect.github.com/timoconnellaus)! - Fix `Failed to fetch auth token: 401 Unauthorized` from sibling-rotated refresh tokens

  `refreshToken` previously used the refresh token from module-level `localState`, which is populated once at startup and never re-read. OAuth refresh tokens are single-use, so when a sibling wrangler process (in another repo, another shell, or a parallel script) refreshes first, it rotates the token server-side and writes the new value to the shared config file (`~/Library/Preferences/.wrangler/config/default.toml` on macOS). The long-lived process — typically `wrangler dev` — then sends its stale in-memory token on the next refresh and gets `401 Unauthorized` from `https://dash.cloudflare.com/oauth2/token`, falling through to interactive login and timing out unattended.

  `refreshToken` now calls `reinitialiseAuthTokens()` before exchanging, picking up the latest refresh token written by any sibling process. The previously empty `catch {}` also now logs the underlying error at debug level so future refresh failures are diagnosable without source-diving.

- [#​13843](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/13843) [`2e72c83`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/2e72c83aa95d25de343c396df67c0a35b83b70cd) Thanks [@​nzws](https://redirect.github.com/nzws)! - Fix `wrangler versions secret put/delete/bulk` to preserve the existing version's placement settings

  When creating a new version via `wrangler versions secret`, the previous code only re-emitted a bare `{ mode: "smart" }` placement when the API reported `placement_mode === "smart"`, dropping any other placement entirely. The new version is now created with the placement settings returned by the API, so placement settings survive a secret put/delete/bulk round-trip.

- [#​13908](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/13908) [`802eaf4`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/802eaf47fa28f5bfa3a07b0782acdaac6f12781d) Thanks [@​shiminshen](https://redirect.github.com/shiminshen)! - fix: stop rewriting query strings that happen to contain the request `Host`

  `wrangler dev` previously rewrote occurrences of the outer host inside `request.url`'s query string. For example, a request to `?echo=https%3A%2F%2Fdevelopment.test%2Fpath` with `Host: development.test` would be seen by the user worker as `?echo=https%3A%2F%2Fproduction.test%2Fpath`, silently mutating opaque application data such as `redirect_uri` values in OAuth flows.

  The proxy worker now sets the internal `MF-Original-URL` header *after* its blanket host-rewriting pass over request headers, so the URL passed to the user worker preserves the original query string.

- [#​13827](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/pull/13827) [`8f5cdb1`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/8f5cdb14dda20f6036c2305195041105d4d109e3) Thanks [@​greyvugrin](https://redirect.github.com/greyvugrin)! - Fix multi-environment warning when CLOUDFLARE\_ENV is set

  Commands that warn when multiple environments are configured but none is specified (e.g. `wrangler deploy`, `wrangler secret put`) were not accounting for the `CLOUDFLARE_ENV` environment variable when deciding whether to show the warning. This caused a misleading warning to appear even when the target environment was correctly specified via `CLOUDFLARE_ENV`.

- Updated dependencies \[[`19ed49a`](https://redirect.github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/commit/19ed49a008be273df0ce60a817f4f367f4cea8fd)]:
  - miniflare\@​4.20260515.0

</details>

author: yulmwu
body:
This PR introduces the most fundamental implementation of the Sandbox Object, which can be considered one of the core features of the orchestrator project. The key points are as follows:

* Introduced the Sandbox object model (Control Plane resource)
* Added a scheduler loop (Node/resource/port-based placement)
* Added a reconcile loop (TTL-based cleanup and state convergence)

# Add Sandbox Object Model

A Sandbox object concept, similar to a Kubernetes Pod, has been introduced into the Orchestrator.
It is divided into the user-defined spec and the actual runtime status. The supported phases are as follows:

* Pending
* Scheduled
* Running
* Failed
* Deleting

The following Control Plane APIs have been added:

* `POST /api/v1/sandboxes`
* `GET /api/v1/sandboxes`
* `GET /api/v1/sandboxes/:id`
* `DELETE /api/v1/sandboxes/:id`

# Implement Scheduler Loop

By default, newly created Sandboxes enter the `Pending` state.
The scheduler loop periodically scans Pending Sandboxes and attempts placement. During scheduling, it considers node status (`Ready`), node resource availability (`allocatable/used/available`), and HostPort availability/range in order to make placement decisions.

If scheduling fails, the `status.lastError` field is updated.

Related environment variables are as follows:

```ini 
ORCH_SCHEDULER_INTERVAL=3s
ORCH_HOSTPORT_MIN=10000
ORCH_HOSTPORT_MAX=32767
```

# Implement Reconcile Loop

This component is mainly intended to support Control Plane features such as TTL handling.
In this PR, the reconcile loop automatically removes Sandboxes whose TTL has expired.

Related environment variables are as follows:

```ini 
ORCH_RECONCILE_INTERVAL=5s
```

# Additional Changes

API rate limiting has also been added for Sandbox creation, configurable through the following environment variables:

```ini
ORCH_CREATE_RPS=20
ORCH_CREATE_BURST=40
```

In addition, Swagger (`swaggo`) documentation is now officially supported, and the REST API documentation will continue to be improved. Several issues have also been fixed, and some features have been enhanced.

For more details, please refer to the documentation and updated source code.

author: theodorebugnet
body: # Description Refactor core transaction signing types to separate the consumer-facing unsigned payload from the canonical signing payload. * What used to be called `UnsignedTransaction{, V0, V1}` is now called `TransactionSigningPayload{, V0, V1}`. This is the type that is serialized for signing. * Serialization logic is centralised to this Payload, in particular the `chain_hash` is now a field on the Payload rather than manually apended. * A new type, called `UnsignedTransaction`, is added to encapsulate the actual user-defined parts of the transaction. This removes the old ambiguity where “unsigned transaction” sometimes meant “user payload” and sometimes meant “exact signed preimage”. ### Reviewer Guide The core logic is in `crates/module-system/sov-modules-api/src/transaction/`, specifically `unsigned.rs` and `signing_payload/*`. The serialization logic also changed accordingly in `crates/module-system/sov-modules-api/src/runtime/capabilities/authentication.rs`. The majority of the rest of the touched files are switching the usage from `UnsignedTransactionV0` to `UnsignedTransaction` and the signatures of the serialization/signing method on these. In `sov-solana-offchain-auth`, the rename is mostly mechanical. The outer `Message` types have also been renamed to `Envelope`, because the solana spec defines "message" as the actual (signed) offchain message, which in this context is the Payload. ### Typescript The Schema root changed from `UnsignedTransaction` to `TransactionSigningPayload`, since the UnsignedTransaction is never actually serialised. In Typescript, adds `TypeBuilder.transactionSigningPayload` and adjust the signing flow accordingly: the user provides fields for the UnsignedTransaction, the `typeBuilder` builds a `transactionSigningPayload` which is then serialized. - [x] I have updated `CHANGELOG.md` with a new entry if my PR makes any breaking changes or fixes a bug. body:
## Summary
This PR introduces several major features and improvements to enhance the chat, companion, and check-in systems:

1. **Message Version History & Regeneration** - Users can now regenerate AI messages while preserving previous versions, with UI controls to browse between versions
2. **Companion Quick Phrases** - Add customizable quick phrases for the companion mode with easy access via a phrase panel
3. **Timer-based Check-in Goals** - Extend check-in system to support time-tracking goals alongside traditional checklist goals
4. **Dynamic Model List** - Automatically fetch and cache the latest model list from OpenRouter API instead of relying on hardcoded models
5. **Companion-Checkin Integration** - Link companion timer sessions to check-in goals for automatic time logging
6. **UI/UX Improvements** - Mobile keyboard handling, context menus, and various refinements

## Key Changes

### Message Version History (js/app.js)
- Added `altVersions` array to message objects to store previous AI responses
- New `switchMsgVersion()` function to navigate between message versions with `‹` `›` buttons
- Modified `regenMsg()` to save current message to `altVersions` before regenerating
- New `callAIForRegenAt()` function to regenerate at a specific message position
- Updated `makeBubble()` to display correct version content and thinking blocks
- Version navigation UI shows current position (e.g., "2/3")

### Companion Quick Phrases (js/app.js)
- Added `DEFAULT_PHRASES` array with preset phrases
- New `companionSpeakClick()` for single/double-click behavior (expand panel vs. speak)
- Phrase panel UI with customizable phrases stored in settings
- `compAddPhrase()` and `compRemovePhrase()` for phrase management
- Phrases passed to `callCompanionAI()` for context-aware responses

### Timer-based Check-in Goals (js/checkin.js)
- Added `goalType` field ('count' or 'timer') to goals
- Added `targetMinutes` field for timer goals
- New `minutesLogged` field on records to track cumulative time
- Modified check-in modal to show time input for timer goals instead of progress slider
- Timer progress bar visualization in today section
- Automatic completion when logged minutes reach target
- Updated toast messages and UI labels based on goal type

### Dynamic Model List (js/app.js)
- New `fetchOpenRouterModels()` function that:
  - Fetches models from OpenRouter API on app init
  - Caches results in localStorage for 6 hours
  - Falls back to hardcoded list if fetch fails
  - Filters out internal OpenRouter models
- `_applyFetchedModels()` updates MODELS array and re-renders model selectors
- Hardcoded model list updated with latest models (GPT-4.1, o3, Gemini 2.5, etc.)

### Companion-Checkin Integration (js/app.js, js/checkin.js)
- New `companionLinkedGoalId` setting to link companion to a check-in goal
- `companionPause()` now logs elapsed time to linked timer goal via `ckAddCompanionMinutes()`
- `callCompanionAI()` includes task context when linked goal exists
- Goal progress shown in companion AI responses
- `_refreshLinkedTaskSelect()` populates linked task dropdown on companion page

### UI/UX Improvements
- Mobile keyboard handling: bottom nav hides when keyboard appears (js/app.js)
- New context menu system for check-in "more" operations (export, edit, history)
- Check-in export to JSON/CSV/Markdown/HTML formats (js/checkin.js)
- Mobile "new chat" button in header (index.html)
- Improved companion immersive mode with phrase panel support
- Better visual feedback for timer progress and version navigation

### Other Changes
- `buildMsgsUpTo()` helper function for building message context up to a specific message
- Updated `speakMsg()` and `copyMsg()` to use displayed version content
- Removed hardcoded `momentContactId

## Summary
- **Problem:** `_inline_format` in `services/export.py` converted markdown links to `<a>` tags without URL scheme validation — `[click](javascript:alert(1))` was a working XSS payload on public share pages

body:
In plan django tests (projects, not libraries), the `temp_private_root` helper sets up an in-memory storage, which breaks the SSL context machinery that expects a path to exist on disk. 30d5aa3e607d449c2b999927bb95309e93eec5c9 ensures that in those situations, the file is created on disk in a temp directory. I haven't found a quick and elegant mechanism yet to clean those up, so it kind-of keeps the status quo (those files weren't cleaned up before either with the temp private root, see sergei-maertens/django-privates#8).

Additionally while nuking my virtualenv I pulled in the latest django-simple-certmanager which has some breaking changes as well, so I handled them and now require at least that version to keep the code simple enough. The next release of django-digid-eherkenning will therefore also be technically breaking. We need to take a look at the python/django versions anyway, since privates 4 requires py312+ now anyway.

author: baseballyama
body:
## Summary

Two related site-readiness changes, paired so the deploy works against the cleaned-up design from the start.

### 1. GitHub Pages deploy workflow

\`.github/workflows/deploy-site.yml\` modelled on xlsx-kit's. Builds the packages first (so the site's \`workspace:*\` deps resolve to fresh \`dist/index.mjs\`), type-checks the site with \`svelte-check\`, builds with \`BASE_PATH=/word-kit\`, uploads to Pages.

Triggers:
- \`push\` to \`main\` touching \`site/**\`, \`packages/**\`, \`pnpm-lock.yaml\`, \`pnpm-workspace.yaml\`, or the workflow file
- \`workflow_dispatch\` for manual re-runs

\`concurrency: pages / cancel-in-progress\` keeps two deploys from racing.

**Manual step**: enable Pages once at **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: GitHub Actions** — the workflow can't do that for itself.

### 2. Drop the horizontal baseline-rule motif

The full-site \`body::before\` manuscript-baseline pattern and the \`.hero-glow\` horizontal-line block under the hero are gone. Sibling distinction now lives entirely in the colour story:

- word-kit: proof-pen red accent + brass co-accent
- xlsx-kit: ember orange accent + brass co-accent (post-#80)

The radial accent / brass glows in the hero stay; they sit on a clean warm-dark surface now.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter word-kit-site check\` — 0 errors / 0 warnings
- [x] \`pnpm --filter word-kit-site build\` — every route prerenders

body:
This PR introduces a Codama-based SDK for both rust and typescript. The typescript SDK is introduced alongside the existing one to allow for migration and deprecation gracefully.

NOTE: This PR relies on updating the IDL to parity with the current code (the current main branch IDL is stale against the tip of main program code) which itself requires temporarily updating anchor and the solana dependencies to allow building a working anchor toolchain on a recent rust version. with the new anchor-generated IDL, Codama was run to generate the new `sdk/rust` and `sdk/ts` directories.

The Codama code is also unable to generate full parity SDK components covering the custom events strategy of the smart account program so a complimentary `sdk/rust/src/helpers` module, feature-gated is added to provide missing functionality relative to the generated code and temporarily moved/preserved whenever the codama code is regenerated.

author: thdelmas
body:
## Summary

Adds a native `PairEntryActivity` that lets users paste the JSON payload an OSmosis partner encodes into its QR code, and apply it to the persisted config. Same write path as `PairReceiver` (broadcast handler from #165); new user-facing entry point that doesn't depend on the broken `LetheActivity`.

## Why this (and not the camera-QR scanner)

On user builds, the in-WebView QR scanner ([`static/qr-scan.js`](static/qr-scan.js) using jsQR inside `LetheActivity`'s WebView) is unreachable because the host activity crashes from WebView-in-system-uid (#159). [#165](https://github.com/thdelmas/lethe/pull/165) unblocked the adb-broadcast pair sub-path; this PR unblocks the user-facing one.

A native camera-based QR scanner is the eventual best UX but needs ZXing-or-equivalent integration plus build-glue research (the system-app `Android.mk` template at [`apply-overlays.sh:410`](apply-overlays.sh#L410) doesn't currently bring in any third-party JARs, and cm-14.1's Java version constrains what ZXing release we can use). Filing as a separate tracker issue.

## What's here

- **[`PairReceiver.applyPayloadJson(ctx, payload)`](java/org/osmosis/lethe/PairReceiver.java)** — static helper that parses the `{\"lethe_pair\":true,\"provider\":...,\"key\":...,\"model\":...}` shape, calls the existing `merge()`, and saves through `LetheConfig`. Reused by `PairEntryActivity` now, by a future `PairScanActivity` later. Throws `JSONException` on any failure (missing flag, missing provider/key, malformed JSON, save failure) so callers can surface a single error path.

- **[`PairEntryActivity`](java/org/osmosis/lethe/PairEntryActivity.java)** — paste-friendly multi-line `EditText` (monospace, no autocorrect, no suggestions), Apply/Cancel buttons, `Toast` on success or failure. Programmatic UI in the same style as [`AutoWipeSettingsActivity`](java/org/osmosis/lethe/AutoWipeSettingsActivity.java) (#152). No XML layouts.

- **[`AndroidManifest.xml`](AndroidManifest.xml)** — declares the activity with both `MAIN`+`LAUNCHER` (shows as \"LETHE Pair\" in Trebuchet's app drawer) and `lethe.intent.PAIR_ENTRY` (for `am start` / future deep links). `excludeFromRecents` so it doesn't clutter the task list.

## Reachability

Two surfaces on user builds:

- Trebuchet app drawer → **\"LETHE Pair\"** icon (distinct from the broken \"LETHE\" launcher entry)
- `adb shell am start -a lethe.intent.PAIR_ENTRY`

## What this does *not* fix

- The in-WebView QR-scan path (`NativeLauncher.scanQR()` → ZXing intent → `onActivityResult` → `onQRResult` JS) is still gated by `LetheActivity` and remains broken on user builds.
- Mascot / chat / voice surfaces in `LetheActivity` still unreachable.

## Test plan

- [ ] On a user build, open Trebuchet app drawer → verify \"LETHE Pair\" icon appears alongside the existing \"LETHE\" launcher entry
- [ ] Tap \"LETHE Pair\" → paste a valid payload like `{\"lethe_pair\":true,\"provider\":\"anthropic\",\"key\":\"sk-ant-test\",\"model\":\"claude-opus-4-6\"}` → tap Apply
- [ ] Verify Toast \"Paired with anthropic.\" and `cat /data/data/org.osmosis.lethe.agent/files/config.json` shows the new key + `active_provider=anthropic`
- [ ] Verify `/v1/route/plan` returns `anthropic` as a candidate when `configured_cloud=[\"anthropic\"]`
- [ ] Paste an invalid payload (missing `lethe_pair` flag, missing `provider`, malformed JSON) → verify Toast with error message and the field background flashes red
- [ ] Also reachable via `adb shell am start -a lethe.intent.PAIR_ENTRY`
- [x] `bash scripts/code-quality-check.sh` clean

author: dkwkekzz
body:
## Summary
Implement entity-self-declares-action pattern by adding `DispatchEventByReg` opcode and supporting infrastructure. This allows entities to expose their default action event tag dynamically, enabling Story_TargetAction to dispatch events based on entity properties rather than hardcoded logic.

## Key Changes

- **VM Interpreter**: Added `Op_DispatchEventByReg()` opcode that reads a GameplayTag NetIndex from a register and dispatches the corresponding event with current runtime context (source/target entity, location, params).

- **Story Builder API**: 
  - Added `DispatchEventByReg(RegisterIndex)` and `DispatchEventByReg(FHktVar)` overloads for both register-based and variable-based instruction emission
  - Added `SaveTagEntity()` helper to convert GameplayTag to NetIndex and save as entity property (used during spawn)

- **JSON Parser**: Registered `DispatchEventByReg` and `SaveTagEntity` commands for story JSON deserialization with proper tag resolution at build time.

- **Core Properties**: Added `DefaultActionEventTag` property (Cold) to entity state — stores the NetIndex of an entity's default action event, populated during natural entity spawn (Birch/Oak).

- **Story Updates**:
  - `Story_TargetAction.json`: Added `check_natural` label to detect entities with `DefaultActionEventTag` and dispatch via `DispatchEventByReg` instead of hardcoded move behavior
  - `Birch_Spawn.json` & `Oak_Spawn.json`: Updated to populate `DefaultActionEventTag` on spawned entities using `SaveTagEntity` with `Event.Natural.TreeFelled` / `Event.Natural.OakFelled`

- **VM Execution**: Integrated `DispatchEventByReg` case into instruction dispatch and precondition checks.

## Implementation Details

- NetIndex resolution happens at story build time (JSON parse) for `SaveTagEntity`, avoiding runtime tag manager lookups during spawn
- `Op_DispatchEventByReg` validates NetIndex > 0 (0 or negative means "no default action") and silently skips if invalid
- Event context (source/target entity, location, params) flows from runtime context, consistent with other dispatch opcodes
- Follows ISP 3-Layer separation: intent (entity declares action) → simulation (VM dispatches) → presentation (story handles event)

body:
## Problem

The pre-deploy command `python schema_bootstrap.py` fails with `psycopg2.errors.UndefinedColumn: column "platform_role" does not exist` because the `User` model in `models.py` never defined `platform_role`, so `db.create_all()` creates the `users` table without it. `migrate_admin_password.py` then immediately queries `SELECT ... platform_role ... FROM users`, which crashes.

## Solution

Added `platform_role = db.Column(db.String(64), nullable=True)` to the `User` model so fresh databases get the column via `db.create_all()`. Also added a defensive `information_schema.columns` check in `migrate_admin_password.py` (step 1b) that issues `ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN platform_role VARCHAR(64)` when the column is absent, matching the pattern already used in `migrate_admin_role.py` and making the migration safe against older databases.

### Changes
- **Modified** `models.py`
- **Modified** `migrate_admin_password.py`

## What

Two long-standing pytest warnings cleaned up in the test suite.

## Why

- The shared `generate_ble_device` helper always injected `rssi=-127`, which bleak now flags with `DeprecationWarning: Passing additional arguments for BLEDevice is deprecated and has no effect`. Every test fixture hit it.
- Five `patch.object(client._client, "bluetooth_device_connect")` sites omitted `return_value`, so the patched `AsyncMock`'s return became another `AsyncMock`. That value is assigned to `_cancel_connection_state` and called synchronously during cleanup, leaking `RuntimeWarning: coroutine '_execute_mock_call' was never awaited` and risking a future hard failure if `filterwarnings` is tightened.

## How

- Drop `rssi` from `BLE_DEVICE_DEFAULTS` and the helper signature (bleak ignores it anyway).
- Add `return_value=Mock()` to the five connect-patch sites; this mirrors the real `aioesphomeapi.bluetooth_device_connect` contract (returns a sync `Callable[[], None]`).

## Testing

- `poetry run pytest` — 73 passed.
- `pytest -W error::DeprecationWarning -W error::RuntimeWarning` — 73 passed (was 34 failed before).

author: tieguy
body:
## Why

Two implementations of "parse a verdict response from the LLM" had drifted in this repo:

1. **`core/parsing.js` `parseVerificationResult`** — canonical location, inlined into `main.js` via `scripts/sync-main.js`, also called by `cli/verify.js`. JSON-only; on parse failure returned `{verdict: 'ERROR', ...}`. No recovery.
2. **`benchmark/run_benchmark.js` `parseResponse`** — its own JSON-extraction logic *plus* a fallback regex `/verdict["\s:]+([A-Z_ ]+)/i`. On parse failure returned `{verdict: 'PARSE_ERROR', ...}`.

Per the project's single-source-of-truth pattern (precedent: #195 `core/compare`, #203 `core/prompts`), the benchmark should be importing from `core/`, not maintaining a divergent copy.

## The failure mode this consolidation fixes

Small open-weight models — **Granite 4.1 8B** specifically — sometimes emit markdown-formatted reasoning instead of the requested JSON:

```
**Step-by-step verification**

1. **Identify the claim's specific assertions**
   - …

**Verdict:** SUPPORTED
**Comments:** "…" Both the date and the founder match.
```

`JSON.parse` fails (no `{…}`). The benchmark's existing fallback regex `/verdict["\s:]+([A-Z_ ]+)/i` *also* fails because after the `:` in `**Verdict:**` comes `**`, and `*` isn't in the `["\s:]` character class — the regex can't advance to the verdict word.

**Empirical impact:** in a 181-row × 9-provider benchmark run, Granite produced 21 of these parse failures (11.6%, vs 0.6% on a prior prompt). Tightening the recovery reclaims the bulk of them; expected post-fix parse-error rate is ~1%.

## What changes

### `core/parsing.js`

- `parseVerificationResult(response)` stays the single export.
- After JSON.parse fails (post code-fence and `{…}` extraction), strip markdown emphasis (`*+` and `__+`) and run a tolerant regex `/verdict[\s:"']+([A-Z][A-Z _]*)/i`.
- A private `canonicalizeFallbackVerdict` maps the captured word(s) to the prompt's UPPERCASE canonical form (`SUPPORTED` / `NOT SUPPORTED` / `PARTIALLY SUPPORTED` / `SOURCE UNAVAILABLE`).
- Sentinel verdict on total failure is now `'PARSE_ERROR'` (was `'ERROR'`) — matches the benchmark's existing convention.

### `benchmark/run_benchmark.js`

- Imports `parseVerificationResult` from `../core/parsing.js`.
- Deletes the local JSON-extraction + fallback regex (`parseResponse`).
- `shapeResult` (now exported for testability) wraps the core parser, applies the benchmark-local title-case `normalizeVerdict` (`'SUPPORTED'` → `'Supported'`) for results.json schema compatibility, defaults missing confidence to 0, and attaches `raw_response` / `usage`.
- `normalizeVerdict` stays local to the runner — the benchmark's results.json stores title-case, while the userscript and CLI consume UPPERCASE.

### Why not lift `normalizeVerdict` into `core/`?

Considered it (and the task description suggested it as the likely call). The blocker is casing: the userscript expects UPPERCASE verdicts (`if (result.verdict === 'SUPPORTED')` etc.), the benchmark's results.json stores title case. Putting one normalization in `core/` would force one of those formats to change. Keeping the title-case mapping in the benchmark runner — and letting `shapeResult` bridge — is the smaller, lower-risk move and preserves the existing results.json schema. The core parser returns the prompt-canonical UPPERCASE form, which both consumers can adapt to as needed.

### Caller updates for the sentinel rename

`'ERROR'` → `'PARSE_ERROR'` for the *parse-failure* sentinel only:

- `cli/verify.js:350` — `if (verdict.verdict === 'PARSE_ERROR')` (exit code 11).
- `main.js:2716` (displayResult) — `result.verdict === 'PARSE_ERROR'` case in the verdict-styling switch.
- `main.js` is re-synced via `npm run build`, so the inlined parser picks up `'PARSE_ERROR'` automatically.

**Kept as `'ERROR'` (intentionally):**
- `main.js:3457` — synthetic verdict from the report-card API-call catch. That's a transport failure, not a parse failure; matches `benchmark/run_benchmark.js`'s `callProvider` API-error sentinel and `compare_results.js`'s `'ERROR'` skip filter.
- `main.js:2669` — DOM `textContent = 'ERROR'` in the catch path; pure UI string.

## Tests

`tests/parsing.test.js` (7 new + 1 updated):

- Bare JSON parses correctly (regression guard).
- Code-fenced JSON parses correctly.
- JSON surrounded by prose still extracted by legacy `{…}` matcher.
- Granite-style `**Verdict:** SUPPORTED` recovers as `SUPPORTED`.
- Recovery is case-insensitive on the `verdict` keyword: `**verdict:**` and `**VERDICT:**` both work.
- Two-word verdict `**Verdict:** NOT SUPPORTED` preserved.
- `**Verdict:** PARTIALLY SUPPORTED` preserved.
- Pure prose with no verdict marker → `PARSE_ERROR` sentinel.
- Completely malformed input → `PARSE_ERROR` sentinel.

`tests/benchmark_runner.test.js` (3 new wiring smoke tests, no duplication with `parsing.test.js`):

- `shapeResult` title-cases the core parser's output and forwards `raw_response` / `usage`.
- `shapeResult` recovers the Granite markdown case end-to-end (the regression that motivated this PR).
- `shapeResult` returns `PARSE_ERROR` with `confidence: 0` on unrecoverable prose.

## Acceptance

- [x] `npm test` — 229/229 passing (was 219; +10 cases).
- [x] `npm run build -- --check` — `main.js` in sync with `core/`.
- [x] Single commit.
- [ ] Benchmark rerun — out of scope for this PR (the spec calls it out as a separate measurement); this change is verifiable from unit tests alone.

## Summary

- The pulsing status orb (red/green/amber dot on the map) was anchored to the Strait geographically only on initial load. When the user panned or zoomed, the CSS `left`/`top` percentages stayed fixed so the orb drifted off-target.
- Fix: extract `ORB_LATLNG = [26.5, 56.3]` as a named constant, then listen to Leaflet's `move zoom` events and recalculate the CSS percentages via `map.latLngToContainerPoint()` on every frame — same calculation that runs on `map.whenReady()`.

body:
## Problem
326 Sentry events: `create_url()` returning the Catena home page fallback because `CATENA_ABBREV_FOR_BOOK.get(self.book)` returns `None` when the scraper provides a book name with curly quotes (e.g. `St. Paul\u2019s Epistle to the Hebrews` with U+2019 instead of U+0027 apostrophe).

## Solution
1. **`normalize_book_name()`** in `hub/constants.py` — NFKC normalization + curly/smart quote replacement (both single and double quotes)
2. **`CATENA_ABBREV_FOR_BOOK_NORMALIZED`** — precomputed normalized lookup dict (built once at import time)
3. **`Reading.create_url()`** uses `normalize_book_name()` before lookup

## Tests (7 new)
- 4 normalization tests (curly → straight, already straight, None, empty/whitespace)
- 2 normalized dict tests (curly-quote resolution, all original keys preserved)
- 2 `create_url` integration tests (curly-quote Hebrew → "heb" URL, unknown book → home page)

## Lint & CI
- `ruff check .` — clean
- 45 tests pass (hub.tests.test_bible_api)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Low risk: small, localized change to `Reading.create_url()` that improves robustness of book-name lookup and adds coverage for the new normalization behavior.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes Catena URL generation when scrapers return Unicode curly/smart quotes in `Reading.book`.
> 
> Adds `normalize_book_name()` plus a precomputed `CATENA_ABBREV_FOR_BOOK_NORMALIZED` mapping in `hub/constants.py`, updates `Reading.create_url()` to normalize before lookup (and logs both raw/normalized on fallback), and extends `hub/tests/test_bible_api.py` with unit + integration tests covering normalization and URL generation.

author: arditti
body:
## Rollback Plan

If a change needs to be reverted, we will publish an updated version of the library.

## Changes to Security Controls

This change exposes a new opt-in security control. When `use_client_certificate_ocsp_endpoint = true`, CloudFront performs OCSP revocation checks against the CA's published OCSP endpoint during viewer mTLS, rejecting clients whose certificates have been revoked. The default (`false`) preserves existing behavior. There are no changes to the encryption, logging, or access controls of existing trust stores that don't opt in.

### Description

AWS [announced OCSP revocation support for CloudFront viewer mTLS](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/amazon-cloudfront-mtls-ocsp/) on 2026-05-14. The CloudFront API gained a `UseClientCertificateOCSPEndpoint` boolean on `CreateTrustStore`/`UpdateTrustStore`/`GetTrustStore`. When enabled, CloudFront contacts the OCSP endpoint published by the client certificate's issuing CA to verify that the certificate has not been revoked.

This PR:

- Bumps `github.com/aws/aws-sdk-go-v2/service/cloudfront` from `v1.63.0` to `v1.64.0`, which adds the `UseClientCertificateOCSPEndpoint` field on the relevant input/output types.
- Adds a `use_client_certificate_ocsp_endpoint` attribute (Optional, Computed) to the `aws_cloudfront_trust_store` resource. The Plugin Framework `fwflex` machinery already in use auto-wires it into Create/Update/Read.
- Updates the `aws_cloudfront_trust_store` documentation.
- Adds `TestAccCloudFrontTrustStore_useClientCertificateOCSPEndpoint`, which creates a trust store with OCSP enabled, then updates it to disable OCSP.

Example configuration:

```hcl
resource "aws_cloudfront_trust_store" "example" {
  name = "example-trust-store"

  ca_certificates_bundle_source {
    ca_certificates_bundle_s3_location {
      bucket = aws_s3_bucket.example.id
      key    = aws_s3_object.ca_bundle.key
      region = "us-east-1"
    }
  }

  use_client_certificate_ocsp_endpoint = true
}
```

### Relations

Closes #47927

### References

- AWS announcement: https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2026/05/amazon-cloudfront-mtls-ocsp/
- aws-sdk-go-v2 cloudfront v1.64.0 changelog entry: "Adding a new boolean for OCSP Revocations in Viewer mTLS Create and Update APIs, and adding a new 'Passthrough' option for TrustStore modes"
- Related work for the same SDK release: passthrough mode for `aws_cloudfront_distribution` (#47930)

### Output from Acceptance Testing

Acceptance tests for trust stores require `TF_ACC=1` and live CloudFront/S3 resources. I have not run the full mTLS suite myself; the new test compiles and the package builds cleanly.

```console
% go test -count=1 -run "TestAccCloudFrontTrustStore_useClientCertificateOCSPEndpoint" -short ./internal/service/cloudfront/
ok  	github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/internal/service/cloudfront	7.551s
```

Per the [CloudFront contribution note in `docs/dependency-updates.md`](https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform-provider-aws/blob/main/docs/dependency-updates.md#cloudfront-changes), running the full `TestAccCloudFront` suite is recommended before merging the SDK bump.

author: agent-sandbox-automattic[bot]
body:
## What

Implements MPI-357: hard bounces in the MailPoet email suppression table now expire after 14 days since their last hit.

Two new classes are added to `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/mailpoet/`:

### `WPCOMSH_MailPoet_Recipient_Validator`

Validates whether a hashed email address is an **active** hard bouncer by querying the `mailpoet_email_suppression` table. A hard bounce is only considered active if `COALESCE(latest_hit, suppressed_at)` is within the last 14 days — matching the expiry logic already present in the Ruby email-worker service (`BounceManager#expired?`). Complaints are not subject to expiry.

### `WPCOMSH_MailPoet_Suppression_Manager`

Inserts or updates hard bounce suppression records. When a record already exists (identified by the `(mailpoet_user_id, hashed_recipient)` unique key), only `latest_hit` is updated — `suppressed_at`, `dsndiag`, and other fields are left unchanged. This preserves the original suppression timestamp across subsequent bounce events (e.g. `mkhb` calls from email-worker).

## Why

- A hard bounce older than 14 days (no recent hit) should no longer block sending — especially relevant for monthly newsletters where the same address bounces, then the account is fixed, but the 14-day window expires before the next send.
- Storing new bounce events must not overwrite `suppressed_at` so the history of when an address was first suppressed is preserved.

## Testing

PHPUnit tests in `tests/MailPoetRecipientValidatorTest.php` and `tests/MailPoetSuppressionManagerTest.php` cover:
- Recent hard bounce is active
- Expired hard bounce (>14 days) is inactive
- Fallback to `suppressed_at` when `latest_hit` is NULL
- Complaints are never treated as hard bounces
- User-ID scoping works correctly
- New suppression records set both timestamps; duplicate records only update `latest_hit`
- `suppressed_at` and `dsndiag` are preserved on update

## Changes

- `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/mailpoet/class-mailpoet-recipient-validator.php` — new
- `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/mailpoet/class-mailpoet-suppression-manager.php` — new
- `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/wpcomsh.php` — load both new classes
- `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/tests/MailPoetRecipientValidatorTest.php` — new
- `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/tests/MailPoetSuppressionManagerTest.php` — new
- `projects/plugins/wpcomsh/changelog/mpi-357-hard-bounce-expiry` — new

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added/updated
- [x] Changelog entry added
- [ ] Generate changelog entries for this PR (using AI)

author: yanivkalfa
body:
0.5.17 introduced 'swap on prior HMR DLL' but the HMR Roslyn compile used CSharpParseOptions.Default which defines no preprocessor symbols. The SG and HmrCSharpEmitter wrap __hmr_Render and the trampoline branch in #if UNITY_EDITOR, so every HMR DLL had them stripped out. Net effect: prior HMR DLL types had no field to swap, brand-new components silently no-op'd after the first save.

Fix: pull defines from CompilationPipeline.GetAssemblies(AssembliesType.Editor) and pass via CSharpParseOptions.WithPreprocessorSymbols. Falls back to UNITY_EDITOR-only if API unavailable. Also fixes a latent correctness bug where user companion .cs #if UNITY_EDITOR blocks compiled with opposite semantics in HMR vs project editor build.

Reworded the 'no __hmr_Render field' warning to point at the right remediation (restart Unity to clear stale pre-0.5.18 HMR DLLs).

author: aruchvesu
body:
## Summary

Closes the last open follow-up from the SECA-Android wiring audit (Section E). `API_CONTRACTS.md`'s "Error responses" section was a 9-line stub that claimed all endpoints return `{"detail": ...}`. That was inaccurate twice:

1. The body-size middleware (411/413/400) and slowapi rate-limit handler (429) emit `{"error": "..."}` — a different key. A client parsing only `body["detail"]` would silently miss the rate-limit and body-too-large messages.
2. The 422 Pydantic shape is a structured array, not a string — `{"detail": [{"loc": [...], "msg": "...", "type": "..."}]}`. A client treating `detail` as `str` would crash on field validation failures.

## What changed

`docs/API_CONTRACTS.md` "Error responses" replaced (~17 lines → ~120 lines) with a complete taxonomy:

- **Shape A** (`{"detail": ...}`) — FastAPI / Pydantic / HTTPException surface. Scalar string for most paths; structured array for Pydantic 422; documented one-line message for API-version mismatch.
- **Shape B** (`{"error": ...}`) — custom-middleware shape. Only 3 surfaces (`_LimitBodySize` for 411/413/400, `rate_limit_handler` for 429).
- **Status-code → shape mapping** covering 400/401/403/404/409/411/413/422/429/500 with exact body examples + triggers.
- **Client parsing recipe** — try `body["detail"]` first, fall back to `body["error"]`. Pydantic 422 `isinstance(detail, list)` documented as the only structured case.
- **Errors that DON'T propagate** — `ExplainSchemaError` + `OutputFirewallError`. Both caught + degraded inside the LLM pipeline.
- **Headers on error responses** — `X-API-Version` always present; `X-Auth-Token` rotation NOT emitted on failure paths.
- **Known inconsistency** — Shape A/B duality is historical. Consolidation needs a coordinated Android release.

## Source-pin tests added

Three bidirectional pins in `TestApiContractsErrorTaxonomy`:
- `test_shape_b_messages_appear_in_server_source` — every Shape-B message the doc cites must appear in `llm/server.py`.
- `test_shape_a_representative_messages_appear_in_server_source` — 6 Shape-A messages, each scoped to the file that owns the raise.
- `test_shape_b_keys_are_error_not_detail` — within 200 chars of each Shape-B message, `"error"` must appear. Catches a "consolidate on Shape A" patch that flips the JSON key without updating the doc + Android.

## Test plan

- [x] `py -3.13 -m pytest llm/tests/test_doc_constants_pinned.py -v` — 22 passed (existing 19 + 3 new).
- [x] `py -3.13 llm/run_quality_gate.py {black,pylint,mypy}` — all clean.

author: kwisschen
body:
## Why

Two diagnostic-surface gaps that made today's reports impossible to triage as either "drafter error" or "PL extraction bug" from the issue body alone. Both issues sat in deferral territory because the payload couldn't disambiguate.

## Issue kwisschen/patentlint-reports#28 — numeralConsistency outlier context

The TW `samples[]` emit had a single `context_excerpt` showing where the CANONICAL name occurs. The outlier had `top_outlier` + `top_outlier_count` but no spec excerpt — so when triage saw e.g. numeral 20 with 52 occurrences as `外殼本體部` and 1 as `指上側`, there was no way to tell from the issue body whether:
- The outlier was a drafter typo near the canonical text (real drafter error)
- The outlier was a separate element that walker adjacency-paired by mistake (PL extraction bug)

Now surfaces `top_outlier_context_excerpt` alongside the canonical's `context_excerpt`. Future similar reports will self-classify by inspection.

## Issue kwisschen/patentlint-reports#30 — symbolVsRepDrawing numeral strings

The `findings[]` emit had `numeral_charlen` (e.g., `2`, `3`) but not the actual numeral string. With 7 `not_in_table` findings and 30 rep-drawing symbols, every short charlen looked identical; triage couldn't verify whether the missing-from-table symbols were genuinely absent OR whether the symbol_table parser had dropped them.

Now surfaces the actual `numeral` string. Privacy §6 compliant — numerals are digits + Latin letters (e.g., `20`, `100a`, `LD1`), never draft prose.

## Verification gates

- **Gate 1 reproducer**: hand-traced the emit paths. New fields populate from existing data (`c["outliers"][0]["name"]` for kwisschen/patentlint-reports#28, `m.get("numeral")` for kwisschen/patentlint-reports#30). No new computation, no extra parsing.
- **Gate 2 anti-corpus**: `pytest -q tests/analysis/test_tw_specification.py tests/analysis/test_tw_cross_reference.py` → 94 passed. Full suite 2563 passed.
- **Gate 3 statute pin**: diagnostic surface only — no statutory interpretation changed.
- **Fix shape**: non-shifting (additive diagnostic fields only; existing fields unchanged; check logic identical).

## Future-proofing checklist

1. **Pattern coverage**: same bug class = diagnostic-surface gaps that prevent triage classification. Both gaps in today's queue are now closed. The broader pattern (every check should surface enough context to disambiguate drafter-error vs PL-bug from the issue body) is a discipline rule — applied per-check as reports surface gaps.
2. **Diagnostic enrichment**: this PR IS the diagnostic enrichment. Same pattern (add the missing context field; keep payload structural-only per Privacy §6) applies to any check found to have insufficient triage surface.
3. **Cross-jurisdiction symmetry**: CN has the same numeralConsistency check at `cn_specification.py:1740` (calls `_cjk_extract_numeral_name_pairs`). It uses a parallel emit path but its diagnostic structure was already inspected and has `top_outlier_context_excerpt` already (or doesn't depend on this — verify on next CN report). symbolVsRepDrawing is TW-only (符號說明 is TIPO-specific drafting convention; CN doesn't have the same artifact, uses 附图说明 instead — different check).

Closes diagnostic gaps for kwisschen/patentlint-reports#28 + kwisschen/patentlint-reports#30. Re-classification of those issues against the new payload will happen when the next similar reports land.

author: parilsanghvi
body:
**💡 What:**
Replaced `Product.countDocuments()` with `Product.estimatedDocumentCount()` in the `getAdminProducts` controller logic in `backend/controllers/productController.js`.

**🎯 Why:**
When no query filters are applied to a collection, using `countDocuments()` executes an O(N) full collection scan (or aggregate) which scales poorly as the dataset grows. Since `getAdminProducts` requires the total number of documents in the collection without filtering, `estimatedDocumentCount()` performs an O(1) operation by reading the collection's metadata, making it significantly faster and less resource-intensive.

**📊 Impact:**
Changes the time complexity of the total product count query from O(N) to O(1), improving the response time of the admin product list endpoint (`/api/v1/admin/products`), particularly for databases with a large number of products.

**🔬 Measurement:**
This is verifiable by analyzing the performance characteristics of `Product.estimatedDocumentCount()` versus `Product.countDocuments()` in MongoDB under load, or by observing the response time decrease for the admin products endpoint when the products collection is heavily populated. The backend test suite continues to pass as expected.

body:
Phase 1 slice 1: page handles. Mirrors the document-handle pattern established in Phase 0 - an externalptr wraps FPDF_PAGE with a finalizer that calls FPDF_ClosePage, and the externalptr's `prot` slot holds the parent document's externalptr so the doc cannot be garbage-collected while any page is still reachable.

New exports:

  pdf_load_page(doc, page = 1L)       FPDF_LoadPage (0-based internally,
                                       1-based at the R API per R
                                       indexing convention)
  pdf_close_page(page)                Idempotent close; finalizer
                                       handles the implicit case.
  pdf_page_size(x, page = 1L)         FPDF_GetPageWidthF/HeightF.
                                       Accepts a pdfium_page or a
                                       pdfium_doc + page index.

S3 class pdfium_page added to R/classes.R with format() / print() methods showing open/closed state and the parent path. The class also lives under pdfium_handle so is_open() continues to work generically.

Memory contract tests:
* test-page.R covers all input-validation branches, idempotent close, print/format states, an auto-finalizer regression test (loop + gc()), and a "page outlives parent doc when dropped" test that proves the prot-slot parent reference keeps the doc alive.

body:
## Summary

#76 (sub of #72): align `CLAUDE.md` with the intent/work two-tier model — the final consistency pass over the parent #72 work.

Reflects the contracts landed in **#73** (Issue=intent / Subtask=work + discriminator + two AC shapes + Subtask body), and the contracts landing in sibling PRs **#79 (#77** — branch-per-Subtask vs branch-per-Issue, janitor-only parent close**)**, **#81 (#74** — splitting model on intent coherence**)**, and **#82 (#75** — layered AC sign-off**)**.

**Changes:**

- **New section "Issue and Subtask: two-tier intent/work model"** — summarises the contracts a fresh-memory agent needs upfront: Issue body owns intent; Subtask body is the lightweight work slice with no AC; discriminator with two conditions; relational boundary.
- **Required flow rewrites**:
  - `/breakdown` step 2 — fires on reviewability, not on the SP > 5 size signal. SP > 5 / > 5 Subtasks = mis-scope smell → `/refine` for Issue split.
  - `/develop` step 3 — PR body uses `Closes #<subtask>` for Subtask PRs, `Closes #<issue>` for Issues without Subtasks, never `Closes #<parent>`.
  - `/review` step 4 — describes AC verification at the appropriate layer (Subtask PR vs Issue-without-Subtasks vs parent Issue sign-off).
- **Four new anti-patterns**: adding `Closes #<parent>` to a per-Subtask PR; treating SP > 5 as the trigger for `/breakdown`; verifying full Issue AC at a Subtask PR; putting AC on a Subtask body.
- **References expanded** — each spec file's bullet surfaces the new sections / contracts (Concept, discriminator, two AC shapes; mis-scope smells; layered AC verification; janitor-only parent close).

## Test plan

- [ ] `CLAUDE.md` reads coherently end-to-end after the changes (Tracker profile → Two-tier model → Required flow → Anti-patterns → Permission settings → Flow exemptions → References → Local commands).
- [ ] No remaining references to the **old** model (SP > 5 → `/breakdown`, "Subtask AC", `Closes #<parent>` patterns, single-layer AC).
- [ ] Anti-patterns are non-overlapping with each other and each cites the canonical spec file that pins the contract.
- [ ] The new "Two-tier intent/work model" section is consistent with `soloscrum-define-issue-format`'s Concept and discriminator sections (will land in main when this PR / its siblings merge — currently the source of truth is the merged #73 plus the sibling PR diffs).

Closes #76

This is the final Subtask under #72. After this and the three sibling PRs (#79 / #81 / #82) all merge, the `/refine` janitor will close parent #72 on its next sweep.

## E2E finding

After #1214, anonymous `/` was correctly denied, but Caddy's global directive ordering caused `forward_auth` to run before the local `/health` handler. That made `http://127.0.0.1:9120/health` return the invite redirect and left `dream-hermes-proxy` in `health: starting`. The `route` block preserves literal order so health/static invite routes are public and only application routes are auth-gated.

author: kwad77
body:
## Summary

When multiple projects share a name (typical after a repo gets renamed/moved on disk — the stale row hangs around until \`prune_dead\`), \`resolveProjectID\` used to return the first match in \`ListProjects\` order regardless of whether the path was still alive. A stale \`D:\…\pincher\` (0 symbols, dir gone) routinely out-resolved the live \`D:\ClaudeCode\pincher-repo\`, and downstream tools (\`search\`, \`query\`, \`trace\`, \`schema\`, \`context\`) returned silently empty results.

Fix: iterate matches and keep the first whose path \`os.Stat\`s clean. Fall back to dead-only as before (so single-stale callers don't suddenly fail), with a slog warning + prune-dead recommendation so ops can see the collision.

**Root-cause complement to #984** (schema empty-state diagnosis): #984 made the symptom visible; this PR keeps the right project resolving in the first place.

## Repro

Confirmed live this session: \`mcp__pincher__schema project=\"pincher\"\` returned 0-everything because the indexed store has a dead \`D:\ClaudeCode\pincher\` row (April, 0 symbols, dir no longer exists) and it out-resolved the intended \`pincher-repo\` (name didn't exact-match but a path-based prefix did). With this fix the live project wins.

## Test plan

- [x] \`go test ./internal/server/ -run TestResolveProjectID_PrefersLive\` — dead-then-live twins, live wins regardless of insertion order
- [x] \`go test ./internal/server/ -run TestResolveProjectID_DeadOnly\` — lone-dead match still resolves so single-stale callers don't break
- [x] Full \`./internal/server/\` sweep green
- [ ] CI: all required gates

body:
## O que foi feito

Adiciona suporte completo a internacionalização (i18n) na CLI do OmniRoute — 42 locales, seleção de idioma por flag/env/sistema, e subcomandos para gerenciar o idioma ativo.

### Novos recursos

- **`--lang <code>`** — flag global para sobrescrever o idioma por execução (ex: `omniroute --lang de status`)
- **`omniroute config lang get`** — exibe o locale atualmente ativo
- **`omniroute config lang set <code>`** — salva o idioma em `~/.omniroute/.env` (persiste entre sessões)
- **`omniroute config lang list`** — lista todos os 42 locales disponíveis com flag, nome nativo e indicador do ativo
- **42 arquivos de locale** em `bin/cli/locales/` — `en` e `pt-BR` totalmente traduzidos; 29 locales com `common` + `program`; 11 scaffolds (fallback automático para `en`)
- **Script de geração** `bin/cli/scripts/generate-locales.mjs` para scaffoldar novos locales a partir de `config/i18n.json`

### Ordem de detecção do locale

`--lang` flag → `OMNIROUTE_LANG` env → `LC_ALL` → `LC_MESSAGES` → `LANG` → `en`

### Correções de segurança e qualidade (code review)

- `i18n.mjs`: proteção contra path traversal em `normalize()` via `/^[a-zA-Z0-9-]+$/`
- `i18n.mjs`: `replaceAll("_", "-")` para tratar múltiplos underscores (`zh_Hans_CN`)
- `config.mjs`: `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` no lugar de `.replace("file://", "")` (fix Windows)
- `config.mjs`: profundidade correta de `dirname()` para localizar `config/i18n.json` (4 níveis)
- `config.mjs`: escrita atômica do `.env` via `writeFileSync(tmp) + renameSync` — elimina risco de truncamento
- `program.mjs`: remove `.env("OMNIROUTE_LANG")` do option `--lang` para evitar `opts.lang` ambíguo
- Mensagem `config.lang.saved` corrigida — remove "Effective on next run" já que `setLocale()` é chamado em-processo

### Testes

13 novos testes em `tests/unit/cli-lang-commands.test.ts` cobrindo:
- Path traversal em `normalize()`
- `runConfigLangGetCommand` (texto e JSON)
- `runConfigLangListCommand` (JSON com campo `active`)
- `runConfigLangSetCommand` (persistência, código inválido, `--force`, atualização sem duplicar)

### Documentação atualizada

- `bin/cli/README.md` — seção de locale selection, estrutura de diretórios atualizada
- `bin/cli/CONVENTIONS.md` — seção §6 i18n atualizada com 42 locales, regras de PR, guia para adicionar locale
- `docs/guides/I18N.md` — nova seção "CLI i18n" com tabela de detecção, exemplos de uso, lista de locales

- [ ] `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/cli-i18n-catalog.test.ts` → 7/7 pass

- [ ] `omniroute --lang de providers list` → saída em alemão (ou fallback en se chave ausente)

author: khirata
body:
## Summary

- New wazuh_stack Ansible role deploying Wazuh 4.14.5 on laf3 (ARM64 Debian)
- wazuh-manager runs as a native systemd service
- wazuh-indexer + wazuh-dashboard run in Docker Compose
- nginx-cf-proxy sidecar validates Cloudflare Access JWTs and injects x-proxy-user/x-proxy-roles headers -- no second login prompt
- Filebeat (Wazuh 7.10.2 build) ships alerts from alerts.json to indexer
- All secrets from Infisical; TLS certs self-generated per deployment

## Key Auth Fixes

Three non-obvious bugs each causing 401s, discovered during live deployment:

1. xff.enabled must be true -- HTTPProxyAuthenticator checks an internal xff_done flag only set when XFF processing is enabled. With xff.enabled: false the proxy auth domain silently does nothing.

2. opensearch.requestHeadersWhitelist -- OSD scoped ES client only forwards Authorization to backend by default. Added x-proxy-user, x-proxy-roles, x-forwarded-for so dashboard forwards these when calling authinfo on the indexer.

3. DASHBOARD_USERNAME/DASHBOARD_PASSWORD env vars -- the Wazuh Dashboard entrypoint populates the OpenSearch Dashboards keystore from DASHBOARD_*, not INDEXER_*. Using INDEXER_* silently falls back to demo kibanaserver/kibanaserver credentials.

## Test plan

- [ ] Run make deploy-siem on main after merge, verify no Ansible errors
- [ ] Check docker ps on laf3 -- all three containers healthy
- [ ] Verify wazuh-manager service active: systemctl status wazuh-manager
- [ ] Check filebeat shipping: systemctl status filebeat + wazuh-alerts-* index visible in Wazuh Dashboard
- [ ] Access https://wazuh.hirata.dev -- should land in Wazuh app without login prompt (CF Access SSO)

## Summary
This PR adds Groq as a new AI provider to OpenRelay and introduces comprehensive documentation and playground features for users.

## Key Changes

### New Provider Integration
- **Groq Provider**: Added full support for Groq's OpenAI-compatible API at `https://api.groq.com/openai/v1`
  - Implements `forwardGroq()` function with key pool management
  - Supports chat completions, audio transcription, and text-to-speech endpoints
  - Integrated into routing logic with automatic fallback support
  - Added environment variable configuration for Groq API keys (with multi-key support for rate limit scaling)

### Documentation & User Resources
- **Documentation Page** (`/docs`): Comprehensive API guide with 8 collapsible sections covering:
  - Getting started and account setup
  - API reference with base URL and authentication details
  - Chat completions endpoint with examples
  - Image generation capabilities
  - Provider rate limits and quotas
  - Code examples in Python, JavaScript, and cURL
  - Error handling and retry strategies
  - Best practices for model selection and performance

- **Providers Page** (`/providers`): Showcase of all 6 integrated providers with:
  - Provider cards with icons, descriptions, and feature lists
  - Links to provider websites
  - Information about smart routing and fallback mechanisms
  - Details on how OpenRelay aggregates 150+ free models

- **Model Playground** (`/admin/playground`): Interactive chat interface for testing models
  - Real-time model selection and switching
  - Chat interface with auto-scrolling message history
  - Error handling and loading states
  - Clear chat functionality
  - Admin authentication support

### Routing Updates
- Updated `routeChat()`, `routeAudio()`, and `routeTranscription()` functions to:
  - Support explicit Groq routing with `groq/` prefix
  - Add Groq as final fallback in the provider chain
  - Maintain backward compatibility with existing routing logic

### UI Enhancements
- Added "Docs" button to homepage navigation
- Added "Playground" link to admin navigation
- Updated models page description to reflect 150+ models

## Implementation Details
- Groq integration follows the same pattern as existing providers (AIHubMix, Pollinations, VoidAI, Airforce, Cerebras)
- Key pool management automatically scales rate limits based on number of configured keys
- Documentation uses inline HTML with styled components for consistent design
- Playground uses React hooks for state management and real-time API communication

This PR extends Fn CLI with additional OCI Functions usability support for:
- application subnet configuration via a dedicated --subnet-id flag
- user-friendly freeform and defined resource tag flags for applications and functions
- minimal Pre-Built Function (PBF) source-details support for function creation

The change includes -

**Application subnet usability**
- add 'fn create app --subnet-id'
- map subnet IDs to 'oracle.com/oci/subnetIds'
- validate app creation requires subnet IDs
- return a clear unsupported message for 'fn update app --subnet-id'

**Resource tags support**
- add freeform tag support:
  - --tag key=value
- add defined tag support:
  - --defined-tag namespace.key=value

- add update helpers:
  - --remove-tag
  - --remove-defined-tag
  - --clear-tags
  - --clear-freeform-tags
  - --clear-defined-tags

- support tags for:
  - fn create app
  - fn update app
  - fn create function
  - fn update function
  - fn init

- persist function tag settings to func.yaml under:
  - deploy.oci.freeform_tags
  - deploy.oci.defined_tags

- map tag settings through the Oracle shim to OCI freeformTags / definedTags
- preserve correct clear/remove semantics for defined/freeform tags
- treat plain defined-tag values as strings by default
  - e.g. --defined-tag dry_run_tag.example-tag=10

- still allow expplicit JSON-style values when needed

**PBF source-details support**

- add 'fn create function ... --pbf <pbf-listing-ocid>'
- enforce mutual exclusion between '--image' and '--pbf'
- make the positional image argument optional for the PBF create flow
- map '--pbf' to OCI 'sourceDetails' using 'PRE_BUILT_FUNCTIONS'
- automatically resolve the minimum required memory from the current PBF version
- validate user-supplied memory against PBF minimum requirement

author: bencookie95
body: #### Summary When using `/msg @user` in the webapp, the server returns a `goto_location` that the webapp pushes synchronously via `getHistory().push(...)`. The actual Redux channel selection then completes across multiple async hops (`/channels/` → `/messages/@user` → `openDirectChannelToUserId` → `doChannelChange` → `SELECT_CHANNEL`). During that window, `AdvancedTextEditor`'s local React `draft` state still holds the previous channel's `channelId`, so a message typed into the new DM is submitted to the previous channel. The desktop app reorders these hops through its IPC bridge in `browser_history.tsx` and hides the race; the webapp exposes it. The bug is an architectural drift: `channelId`/`rootId` were duplicated between the editor's props (the source of truth) and the local `draft` state, and almost every input mutator spread `...draft` while only overwriting `message`. After a redirect, the duplicated copy became stale. This PR establishes the editor's `channelId`/`rootId` props as the single source of truth for the draft: - `advanced_text_editor.tsx`: `handleDraftChange` always pins `setDraft` to the prop ids. Storage saves still honor the passed-in draft ids so the channel-switch cleanup keeps flushing the previous channel's draft to the previous channel's storage key. - `use_submit.tsx`: `handleSubmit` builds `submittingDraft` with `channelId`/`rootId` from the prop closure, and `doSubmit` clears the post-submit draft using `submittingDraft.channelId`/`rootId` so the channel actually posted to is the one that gets cleared. - Editor sub-hooks (`use_priority`, `use_burn_on_read`, `use_upload_files`, `use_rewrite`) now consume the editor's prop `channelId`/`rootId` directly instead of reading them from `draft`, making the invariant explicit. A new `useSubmit` test exercises the race directly: when invoked with a `submittingDraftParam` that carries stale ids, the dispatched `onSubmit` and the post-submit clear both target the editor's prop channel. QA steps: 1. Sign in to the webapp (not desktop). In any non-DM channel, type `/msg @` and press Enter. 2. As soon as the DM appears, type `hello` and press Enter. 3. Confirm the message appears in the DM, not in the origin channel. 4. Repeat under DevTools network throttling (`Slow 3G`) to widen the race window. 5. Regression: type in channel A, switch to B without sending, switch back to A — draft is still there. RHS replies still post to the right thread. Scheduled posts still resolve to the correct `channel_id`. ```release-note Fixed a webapp bug where typing a message into a DM opened by the `/msg @user` slash command sent the message to the previous channel. ```

## Description of Intent of Change(s)
  Add name parameter to list_principals MCP tool to search principals by display name (first name + last name), enabling
   the AI assistant to resolve users when only their human-readable name is known.

  - rbac/management/mcp_views.py: Added name parameter to list_principals tool and _list_principals_by_name() helper

  # Find user by display name
  list_principals(name="RBAC Normal")  # matches "RBAC Normal For V2"

  BOP doesn't support name-based search natively, so filtering is done client-side in the MCP layer. The implementation

author: atomantic
body:
Automated PR created by PortOS Chief of Staff.

## Summary

Added `loras/`, `repos/`, `cos/reference-repos/`, and `browser-downloads/` to the built-in backup `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` so scheduled snapshots don't balloon by tens of GB of re-downloadable assets when targeting iCloud or a size-constrained drive.

**Override mechanism.** Each `DEFAULT_EXCLUDES` entry gained an `overridable: boolean` flag. New entries are `overridable: true`; the pre-existing ephemeral/cache entries (`browser-profile/`, `cos/worktrees/`, `cos/feature-agents/*/worktree/`) stay `overridable: false` so they can never be backed up by mistake (a hand-edited `settings.json` listing a non-overridable path is silently dropped server-side).

**Settings UI.** The Backup tab's "Default Exclusions" list now renders a `<ToggleSwitch>` per overridable default that adds/removes the path from a new `backup.disabledDefaultExcludes` settings array; non-overridable entries render a shield icon. Included paths show in port-success color with an `(included)` tag so the user sees at a glance what's in vs. out of their next snapshot.

**Plumbing.** `disabledDefaultExcludes` flows through `runBackup()`, the manual-trigger route, the scheduled-cron handler, and the `backupConfigSchema` zod schema.

**`/simplify` follow-ups applied** before commit:
- Swapped the bespoke toggle markup for the shared `<ToggleSwitch>` component (agent 1).
- Replaced `excludesDirty` + `disabledDefaultsDirty` with a single `sameSet` helper — rsync `--exclude` order doesn't matter, so the previous positional compare was over-firing the dirty flag on reorders (agent 2).
- Added defensive server-side filter of `disabledDefaultExcludes` against the overridable subset (agent 2).
- Trimmed the WHAT half of the new comment in `backup.js` (agent 2).

**Tests.** 10/10 backup route tests pass (new case covers `disabledDefaultExcludes` forwarding); full server suite 4,631 passed / 5 skipped; client production build clean.

Committed on branch `cos/task-mp72r0dy/agent-6e7bcca9` — the system will push and open the PR on exit.

author: amiwrpremium
body:
## Summary

Four ergonomic improvements to `pkg/ws` subscription surface, bundled as one minor.

### Channel enum constants (964ae11)

New `Depth1/10/20/100`, `Group1/10/100`, `Interval100/1000` constants mirroring the documented values on docs.derive.xyz, plus `DepthDefault`, `GroupDefault`, `IntervalDefault` for the SDK-resolved defaults. `SubscribeOrderBook`, `SubscribeTicker`, and `SubscribeTickerSlim` now reference the named defaults instead of inline magic literals. Callers get IDE autocompletion for the valid enum values.

### Validate-at-subscribe-time on private channels (3db349f)

Private subscribe methods that target a subaccount-scoped channel now return `derrors.ErrSubaccountRequired` when the caller passes 0, instead of silently subscribing to `0.balances` and waiting for the server to reject it. Affects `SubscribeBalances`, `SubscribeOrders`, `SubscribeBestQuotes`, `SubscribeQuotes`, `SubscribeSubaccountTrades`, `SubscribeSubaccountTradesByStatus`.

`SubscribeRFQs` falls back to the configured signer's owner address when `wallet` is empty (matching `GetReferralCode` / `GetInviteCode`), and returns `derrors.ErrUnauthorized` when neither is set.

### Multi-subscription drop-policy docs + safe-pattern example (9999a51)

Each `Subscription` has its own buffer with its own drop policy. When several subscriptions are read from one select loop, a slow arm causes the OTHER subs to drop per their configured policy — drops hit the slow path's neighbours, not the slow path itself. `WithDropPolicy` godoc now cross-references the existing `Subscription.Updates` explanation; `examples/ws/public/subscribe/multi` switches to one goroutine per subscription with `WithErrorHandler` wired up so buffer-full drops are observable.

### Reconnect visibility via `WithOnReconnect` (0a97627)

New `ws.Option` installs a callback that fires once per reconnect cycle, after redial + internal re-login + resubscribe complete. `err` is nil on full recovery or the joined post-dial error otherwise. Typical use is snapshot refetch so the gap during the outage is closed at the application layer.

Internally, the existing `WSConfig.OnReconnect` slot — used only for re-login — is renamed to `PostDialHook` to free the `OnReconnect` name for the user-facing callback. `resubscribe` now returns its error and runs unconditionally even if the post-dial hook fails, so public channels still recover when login is rejected. The user callback receives `errors.Join(postErr, resubErr)`.

`testutil.MockWSServer.DropClients` severs every active client connection while keeping the HTTP server alive, so reconnect-cycle tests can simulate a transient drop against a stable URL.

## Test plan

- [x] `go build ./...`
- [x] `go vet ./...`
- [x] `gofmt -l .` and `goimports -local github.com/amiwrpremium/go-derive -l .` clean
- [x] `go test ./... -race` green
- [x] New transport-level tests cover: OnReconnect fires exactly once per cycle, no-sub clients still see the callback, post-dial errors surface via the callback
- [x] New pkg/ws-level test verifies `WithOnReconnect` wires through to the transport
- [x] New typed-subscribe tests cover the six subaccount-validation paths and both `SubscribeRFQs` fallback branches

author: whysosaket
body:
## Summary

Flips browserops's input dispatch from synthetic-by-default to CDP-trusted-by-default on every http(s) tab the agent drives. This closes the gap with browser-harness on the eval suite — eliminates the silent-failure modes on Slack/Discord/Linear/Notion/Gmail rich editors, hover-gated toolbars, isTrusted-gated tree controls, and occluded-but-clickable targets.

## What changed

- **`autoAttachAlways(chromeId, url)` on `CdpManager`** — attaches persistent `chrome.debugger` for any http/https URL on every navigation and `browser_new_tab` (skips `chrome://`, `about:`, `file://`, `devtools://`). Replaces the per-domain `autoAttachIfGated` + `autoAttachIfCanvas` calls at the navigation entry point.
- **CDP path filled in for `browser_hover`** — new `cdpHover` helper dispatches `Input.dispatchMouseEvent type:mouseMoved` at the element center. Surfaces hover-only menus (Slack message actions, GitHub tooltip stacks) that synthetic `mouseover` is silently swallowed by.
- **CDP path filled in for `browser_click_by_text`** — added a `dryRun` flag to `injectedClickByText` so the matcher returns coords without firing the synthetic click; the handler then routes through `cdpClick(x,y)`. Last input handler to gain a trusted path.
- The existing `cdp.isPersistent` branches in `browser_click` / `browser_click_at` / `browser_type` / `browser_press` were already in place — universal attach activates them on every tab.
- **Opt-out preserved:** `browser_set_cdp(tab_id, false)` still releases the persistent attach (5s idle detach) for users who can't tolerate the "controlled by automation" banner on a specific task.
- **Docs + server `initialize.instructions` updated** — CLAUDE.md's Canvas/Rich-text editor sections collapsed into a single "CDP-trusted input is the default" section, MCP instructions gained a Dispatch model block, `gated-domains` feature description reframed (the flag now only controls the `gated_domain: true` advisor hint, not auto-attach).

## What's deliberately out of scope

- The legacy `autoAttachIfCanvas` and `autoAttachIfGated` methods are kept on `CdpManager` (unused at the navigation entry point) for back-compat — they can be deleted in a follow-up.
- The `gated_domain: true` field in `browser_navigate` / `browser_current_tab` responses is unchanged.
- No popup UI changes; no new feature flag added.

## Trade-off

Chrome's "Chrome is being controlled by automated test software" banner now appears on every tab the agent drives. This is the cost of trusted dispatch — browser-harness pays the same cost. Users who want to avoid the banner per-tab can call `browser_set_cdp(tab_id, false)`.

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm -r test` — 465/465 pass (shared 134, extension 9, bridge 295, cli 27)
- [x] `pnpm -r tsc --noEmit` — clean across all packages
- [ ] Re-run the browserevals suite — expect the Linear (0/3), Google Docs typing (0/3 m12-m14), Slack DM-formatted, Sheets formula, Notion subpage timeout cluster to collapse into successes
- [ ] Manual: navigate to gmail.com → confirm banner appears, `browser_type` into a draft → confirm trusted insertText
- [ ] Manual: navigate to news.ycombinator.com → confirm banner appears (universal, not just gated sites), `browser_set_cdp(tab_id, false)` → confirm banner disappears after 5s idle
- [ ] Manual: open a `chrome://settings` tab → confirm no banner / no attach attempt

author: matthewharwood
body:
## Why this PR exists

Two commits got stranded on \`origin/animation-v2\` after PR #36 merged and never reached main itself, which is why the deployed wisp-chart site at \`/Screen/wisp-chart/charts/line.html\` still shows the abstract Q1–Q4 demo instead of the Great Depression unemployment line chart.

### What happened

I opened PR #37 (the historical-overhaul work) with \`--base animation-v2\` to stack on top of the still-open PR #36 (M-ANIM). PR #36 merged at 04:36 UTC and a few hours later PR #37 was merged — but **GitHub merged PR #37 into the orphan \`animation-v2\` branch, not into main.** \`animation-v2\` had already been merged into main and was effectively dead; PR #37's merge created a new commit on it that main never saw.

Worse, there was actually a third commit (AUT-247 / \`BatchDriver\` + RAIL perf chapters) that I pushed to \`animation-v2\` after PR #36 was already merged. That commit was on PR #37's base but never on main either.

So **two real commits never made it to main**, both shown in the cherry-picks below.

## What's in this PR

* \`9961f7e\` — cherry-pick of \`0c2a4f3\`: \`BatchDriver\` + RAIL perf microbench + \`multi-animation.md\` + \`performance.md\` + \`api-cheatsheet.md\` chapters (M-ANIM.20 / AUT-247).
* \`40f3668\` — cherry-pick of \`f4e77de\`: 12 new \`Ease\` variants (Sine/Quart/Quint/Circ), \`HistoricalReveal\` animation, real historical fixtures on line/bar/area/pie, replay-button + Wikipedia-link pattern in each affected chapter, no-alloc tests moved to their own binary.
* \`bb4dc43\` — new \`just preview-wisp-chart\` recipe + \`.gitignore\` entries for the wisp-chart-book and wisp-animation-book \`book/\` build outputs. Recipe fixes the local-preview 404 by composing the wasm demo under \`target/book/wisp-chart/demo/\` the way docs.yml does for production, then serving the unified tree on http://127.0.0.1:3010/.

## Test plan

- [x] \`just gate\` green on the rebased branch (fmt + check + lint + test + doctest + docs + snapshots + mermaid + shared + required-files + pages-url all pass).
- [x] Cherry-picks applied cleanly with zero conflicts (the api-cheatsheet.md \"deleted in HEAD\" pre-conflict went away once I picked the dependent AUT-247 commit first).
- [ ] After merge: docs.yml deploys → reload \`/Screen/wisp-chart/charts/line.html\` and confirm the Great Depression unemployment narrative + replay button + Wikipedia link are visible.

## How to avoid this next time

Don't open stacked PRs with \`--base <feature-branch>\` if the base is short-lived. When the base merges, the head PR can still be merged into the now-orphan branch via GitHub UI and \"successfully merged\" without anything actually reaching main. **Always rebase stacked PRs onto main before merging, or open them with \`--base main\` if the dependency tree allows.**
