author: jmontgomery-aurora
body:
Units variables of integral types with large magnitudes can overflow unnecessarily when applying the scaling factor $$\frac{P \cdot X}{Q}$$.

We can mitigate this for small values of P and Q (which should be most cases) by rewriting X as a quotient and remainder relative to Q, which gives us $$P \cdot \lfloor X / Q \rfloor + \frac{P \cdot (X \pmod Q)}{Q}$$. This eliminates overflow as long as $$P \cdot (Q - 1) \le \text{TypeMax}$$. Factoring out $$GCD(P, Q)$$ gives us an even larger range of non-overflowing factors P and Q. 

The practical result is that for reasonably sized factors and most larger factors, the entire type range becomes usable without overflow. There's also some truncation risk changes to accommodate the new operation.

author: t11z
body:
## Summary

Both top-level workflow badges have been stuck red. The diagnoses and fixes are intertwined enough to belong in one PR.

### Why hourly was red

The trailing **`Fail workflow if any generator failed`** step exited 1 whenever *any* scraper had failed. With 8 of 32 scrapers currently broken (vendor pages restructured), the whole workflow went red — even though the workflow itself ran cleanly: generators executed, badges were written, `.txt` outputs preserved by the safety net, commit pushed. The "which scraper broke" signal is already encoded in the per-list status badges; the top-level badge doesn't need to duplicate it.

**Fix:** the step is replaced with a summary that warns in the log but doesn't fail the workflow. The hourly badge now only goes red on real CI-mechanical breakage (test suite, `git push`, infra). Per-slug failures stay visible in the README table's Status column.

### Why auto-issue was red

It triggered on `failure` only, then the Claude Code action ran unconditionally. If `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` was unset/invalid (or the secret simply hadn't been provisioned yet), the action failed → workflow red. Any config gap turned the bot's badge red.

**Fix:** triggers on `completed` (any conclusion) and adds three explicit gating steps:
1. Download artifact (`continue-on-error`)
2. Check whether any generator actually failed
3. Check whether `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is set

Each subsequent step only runs if its precondition holds; if any is false the workflow exits green with a warning. No more red badge purely because the secret hasn't been provisioned.

### Drive-by fix

The commit step's "no changes" detection only looked at `*/*.txt` changes, so when only a badge JSON flipped (passing↔failing without entry-count change) the badge update never got committed. Now badge-only diffs are recognised and committed with a clear `Update EDL badges only` message.

### What this means in practice

- **Both top-level badges should go green within the next hourly run** (one for green-because-CI-mechanic-OK, one for green-because-correctly-skipped-due-to-missing-secret).
- The 8 currently-broken scrapers stay surfaced in the per-list badges; nothing about that signal is lost.
- Once you add `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to repo secrets, the next hourly run will trigger Claude Code, which will file one GitHub issue per failed slug.

## Test plan

- [x] `python -m pytest tests/` — 138 tests pass (no test changes)
- [ ] Trigger `workflow_dispatch` on the hourly workflow after merge — confirm it exits 0 even with the current ~8 failing scrapers, and that the auto-issue workflow runs next, logs the missing-token warning (assuming the secret isn't set yet), and exits 0
- [ ] After adding `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`: same trigger should result in 1 GitHub issue per failed slug, tagged `generator-failure`
- [ ] Verify badge-only commit path: locally force a badge change without a `.txt` change and confirm the commit step still produces a commit

body:
#### 9ed47b46a8bef399472fd82703c995ca5a817680 
Rewrite http/tests/security/cross-origin-indexeddb.html to actually verify storage blocking policy
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=314922
rdar://177202636

Reviewed by Per Arne Vollan.

While debugging cross-origin storage tests under Site Isolation, I noticed this test passes even when storage blocking
policy is not properly configured under SI. It turns out the test only exercises an IndexedDB behavior (open() succeeds)
that holds under both `StorageBlockingPolicy::AllowAll` and `StorageBlockingPolicy::BlockThirdParty`, so the result
tells us nothing about whether the policy is actually applied.

Rewrite the test to verify whether the third-party database is ephemeral instead: the storage should be ephemeral under
BlockThirdParty policy and persistent under AllowAll policy. With this change, if the wrong policy is in effect the test
produces a visibly different result instead of silently passing.

author: adrienbrault
body:
The previous setup combined three slowdowns:

1. Generous timeouts hid broken locators. The `daily challenge` test
   matched two elements (button + feature row) and timed out at 30s on
   all four projects (120s wasted). The `solo - in progress` test
   targeted a numpad button hidden by `lg:hidden` on Desktop and timed
   out at 30s (another 30s wasted). Those 150s of timeout dwarfed the
   actual work.

2. Excessive waits. `waitForLoadState("networkidle")` waits 500ms of
   network silence and can hang on long-lived connections. Stacked
   `waitForTimeout(500/800/1000)` between every step compounded the
   problem. Tests that set localStorage navigated twice — once to set,
   once to render.

3. Cell-reveal animations stagger up to ~630ms (6ms × 80 cells + 150ms
   anim), forcing the 800ms `waitForTimeout` after entering a game.

Changes:

- Disable CSS animations and transitions via `addInitScript` so the
  final state is paintable immediately. Removes the 800ms post-nav wait.
- Seed localStorage via `addInitScript` in a fixture, eliminating the
  double `goto`.
- Replace `networkidle` and blanket timeouts with explicit waits on the
  selector that matters (`numpad`, `heading`, `Easy` button).
- Use `:visible` filter on the numpad locator so Desktop tests target
  the visible variant instead of the `lg:hidden` mobile copy.
- Use `getByRole("button", { name: /Daily Challenge/ })` so the locator
  no longer collides with the lowercase "Daily challenge" feature row.
- Set test-level timeouts (8s test, 3s action, 5s nav) so genuine bugs
  surface in seconds, not 30s.
- Enable `fullyParallel: true` to run tests within a file concurrently.

Result: 1m33s with 5 failures → 27s with 68/68 passing.

author: markmichaelis
body:
Closes #63.

## What

Codegen now marks a generated C# record property as nullable when JSON evidence shows the value `null` or the key absent in **at least one observed sample** for that endpoint -- including nested object/array fields, which previously dropped nullability when sample shapes diverged.

## Why

Per the dogfood report (`docs/dogfood/tripit-dry-run-report.md`, Model-Shape Fidelity section), the agent was emitting required-init properties for fields the HAR samples showed were intermittently null/absent. Round-trip deserialization could throw on the first response that omitted the field.

## How

In `templates/api-wrapper-scaffold/scripts/generate-wrapper.js`:

1. `inferShape` records **field-level** nullability per object: `fields[k].nullable = (val[k] === null)`. This is distinct from `shape.nullable` on a primitive, which gets lost when a null sample is merged against an object/array sample.
2. `mergeShapes` propagates `nullable` per field via OR across samples (both, only-a, only-b cases).
3. `mergeShapes` gains an `isNullSentinel` short-circuit: when one side is the literal `null` placeholder (`{kind:'primitive', type:'object', nullable:true}`) and the other side is a real object/array shape, prefer the real shape. Field-level `nullable` retains the null observation. (Previously the merge collapsed to `{kind:'unknown'}` -> `JsonElement`, losing both the shape and the nullability.)
4. `shapeSignature` includes field-level `nullable` so otherwise-identical records with different nullability profiles are no longer aliased.
5. `emitModels` appends `?` to the C# type when **either** `f.optional` (absent) **or** `f.nullable` (null) is true.

## Tests

- New: `templates/api-wrapper-scaffold/scripts/nullability.test.js` -- 12 zero-dep Node `assert` cases covering the five TDD anchors in #63 plus regressions for nested-object-null and array-null.
- New: `.github/agents/tests/nullability-heuristic.Tests.ps1` -- Pester wrapper that runs the Node test.
- Full Pester suite: 278 passed, 0 failed, 4 skipped (no regressions).

## Evidence (Phase 5b)

Captured under `.evidence/phase-5b-20260515T231130Z/` (gitignored, will be attached as a PR comment). Highlights:

- TripIt synthetic multi-sample HAR (3 samples per endpoint) -- BEFORE and AFTER `Models.Generated.cs` are **identical** (4 nullable props on Profile + Trip combined). Confirms no regression on the canonical scenario.
- Nested multi-sample HAR (object null + array null in one sample of three):
  - BEFORE (origin/main): `User User { ... } = default!;` and `IReadOnlyList<string> Tags { ... } = default!;` -- **both non-nullable despite null evidence**.
  - AFTER (this branch): `User? User { get; init; }` and `IReadOnlyList<string>? Tags { get; init; }` -- correctly nullable, with the nested `User` record still emitted.

## Out of scope

Per issue: element-type nullability inside arrays is deferred. Only the array reference itself is made nullable when the array is null/absent.

## Merge

Rebase-only: `gh pr merge <n> --rebase --delete-branch`.

author: verse-mate-agent
body:
## Summary

- **Bug:** Looking up words with KJV Latin ligatures (æ, œ) always returned "no definition found"
- **Root cause:** `normalizeWord()` did not expand ligatures, so `"zacchæus"` never matched Easton key `"zacchaeus"` (Levenshtein distance exceeded fuzzy threshold)
- **Fix:** Explicit `LIGATURE_MAP` in `word-mapping-service.ts` expands æ→ae, Æ→AE, œ→oe, Œ→OE before the NFKD + diacritic-strip pass

**Correction to QA's proposal:** `.normalize('NFKD')` does NOT decompose æ/œ — Unicode treats them as independent Latin letters, not compatibility forms. The explicit map is required.

**Verified working:**
| Input | Output | Easton hit |
|---|---|---|
| Zacchæus | zacchaeus | EXACT |
| Cæsar | caesar | EXACT |
| Phœnicia | phoenicia | EXACT |
| Judæa | judaea | fuzzy (→ judea, dist=1) |
| Galilæan | galilaean | fuzzy (→ galilean, dist=1) |

## Files changed

- `services/word-mapping-service.ts` — fix in `normalizeWord()`
- `__tests__/services/word-mapping-service.test.ts` — new unit tests covering ligature cases

author: samgutentag
body:
## Summary

- New R2 artifact `gbfs/{systemId}/popularity.json` precomputes top stations, top routes, and per-pair duration stats over a rolling 30-day window.
- `/route/:from/:to` shows an empirical `avg N min over M trips` badge alongside the existing typical-time badge when the directed pair has at least 3 observed trips.
- `/explore` gains two new tiles: top stations (departures + arrivals) and top routes (inferred trips), both 30d.
- Refresh cadence: every 4 hours via the new `popularity` workflow.
- Zero KV ops added (rollup is R2-only).

Closes #8 (avg duration) and #9 (popular stations + routes).

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-15-popularity-rollup-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-15-popularity-rollup.md`

## How it works

The build script (`scripts/compute-popularity.ts`):
1. Lists `station_status/dt=*` parquet partitions on R2 for the last 30 days.
2. Parses each via the existing `parquetToSnapshots` helper.
3. Synthesizes departure/arrival events by diffing `num_bikes_available` between consecutive per-station snapshots.
4. Re-runs the existing `inferTrips` function over the synthesized event stream.
5. Aggregates: station counts (departures + arrivals), pair counts + mean duration.
6. Writes one JSON to `gbfs/{systemId}/popularity.json`.

The web app reads that JSON via a new `useRoutePopularity` hook (mirrors `useRouteCache` / `useTravelMatrix`).

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean (one pre-existing unrelated `test-setup.ts` warning from the Harmony merge)

## Summary

Replaces `Handler.feePayer` from `tempo.ts/server` with `Handler.relay` from `accounts/server` (same handler wallet-next uses).

### Why

The old `tempo.ts` handler lacks fee token resolution — clients had to manually set `feeToken` on the chain config or the transaction would be sent without one, causing FeeAMM swap errors even when validators accept pathUSD.

### What changes

- **Dependency**: `tempo.ts` → `accounts` (already in workspace catalog at `~0.8.1`)
- **Handler**: `Handler.feePayer()` → `Handler.relay()` with `features: "all"`
- **Multi-chain**: Transports for mainnet, moderato, and devnet (resolves chain from tx `chainId`)
- **Fee token resolution**: Relay auto-detects the best fee token from sender balances
- **Auto-swap**: Built-in cross-token fee payment when needed
- **Simulation**: Balance diffs + fee breakdown in `eth_fillTransaction` responses

### Handler config

```ts
Handler.relay({
  cors: false,
  features: "all",
  feePayer: {
    account: privateKeyToAccount(env.SPONSOR_PRIVATE_KEY),
    name: "Tempo Sponsor",
    url: "https://sponsor.tempo.xyz",

  transports: {
    [tempo.id]: http(env.TEMPO_RPC_URL ?? ...),

})

author: sofianebenhelli
body:
## Summary

Lands **EPIC-1 slice 1.2** (#339) — ADR-018's versioning lifecycle as code. Adds a **sibling store layer** alongside the existing `TaxonomyStore` so the `DRAFT → CANDIDATE_V0 → VALIDATED_V1 → ARCHIVED` version chain and the per-suggestion `NEW → UNDER_REVIEW → ACCEPTED / REJECTED / MERGED / DEFERRED` workflow have a real home. The existing YAML loader + B2 read route are untouched.

## Why a sibling layer (not widening the existing `Taxonomy`)

The existing `Taxonomy` is consumed by the Explorer left rail + the classifier. Widening it would force every consumer to handle the new lifecycle fields. A sibling `TaxonomyVersion` lets ADR-018's versioning ride on a wrapper while the published shape stays stable — the public read route in B2 keeps returning the active Validated's tree; the admin / workflow routes (slices 1.7 / 1.8) serve `TaxonomyVersion` directly.

## What's in

**Schemas** (`apps/api/app/schemas/taxonomy_version.py`):

| Type | Role |
|---|---|
| `TaxonomyState` | Literal — `DRAFT` / `CANDIDATE_V0` / `VALIDATED_V1` / `ARCHIVED` / `DISCARDED` |
| `ConceptSuggestionState` | Literal — `NEW` / `UNDER_REVIEW` / `ACCEPTED` / `REJECTED` / `MERGED` / `DEFERRED` |
| `ConceptSuggestionSource` | Literal — `extractor` / `llm` / `operator` (audit attribution) |
| `ConceptSuggestion` | Pydantic model with merge-target coupling validator |
| `TaxonomyVersion` | Wraps `Taxonomy` with id / version_number / state / audit timestamps; validator pins "suggestions only on DRAFT" |
| `is_legal_version_transition`, `is_legal_concept_transition` | Module-level predicates over the transition tables |

**Store** (`apps/api/app/services/taxonomy_version_store.py`):

- `TaxonomyVersionStoreProtocol` is the persistence boundary.
- `InMemoryTaxonomyVersionStore` is the MVP implementation.
- `active_validated` is implicit per ADR-018 §4 — `MAX(version_number) WHERE state == 'VALIDATED_V1' AND state != 'ARCHIVED'`. No `is_active` flag.
- Eight transition functions: `create_draft`, `promote_to_candidate`, `validate_version`, `archive_version`, `discard_draft`, `add_suggestions`, `transition_concept`.
- `IllegalTaxonomyTransition` carries the `(from_state, to_state, kind)` triple so the route layer can surface 409s.

**Audit trail** (ADR-018 §7): every transition emits a structured-log event consumed by the existing `AuditEventStore`. `actor` follows the #91 backfill pattern (PRs #460 / #462 / #464) — included when threaded, omitted from the payload entirely when system-driven.

## Tests

~35 cases in `apps/api/tests/test_taxonomy_version_store.py`:

- Schema invariants (merge-target coupling, draft-only suggestions, min lengths).
- Transition predicates (parametrised over the state-machine matrix).
- Store CRUD (`get` / `list_for_taxonomy` ordering / `active_validated` derivation).
- Per-transition happy paths.
- Illegal-transition rejection across every non-edge.
- Audit-event emission via `caplog` with the `actor` field verified.
- End-to-end V1 → V2 supersede flow with audit fields and `superseded_version_number` checked.

## Out of scope (queued)

- **SQLite implementation** of the Protocol — follow-up; the Protocol + in-memory impl is the contract the SQLite store mirrors.
- **YAML-loader wrap** that emits the promotion chain — ADR-018 §10 describes the shape; the existing loader still uses the singleton `TaxonomyStore` until the wrap is wired.
- **Tree mutation on promote** — accepted suggestions snapshotting into the published tree belongs in slice 1.8 (#345) where the validation workflow lives.

## Depends on

- **PR #469** (ADR-018) — the design this PR implements. Reviewing the lifecycle decisions in #469 is the prerequisite to reviewing this code.
- **PR #468** (slice 1.1 deterministic extractor) — not a hard dep, but the corpus aggregator (slice 1.5) will tag suggestions sourced from the extractor as `source="extractor"`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `pytest apps/api/tests/test_taxonomy_version_store.py -v` — ~35 cases.
- [ ] `pytest apps/api/tests/test_taxonomy_store.py` — existing singleton store still green (untouched).
- [ ] `ruff check apps/api/app/schemas/taxonomy_version.py apps/api/app/services/taxonomy_version_store.py apps/api/tests/test_taxonomy_version_store.py` — clean.

## Provenance

Filed 2026-05-15 as **EPIC-1 slice 1.2**. Third PR in the EPIC-1 arc opened today: #468 (1.1 extractor), #469 (ADR-018), this (1.2 store).

author: aristocles
body:
# What changed

Schedule cards (peptides / medications / supplement stacks) that opt into the daily prompt previously rendered a free-text Item name + editable date + time-picker form on app open. The card already knows what's scheduled today, so the form was the wrong shape: the operator wants one tap to mean "I took it just now."

Adds `meta.prompt.mode: "checklist"` as a first-class prompt shape alongside the existing `"modal"`. When set, the modal renders one row per item that `isScheduledOnDate` flags as scheduled today, each with a single Taken button that stamps `{scheduledDate, takenAt}` into the item's `doses[]` (or `takenDates[]` for plain supplement items). Rows update in place; the modal auto-closes once every scheduled item is marked. The card's normal renderer + add-form for off-schedule entries is untouched.

Eligibility for checklist-mode prompts is per-item: a new `allScheduledTakenForDate` helper in `prompt-queue.js` suppresses the prompt only when EVERY today-scheduled item already has a logged dose. Default `mode: "modal"` (or absent) keeps existing behaviour.

`medication-schedule`, `injection-protocol`, and `supplement-stack` templates now ship with `prompt: { enabled: true, mode: "checklist", whenMissing: true }` enabled by default. The chat agent's system prompt suggests the same default when creating schedule-style cards.

# Why

Fixes #185. Observed in 2026-05-11 manual QA: the morning peptide reminder presented three blank fields the operator had to retype values into, when the desired interaction is one tap per item.

# How

- `public/js/components/eh-prompt-modal.js`: branch on `card.meta.prompt.mode` inside `render()`. Approach A from the issue (single component, two render paths). Existing `mode: "modal"` flow untouched.
- `public/js/lib/prompt-queue.js`: new `allScheduledTakenForDate` exported and used by `buildPromptQueue` when `prompt.mode === "checklist"`. Falls back to the existing `entryExistsForDate` for `"modal"` mode.
- `public/js/lib/schedule.js`: no changes — `isScheduledOnDate` reused as-is.
- Schema docs: `MANIFEST-SCHEMA.md` and `docs/CARDS.md` now describe both modes with a per-mode behaviour table.
- Templates updated; the e2e seed leaves the prompt off so unrelated specs stay green and the new spec patches it on at runtime.
- Adds 10 unit tests covering `allScheduledTakenForDate` (NONE / SOME / ALL taken, doses + takenDates shapes) and the checklist-mode branch in `buildPromptQueue`.
- Adds `tests-e2e/schedule-checklist-prompt.spec.js` covering the full happy path: modal opens with two rows, taps mark them in place, modal auto-closes, writes land in `doses[]`, and a reload does not re-fire the prompt.

# Testing

- [x] `npm test` passes locally (851/852; the lone failure is a pre-existing infra-noise hygiene assertion present on main, unrelated to this change).
- [x] `npm run test:e2e` passes locally (28/28).
- [x] New unit + e2e coverage added.
- [x] New e2e spec verified to fail on `main` before the fix lands (asserts `.row` count = 2 against the old form-only modal which has no `.row` elements).
- [x] Manual smoke: ran the sandbox locally, confirmed the modal renders two rows, Taken updates in place, modal closes after the last tap, and a reload no longer fires it.

# Checklist

- [x] Commit message follows CONTRIBUTING.md conventions
- [x] CHANGELOG.md updated under ## Unreleased
- [x] Docs updated (`MANIFEST-SCHEMA.md`, `docs/CARDS.md`, system prompt)
- [x] No personal identifiers or hardcoded paths
- [x] No secrets or high-entropy tokens

# Breaking changes

None. `mode` is optional and defaults to `"modal"`; existing manifests without `prompt.mode` continue to render the legacy form. The two production instances run schedule cards without `prompt.mode` set today, so no migration is required to upgrade.

author: arthur-debert
body:
## Summary

- Adds `.claude/settings.json` with a SessionStart hook calling `scripts/setup-dev-env.sh`, so a fresh cloud session warms project deps + wires lefthook automatically.
- Adds `scripts/setup-dev-env.sh` — universal stack-detecting script (rust / node / ruby / lefthook). Cloud-only via `CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE` gate, so it no-ops on local sessions.
- Updates `.github/workflows/copilot-review.yml` to the new `[opened]`-only policy: drafts get Copilot at PR open, and flipping draft→ready does **not** re-trigger Copilot. This avoids the prior "two reviews per PR" pattern.

## Why

This is the per-consumer fanout for [arthur-debert/release#26](https://github.com/arthur-debert/release/issues/26) (Phase 2 / Group B). Tracking issue: [arthur-debert/release#34](https://github.com/arthur-debert/release/issues/34).

The mechanism was proven on arthur-debert/release and arami-core. This PR brings lex-fmt/comms onto the same canonical loop.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on this PR
- [ ] Copilot review fires at PR open (validates new `[opened]` policy)
- [ ] On merge, a fresh cloud session in this repo triggers the SessionStart hook without errors

* api-change:``grafana``: Adds support for dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) connectivity to Amazon Managed Grafana workspaces. Customers can configure the ipAddressType parameter when creating or updating a workspace to choose between IPv4-only or dual-stack (IPv4 and IPv6) access.
